aq-001.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-001.q: How many pillars of īmān are listed in the hadith of Jibrīl?
aq-001.e: In the hadith of Jibrīl the Prophet lists six pillars of faith: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and the decree (qadar). Five is the number of the pillars of islām.

aq-002.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (Islam is built on five)
aq-002.q: What is the first of the five pillars of islām?
aq-002.e: The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar on which Islam is built begins with testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is His messenger; prayer, zakāt, fasting and ḥajj follow.

aq-003.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-003.q: Which of the following is a pillar of īmān rather than a pillar of islām?
aq-003.e: Belief in the angels is one of the six pillars of faith. Fasting, zakāt and ḥajj are among the outward pillars of islām named in the same hadith.

aq-004.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-004.q: How does the hadith of Jibrīl define iḥsān?
o: Worshipping Allah as though you see Him
Giving charity beyond the obligatory zakāt
Being kind to parents and relatives
Reciting the Quran with beautiful tajwīd
aq-004.e: The Prophet defined iḥsān as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then knowing that He sees you. Kindness and charity are fruits of it, but not its definition in this hadith.

aq-005.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-005.q: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from which Companion does Ibn ʿUmar narrate the hadith of Jibrīl?
aq-005.e: At the start of Kitāb al-Īmān in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrates the hadith of Jibrīl from his father ʿUmar, who was present when the stranger in white clothes came to the Prophet.

aq-006.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on tawḥīd
aq-006.q: What does the word tawḥīd mean linguistically?
aq-006.e: Tawḥīd is the verbal noun of waḥḥada, to make one or declare one. In creed it means affirming that Allah is one, without partner. Submission is the meaning of islām, and belief that of īmān.

aq-007.q: According to the verse shown, which sin does Allah not forgive (for one who dies upon it)?
aq-007.e: The verse shown states that Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Scholars explain this of one who dies upon shirk without repenting.

aq-008.q: In the verse shown, Luqmān warns his son against shirk. How does he describe shirk with the highlighted word and the word after it?
aq-008.e: Luqmān calls shirk a tremendous ẓulm, a wrong in its highest form, because it places worship where it does not belong. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī the Prophet explained the ẓulm of 6:82 by this verse.

aq-009.q: Which angel was entrusted with bringing revelation to the prophets?
aq-009.e: Jibrīl is the angel of revelation, called in the Quran the Trustworthy Spirit (26:193). Mīkāʾīl is commonly associated with rain, Isrāfīl with the trumpet, and Mālik is the keeper of Hell.

aq-010.src: Ibn Kathīr, al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya, on the creation of the angels
aq-010.q: Which angel is commonly described by the scholars as entrusted with rain and vegetation?
aq-010.e: Scholars commonly mention Mīkāʾīl as the angel entrusted with rain and plants. Jibrīl is linked to revelation, which gives life to hearts, and Isrāfīl to the blowing of the trumpet.

aq-011.q: The people of Hell call out to an angel by name with the highlighted word. Who is he?
o: Isrāfīl, the blower of the trumpet
aq-011.e: In the verse shown the people of the Fire call out to Mālik, asking that their Lord put an end to them. Mālik is the keeper of Hell named in the Quran.

aq-012.q: To which prophet was the Tawrāt revealed?
aq-012.e: The Tawrāt was revealed to Mūsā, the Zabūr to Dāwūd and the Injīl to ʿĪsā. The Quran mentions scriptures (ṣuḥuf) of Ibrāhīm as well.

aq-013.q: To which prophet was the Zabūr given?
aq-013.e: The Quran states that Allah gave Dāwūd the Zabūr (4:163, 17:55). Sulaymān was his son, and Yaḥyā is not associated with a named book.

aq-014.q: Which revealed book has Allah Himself guaranteed to preserve?
aq-014.e: In 15:9 Allah says that He sent down the Reminder and will preserve it. The earlier books were entrusted to their communities to guard (5:44) and were not preserved in their original form.

aq-015.q: With the highlighted word and the word after it, how does the verse shown describe the Prophet Muḥammad?
o: As the Seal of the Prophets
As the first of the messengers
As the one spoken to directly
aq-015.e: The verse calls the Prophet the Seal of the Prophets: no prophet comes after him. This is a matter of consensus; ʿĪsā's return at the end of time does not contradict it, as he was a prophet before.

aq-016.q: The verse shown states that Allah spoke directly to the prophet named in the highlighted word. Who is he?
aq-016.e: The verse affirms that Allah spoke to Mūsā with real speech, emphasised by the verbal noun after his name. For this he is known as Kalīm Allāh.

aq-017.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
aq-017.e: Al-Ḥayy is the Ever-Living, whose life has no beginning and no end and is free of every deficiency. Scholars note that all the attributes of perfection depend on this perfect life.

aq-018.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
aq-018.e: Al-Qayyūm is the One who subsists by Himself, needing nothing, and by whom everything else subsists and is maintained. Al-ʿAliyy (the Most High) comes at the end of the same verse.

aq-019.q: Which meaning do the exegetes give for the divine name in the highlighted word?
o: The Master all turn to in need
The One who is First before all
The Owner of the mighty Throne
aq-019.e: Al-Ṣamad is explained by Ibn ʿAbbās and others as the Master perfect in His attributes, to whom all creatures turn in their needs, while He needs no one.

aq-020.q: What does the highlighted word affirm about Allah?
o: That He is One and unique
That He is the Most Merciful
That He is the Most High
aq-020.e: Aḥad affirms that Allah is one and unique in His essence, attributes and acts, with none like Him. This is why Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is the sūra of tawḥīd.

aq-021.q: According to the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is equal to what portion of the Quran?
aq-021.e: The Prophet said that Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ equals a third of the Quran. Many scholars explain that the Quran deals with rulings, narratives and tawḥīd, and this sūra is devoted entirely to tawḥīd.

aq-022.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Ṣalāt al-Musāfirīn (virtue of Āyat al-Kursī)
aq-022.q: According to the hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, what is special about the verse shown?
o: It is the greatest verse in the Book of Allah
It was the first verse revealed
It was the last verse revealed
It is the longest verse of the Quran
aq-022.e: The Prophet asked Ubayy which verse of the Book of Allah is greatest, and he named Āyat al-Kursī, and the Prophet praised his knowledge. The longest verse of the Quran is 2:282, not this one.

aq-023.src: Ibn al-Qayyim, Kitāb al-Rūḥ, on the barzakh
aq-023.q: What is meant by the barzakh in creed?
o: The stage between death and the resurrection
The wall between Paradise and Hell
The gathering place on the Day of Judgment
aq-023.e: Barzakh means a barrier; in creed it is the life of the grave between death and resurrection, in which there is bliss or punishment. The bridge is al-Ṣirāṭ and the wall between Paradise and Hell is linked to al-Aʿrāf.

aq-024.src: al-Tirmidhī, al-Jāmiʿ, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz (questioning in the grave)
aq-024.q: By which names are the two angels who question the dead in the grave known, as in a hadith in Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī?
aq-024.e: A hadith in al-Tirmidhī names the two questioning angels Munkar and Nakīr. Hārūt and Mārūt are mentioned in 2:102 in connection with Babylon, and Raqīb and ʿAtīd are descriptions of the recording angels in 50:18.

aq-025.src: al-Ṭaḥāwī, al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya; Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of the intercession)
aq-025.q: What is al-Ṣirāṭ on the Day of Judgment?
o: A bridge set over Hell that people must cross
The scale on which deeds are weighed
The basin from which believers drink
The book of deeds given to each person
aq-025.e: Al-Ṣirāṭ is a bridge stretched over Hell; people cross it according to their deeds. The scale is the mīzān, the basin is the ḥawḍ, and the record of deeds is the kitāb.

aq-026.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Riqāq (on the ḥawḍ)
aq-026.q: What is the ḥawḍ affirmed by Ahl al-Sunna?
o: The Prophet's basin from which his community drinks
A river flowing beneath the Throne of Allah
The spring in which the dead are washed
The well of Zamzam brought to the Hereafter
aq-026.e: The ḥawḍ is the basin granted to the Prophet on the Day of Judgment; authentic hadith describe its water as whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and whoever drinks from it will never thirst again.

aq-027.q: The highlighted word states that Allah created everything with what?
o: With a fixed number of days
With the help of the angels
aq-027.e: The verse states that Allah created everything according to qadar: a measure and decree He determined beforehand. Scholars cite it among the main Quranic proofs of the sixth pillar of faith.

aq-028.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
o: The One free of every flaw
aq-028.e: Al-Malik is the King who owns and governs all things with complete authority. Al-Quddūs (the Most Holy), al-Muhaymin (the Guardian) and al-Jabbār (the Compeller) follow in the same verse.

aq-029.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
o: The Creator who determines all things
The Originator who brings into being
aq-029.e: Al-Khāliq is the Creator who determines and brings things about. The verse then names al-Bāriʾ (the Originator) and al-Muṣawwir (the Fashioner), and closes with al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm.

aq-030.q: At the end of the hadith of Jibrīl, what did the Prophet say was the purpose of Jibrīl's visit?
o: To teach the people their religion
To announce the signs of the Hour
To test the knowledge of ʿUmar
To bring a new revelation of the Quran
aq-030.e: The Prophet said that it was Jibrīl, who came to teach the people their religion. Scholars therefore see islām, īmān and iḥsān together as the levels of the whole religion.

aq-031.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-031.q: When asked in the hadith of Jibrīl about the time of the Hour, what did the Prophet reply?
o: The one asked knows no more than the one asking
It will come after a thousand years
It will come on a Friday in Muḥarram
Only Jibrīl has been told its time
aq-031.e: The Prophet answered that the one asked knows no better than the questioner, showing that knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah alone. He then mentioned some of its signs.

aq-032.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Jibrīl)
aq-032.q: Which sign of the Hour is mentioned in the hadith of Jibrīl?
o: Barefoot shepherds competing in tall buildings
The sun rising from the place of its setting
The emergence of the Beast from the earth
The descent of ʿĪsā son of Maryam
aq-032.e: In the hadith of Jibrīl the Prophet mentions that the slave woman gives birth to her mistress and that barefoot, destitute shepherds compete in constructing tall buildings. The other three are major signs from other hadith.

aq-033.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on tawḥīd
aq-033.q: In the threefold division of tawḥīd common in the Atharī tradition, what is tawḥīd al-rubūbiyya?
o: Affirming Allah alone as Creator, Owner and Disposer
Directing all acts of worship to Allah alone
Following the Prophet alone in religion
aq-033.e: Tawḥīd al-rubūbiyya is singling Allah out in His acts: creating, owning, providing and governing. Directing worship to Him alone is tawḥīd al-ulūhiyya, and affirming His names and attributes is tawḥīd al-asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt.

aq-034.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on tawḥīd
aq-034.q: In the same threefold division, what does tawḥīd al-ulūhiyya mean?
o: Directing all worship to Allah alone
Affirming that Allah has no beginning
Believing that Allah alone knows the unseen
aq-034.e: Tawḥīd al-ulūhiyya (also called tawḥīd al-ʿibāda) is singling Allah out with every act of worship: prayer, supplication, sacrifice, vows, reliance and the like. It is the meaning of the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

aq-035.src: al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd sharḥ Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, on waḥdāniyya
aq-035.q: Ashʿarī and Māturīdī texts commonly explain Allah's oneness (waḥdāniyya) as oneness in which three respects?
aq-035.e: Kalām manuals explain waḥdāniyya as oneness in essence (no composition and no second), in attributes (none like His) and in acts (no creator besides Him). The lordship–worship–names scheme is the common Atharī division.

aq-036.src: Aḥmad, al-Musnad, hadith of Maḥmūd ibn Labīd (the minor shirk)
aq-036.q: What did the Prophet call "the minor shirk", which he feared most for his community?
aq-036.e: In the hadith of Maḥmūd ibn Labīd in the Musnad, the Prophet said what he feared most for them was the minor shirk, and when asked, he said it is riyāʾ: doing a deed of worship to be seen by people.

aq-037.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on shirk
aq-037.q: What is the main difference between major and minor shirk according to the scholars?
o: Major shirk takes one out of Islam; minor shirk does not by itself
Minor shirk is in the heart; major shirk only on the tongue
Major shirk is forgiven by good deeds; minor is not
Minor shirk concerns other religions; major concerns Muslims
aq-037.e: Major shirk, such as worshipping other than Allah, takes a person out of Islam and is not forgiven if one dies upon it. Minor shirk, such as slight riyāʾ, is a grave sin and a means to major shirk, but does not by itself remove one from Islam.

aq-038.src: al-Tirmidhī, al-Jāmiʿ, Kitāb al-Daʿawāt (supplication is worship)
aq-038.q: Which hadith, narrated by al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr in the Sunan, shows that supplication must be directed to Allah alone?
aq-038.e: The Prophet said that supplication is worship and then recited 40:60. Since duʿāʾ is worship, directing it to anyone besides Allah contradicts tawḥīd al-ʿibāda.

aq-039.q: What does the verse shown instruct the believers to do with Allah's beautiful names?
o: To call upon Him by them
To write them on their homes
To count them on their fingers
To keep them secret from others
aq-039.e: The verse states that the most beautiful names belong to Allah and commands that He be called upon by them, and warns against those who deviate regarding His names.

aq-040.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tawḥīd (Allah has ninety-nine names)
aq-040.q: According to the hadith of Abū Hurayra in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, whoever does what with Allah's ninety-nine names enters Paradise?
o: Whoever hangs them in his house
aq-040.e: The hadith says that Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever enumerates them (aḥṣāhā) enters Paradise. Scholars explain this as learning them, understanding their meanings and acting by them.

aq-041.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
o: The Most Holy, free of every imperfection
The Source of peace and safety
aq-041.e: Al-Quddūs is the One utterly pure and free from every deficiency and fault, deserving every praise. Al-Salām, which follows, is often explained as the One free of defects and the source of safety.

aq-042.q: Which meaning do the exegetes give for the divine name in the highlighted word?
o: The Witness and Guardian over His creation
The Mighty who is never overcome
The One who mends what is broken
aq-042.e: Al-Muhaymin is explained by Ibn ʿAbbās and others as the Witness over the deeds of His creatures, watching and guarding them. Granting security belongs to al-Muʾmin just before it, and might to al-ʿAzīz after it.

aq-043.q: The highlighted word and the two after it describe Allah as the Knower of what?
aq-043.e: The verse describes Allah as the Knower of the ghayb and the shahāda: what is hidden from creatures and what they perceive. Nothing in either realm is hidden from Him.

aq-044.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
o: The Fashioner who gives each thing its form
The Originator who brings into being
aq-044.e: Al-Muṣawwir is the One who gives every creature its particular shape and form. Scholars describe the sequence of the verse as determining (al-Khāliq), bringing into being (al-Bāriʾ) and forming (al-Muṣawwir).

aq-045.q: According to the verse shown, what of Allah's encompasses the heavens and the earth (highlighted word)?
aq-045.e: The verse states that His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, which is why it is called Āyat al-Kursī. Many scholars distinguish the Kursī from the Throne (ʿArsh), which is greater still.

aq-046.q: What does the divine name in the highlighted word mean?
aq-046.e: Al-ʿAliyy is the Most High, exalted in rank, in power and above His creation. Al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent) is the name that closes the verse right after it.

aq-047.q: What does the highlighted word negate of Allah?
aq-047.e: Kufuw means an equal or match. The verse negates that anyone is comparable to Allah, completing the sūra's affirmation of His oneness and His freedom from begetting and being begotten.

aq-048.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zuhd (creation of angels from light)
aq-048.q: According to the hadith of ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from what were the angels created?
aq-048.e: The hadith states that the angels were created from light, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire, and Ādam from what has been described (clay).

aq-049.q: According to the verse shown, to which kind of creation did Iblīs belong?
aq-049.e: The verse states explicitly that Iblīs was of the jinn and departed from his Lord's command. Angels do not disobey Allah (66:6), which is one reason scholars distinguish him from them.

aq-050.q: Which two angels are named in the verse shown, in connection with Babylon?
aq-050.e: The verse mentions what was sent down to the two angels in Babylon, Hārūt and Mārūt, who warned that they were only a trial. Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl are named together in 2:98.

aq-051.q: By what title does the verse shown refer to the angel who takes the souls?
aq-051.e: The Quran calls him malak al-mawt, the angel of death. The name ʿAzrāʾīl is widespread among Muslims, but scholars note that it is not found in the Quran or in an authentic hadith.

aq-052.q: The verse shown mentions the scriptures (ṣuḥuf) of which two prophets?
aq-052.e: Sūrat al-Aʿlā closes by referring to the earlier scriptures, the ṣuḥuf of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā. Belief in the books includes believing in every book Allah revealed, named or unnamed.

aq-053.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on prophethood
aq-053.q: Which statement reflects the common view on the relation between nabī (prophet) and rasūl (messenger)?
o: Every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger
Every prophet is a messenger, but not every messenger is a prophet
The two words always mean exactly the same
A messenger is an angel, a prophet a human
aq-053.e: Most scholars hold that rasūl is more specific: every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. They differ on the exact criterion, for example being sent with a new law or to a people who reject.

aq-054.q: How many prophets and messengers are commonly counted as named in the Quran?
aq-054.e: Scholars commonly count twenty-five prophets named in the Quran, eighteen of them in 6:83–86. The Quran states that there are others not narrated to the Prophet (4:164).

aq-055.q: Which prophet is commonly counted among the Ulū al-ʿAzm (the messengers of firm resolve)?
aq-055.e: The most widespread view counts five as Ulū al-ʿAzm: Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Muḥammad, who are named together in 33:7 and 42:13.

aq-056.src: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, al-Shifā, section on the ʿiṣma of the prophets
aq-056.q: On which aspect of the prophets' protection (ʿiṣma) is there consensus?
o: Protection from error in conveying the message
Protection from all illness and hardship
Protection from ever being harmed by enemies
aq-056.e: Scholars agree that the prophets are protected from lying or erring in conveying what Allah revealed. Prophets did suffer illness, hardship and harm from enemies, which does not contradict their ʿiṣma.

aq-057.q: What do the scholars regard as the greatest miracle of the Prophet Muḥammad?
aq-057.e: The Quran is his greatest and lasting miracle, with which he challenged the Arabs to produce anything like it. The other miracles were witnessed at their time; the Quran remains for every generation.

aq-058.q: How many blowings of the trumpet are explicitly mentioned in the verse shown?
o: Two: one causing all to swoon, one raising them
Four: one for each corner of the earth
aq-058.e: The verse mentions a first blowing at which all in the heavens and earth swoon, except whom Allah wills, and then another blowing at which they stand looking on. Some scholars add a blowing of terror from 27:87, but this verse names two.

aq-059.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tawḥīd (hadith of the intercession)
o: The Prophet's intercession for the judgment to begin
The martyrs' intercession for their families
The Quran's intercession for its reciters
aq-059.e: In the long hadith of intercession people go from prophet to prophet until they come to Muḥammad, who intercedes for all of creation so that the judgment may begin. Scholars connect this with the Praised Station (17:79), and it is specific to him.

aq-060.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on intercession
aq-060.q: The highlighted word concerns intercession. Which two conditions do scholars derive from this and related verses (20:109, 53:26)?
o: Allah's permission and His being pleased with the one interceded for
The intercessor's lineage and the sinner's wealth
A request in writing and witnesses for it
The intercessor's presence at the grave and a sacrifice
aq-060.e: The verse states that none intercedes with Him except by His permission. Combined with verses on His being pleased with the one interceded for, scholars derive two conditions: the permission of Allah and His acceptance of the person concerned.

aq-061.q: Ahl al-Sunna cite the verse shown (with the one before it) as proof of what?
o: That the believers will see their Lord in the Hereafter
That Paradise has eight gates for the believers
That the righteous will intercede for their families
That the sun will be brought near to the creatures
aq-061.e: The verses describe radiant faces looking at their Lord. Together with mass-transmitted hadith, Ahl al-Sunna across the Atharī, Ashʿarī and Māturīdī schools affirm that the believers will see Allah in the Hereafter.

aq-062.q: The people standing on the heights between Paradise and Hell give their name to which sūra?
aq-062.e: Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:46–49) describes people on the heights of the partition between the two abodes; many scholars explain them as those whose good and bad deeds are equal, who will eventually enter Paradise.

aq-063.q: What does the highlighted verb state happens to the believers when Allah's verses are recited to them?
aq-063.e: The verse says that the recitation of His verses increases them in faith. Scholars who hold that īmān increases and decreases cite this verse, together with 48:4 and others.

aq-064.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal
aq-064.q: Which imam is famous for his steadfastness during the Miḥna over the claim that the Quran is created?
aq-064.e: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal refused under imprisonment and flogging to say that the Quran is created, affirming that it is the uncreated speech of Allah. Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa and Sufyān al-Thawrī had died before the Miḥna.

aq-065.src: al-Sanūsī, Umm al-Barāhīn, on the attributes of maʿānī
aq-065.q: In the Ashʿarī scheme, which of the following belongs to the seven attributes of maʿānī (attributes of meaning)?
aq-065.e: The seven maʿānī are life, knowledge, power, will, hearing, sight and speech. Baqāʾ, qiyām bi-l-nafs and waḥdāniyya are counted among the negating (salbī) attributes in the same scheme.

aq-066.src: Ibn ʿAsākir, Tabyīn Kadhib al-Muftarī, on the lineage of al-Ashʿarī
aq-066.q: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī descended from which Companion?
aq-066.e: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ashʿarī traced his lineage to the Companion Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, which is why Ibn ʿAsākir and others connect him with the Prophet's praise of the Ashʿarī tribe.

aq-067.src: Ibn Abī al-Wafāʾ, al-Jawāhir al-Muḍiyya, biography of al-Māturīdī
aq-067.q: In which city did Abū Manṣūr al-Māturīdī, author of Kitāb al-Tawḥīd and Taʾwīlāt Ahl al-Sunna, live and teach?
aq-067.e: Al-Māturīdī was a Ḥanafī theologian of Samarqand in Transoxiana; Māturīd is a quarter of that city. Al-Ashʿarī was active in Basra and Baghdad, and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Egypt.

aq-068.q: Al-Ṭaḥāwī says in the introduction of his creed that it presents the doctrine of which scholars?
o: Abū Ḥanīfa, Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad al-Shaybānī
aq-068.e: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭaḥāwī, himself a Ḥanafī jurist of Egypt, states that he presents the creed of Ahl al-Sunna according to Abū Ḥanīfa and his two companions Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Shaybānī.

aq-069.src: Ibn Rajab, Dhayl Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābila, biography of Ibn Qudāma
aq-069.q: Which Ḥanbalī scholar, also author of the fiqh encyclopedia al-Mughnī, wrote the short creed Lumʿat al-Iʿtiqād?
aq-069.e: Muwaffaq al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qudāma al-Maqdisī wrote Lumʿat al-Iʿtiqād as well as al-Mughnī and al-ʿUmda. Ibn Taymiyya wrote al-ʿAqīda al-Wāsiṭiyya.

aq-070.src: Ḥājjī Khalīfa, Kashf al-Ẓunūn, entry on al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya
aq-070.q: Who wrote the most famous commentary on al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya of Najm al-Dīn ʿUmar al-Nasafī?
aq-070.e: Al-Taftāzānī's Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya became a standard text in madrasas and attracted many glosses. Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz commented on the Ṭaḥāwiyya, al-Bayjūrī on Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, and al-Qārī on al-Fiqh al-Akbar.

aq-071.src: Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī, Minaḥ al-Rawḍ al-Azhar fī Sharḥ al-Fiqh al-Akbar, introduction
aq-071.q: The short creed al-Fiqh al-Akbar is traditionally attributed to which imam?
aq-071.e: Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is attributed to Abū Ḥanīfa through the transmission of his students, and was commented on by Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī and others. Here 'fiqh' means understanding of the religion's foundations, not law.

aq-072.q: How do the Atharī scholars, following the early ahl al-ḥadīth, commonly define īmān?
o: Belief of the heart, statement of the tongue and action of the limbs
Assent of the heart alone, without speech or deeds
Statement of the tongue alone, even without belief
Knowledge of Allah by the intellect, without assent
aq-072.e: The ahl al-ḥadīth define īmān as belief in the heart, speech on the tongue and deeds of the limbs, and say it increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience. The Ḥanafī-Māturīdī tradition defines its core differently.

aq-073.q: How does al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, in line with the Ḥanafī tradition, define īmān?
o: Affirmation with the tongue and assent with the heart
Assent of the heart, speech and deeds of the limbs
Knowledge of the heart without any statement
aq-073.e: Al-Ṭaḥāwī defines īmān as affirmation (iqrār) with the tongue and assent (taṣdīq) with the heart, reflecting the view of Abū Ḥanīfa. Deeds are required and rewarded but not counted as part of the essence of īmān in this definition.

aq-074.src: al-Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya, on the increase and decrease of īmān
aq-074.q: Which statement correctly describes the positions on whether īmān increases and decreases?
o: Many Ḥanafī-Māturīdīs hold its core does not vary; Atharīs and most Ashʿarīs affirm increase and decrease
All Sunni schools deny that īmān increases or decreases in any sense whatsoever
The Ḥanafīs affirm increase and decrease, while the Atharīs and Ashʿarīs deny it entirely
Only the Ashʿarīs hold that īmān increases, and only through more knowledge of the proofs
aq-074.e: The Atharīs and most Ashʿarīs affirm that īmān increases and decreases. Many Ḥanafī-Māturīdīs hold that its core (taṣdīq) does not increase or decrease, while its strength and fruits do vary; several scholars therefore regard much of the difference as verbal.

aq-075.src: al-Ṭaḥāwī, al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on the people of major sins
aq-075.q: According to al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, what is the state in the Hereafter of a believer who dies with major sins unrepented?
o: Under Allah's will: He may forgive or punish, but not eternally
Neither a believer nor a disbeliever, in an intermediate station
aq-075.e: Ahl al-Sunna hold that such a person remains a believer whose fate is under Allah's will: He may forgive him by His grace or punish him by His justice, then bring him out of the Fire. He does not remain in it forever.

aq-076.src: Ibn al-Qayyim, Shifāʾ al-ʿAlīl, on the levels of qadar
aq-076.q: Which list gives the four levels (marātib) of belief in qadar as commonly taught?
aq-076.e: Scholars commonly teach four levels: Allah's eternal knowledge of everything, His writing of it in the Preserved Tablet, His will by which whatever He wills happens, and His creation of all things, including the acts of His servants.

aq-077.q: The highlighted word states that every calamity is in something before it occurs. Which level of qadar does this verse most directly establish?
aq-077.e: The verse says every misfortune is recorded in a Book before Allah brings it into being, which is the level of writing in the Preserved Tablet. Knowledge is implied, but the explicit point is the prior record.

aq-078.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Qadar (hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr)
aq-078.q: According to the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, when did Allah write the measures of creation?
o: Fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth
On the Night of Decree, renewed in every single year
When the soul is breathed into the foetus in the womb
One thousand years before the creation of Ādam
aq-078.e: The hadith states that Allah wrote the measures of all creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. The yearly decree on Laylat al-Qadr and the writing for the foetus are further, detailed records.

aq-079.q: In what is everything that Allah decreed recorded, according to the creed of Ahl al-Sunna?
o: The scrolls of the recording angels
aq-079.e: Ahl al-Sunna believe that Allah recorded everything until the Day of Resurrection in the Preserved Tablet. The recording angels write the deeds of each person as they happen, which is a different record.

aq-080.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, on 39:68 (hadith of Abū Hurayra)
aq-080.q: According to the hadith of Abū Hurayra in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, which part of the human body does not decay and is the origin of re-creation?
o: The base of the spine (ʿajb al-dhanab)
The tip of the tongue (ṭaraf al-lisān)
aq-080.e: The Prophet said that every part of the human being decays except ʿajb al-dhanab, the tip of the tailbone, from which he was created and from which he will be re-created. Ahl al-Sunna affirm a bodily resurrection.

aq-081.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Faḍāʾil (I am the master of the children of Ādam)
aq-081.q: According to the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, who is the first for whom the grave will split open on the Day of Resurrection?
aq-081.e: The Prophet said that he is the master of the children of Ādam on the Day of Resurrection, the first for whom the grave splits open, the first to intercede and the first whose intercession is accepted.

aq-082.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Fitan (hadith of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān)
aq-082.q: According to the hadith of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, where will ʿĪsā kill the Dajjāl?
aq-082.e: The hadith relates that ʿĪsā descends near the white minaret east of Damascus, pursues the Dajjāl and kills him at the gate of Ludd. Other hadith state that the Dajjāl cannot enter Medina.

aq-083.q: The Prophet connected the verse shown with which major sign, after which faith or repentance no longer benefits one who had not believed before?
o: The rising of the sun from the west
The coming of Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj
The fire that drives people to the gathering
aq-083.e: In al-Bukhārī the Prophet said that the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west, and when people see it they will all believe, but that is when faith does not benefit a soul that had not believed before; he then recited this verse.

aq-084.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Fitan (hadith of Ḥudhayfa ibn Asīd)
aq-084.q: How many major signs of the Hour are listed in the hadith of Ḥudhayfa ibn Asīd in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim?
aq-084.e: The hadith lists ten signs: the smoke, the Dajjāl, the Beast, the sun rising from the west, the descent of ʿĪsā, Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, three landslides (in the east, the west and Arabia), and a fire from Yemen driving people to their gathering.

aq-085.q: What do Ahl al-Sunna affirm about the scales mentioned in the highlighted word?
o: Real scales with pans, set up on that Day
Only a metaphor for Allah's perfect justice
Scales set up only for the disbelievers
Scales held by the prophets for their peoples
aq-085.e: Ahl al-Sunna affirm a real balance; the hadith of the card (al-biṭāqa) in al-Tirmidhī mentions its pans. Taking it as a mere metaphor for justice was the view of some outside Ahl al-Sunna.

aq-086.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Jihād (degrees of the mujāhidīn)
aq-086.q: According to the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, which level of Paradise is the highest, with the Throne of the Most Merciful above it?
aq-086.e: The Prophet said that when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise, above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow.

aq-087.q: According to the highlighted word, how many will bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day?
aq-087.e: The verse states that on that Day eight will carry the Throne of your Lord above them. Some reports say they are four before the Day of Judgment, completed to eight on that Day.

aq-088.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Badʾ al-Khalq (hadith of the Miʿrāj)
aq-088.q: According to the hadith of the Miʿrāj in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, how many angels enter al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr every day, never to return to it?
aq-088.e: In the hadith of the Miʿrāj the Prophet was shown al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, which seventy thousand angels enter every day and never return to. Scholars cite it to show the vast number of angels, known fully only to Allah (74:31).

aq-089.q: The highlighted word describes the angels who guard over people as doing what?
aq-089.e: Sūrat al-Infiṭār describes guardians over people who are noble and who write, knowing what people do. These are the recording angels; elsewhere one on the right and one on the left are mentioned (50:17).

aq-090.src: al-Ṭaḥāwī, al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on the karāmāt of the awliyāʾ; al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd
aq-090.q: What distinguishes a karāma from a muʿjiza in Sunni creed?
o: It occurs for a righteous believer who claims no prophethood
It can only occur after the death of the righteous person
It is always greater in scale than any muʿjiza
It is a natural event that science can explain
aq-090.e: Both break the normal course of things. A muʿjiza accompanies a claim of prophethood with a challenge, while a karāma is an honour for a righteous follower who claims no prophethood. Ahl al-Sunna affirm the karāmāt of the awliyāʾ.

aq-091.src: al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd sharḥ Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, on the muʿjiza
aq-091.q: Which element is part of the theologians' definition of a muʿjiza?
o: It is coupled with a challenge (taḥaddī) by one claiming prophethood
It must be witnessed by every member of the community
It must occur in the Ḥaram of Mecca
It must leave a physical trace until the Last Day
aq-091.e: Theologians define a muʿjiza as an event breaking the normal course of things, coupled with a challenge by one who claims prophethood, and which cannot be matched. This distinguishes it from a karāma and from sorcery.

aq-092.src: al-Bayhaqī, al-Asmāʾ wa-l-Ṣifāt, chapter on istiwāʾ
aq-092.q: Asked how the act in the highlighted word is, which imam famously replied that it is known, its 'how' is not comprehended, believing in it is obligatory and asking about it is an innovation?
aq-092.e: This answer is widely reported from Imām Mālik, with similar words from his teacher Rabīʿa. Atharīs, Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs all cite it, while reading it in light of their own approaches to the attributes.

aq-093.q: The highlighted expression and the end of the verse are cited by all Sunni schools as the basis for which principle?
o: Negating any likeness to Allah while affirming His attributes
Interpreting every attribute in a metaphorical sense
Affirming the attributes with a likeness to creatures
Refraining from mentioning any attribute at all
aq-093.e: The verse negates that anything is like Him, then affirms that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Scholars derive from it the balance between tanzīh (negating likeness) and affirmation, avoiding both tashbīh and taʿṭīl.

aq-094.src: Abū Dāwūd, al-Sunan, Kitāb al-Ṭibb (on ṭiyara)
aq-094.q: In the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, how did the Prophet describe taking evil omens (ṭiyara)?
o: As a form of trust in Allah
aq-094.e: The Prophet said that ṭiyara is shirk, repeating it, because it attributes harm and benefit to omens. Scholars classify it as minor shirk unless one believes the omen itself causes events.

aq-095.src: Ibn Rajab, Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam, hadith on the signs of the hypocrite
aq-095.q: What distinguishes major hypocrisy (nifāq iʿtiqādī) from minor hypocrisy (nifāq ʿamalī)?
o: Major conceals disbelief under outward Islam; minor is traits like lying
Major is lying in speech; minor is concealing disbelief in the heart
Major concerns those in authority; minor concerns ordinary people
Major is expiated by fasting and charity; minor is never expiated
aq-095.e: Major hypocrisy is outwardly showing Islam while concealing disbelief, and takes one out of the religion. Minor hypocrisy consists of traits such as lying, breaking promises and betraying trusts, mentioned in the hadith of al-Bukhārī and Muslim; it is sinful but does not by itself remove one from Islam.

aq-096.src: al-Ṭaḥāwī, al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on Paradise and the Fire
aq-096.q: What does al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya state about Paradise and the Fire?
o: They are already created and will never perish or end
They will be created only after the Day of Judgment
They exist now but will both come to an end
They are states of the soul, not real places
aq-096.e: Al-Ṭaḥāwī states that Paradise and the Fire are created, and will never perish or come to an end. That they already exist is supported by the Quran's description of them as prepared, and by hadith of the Miʿrāj.

aq-097.src: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, introduction
aq-097.q: Which commentary on al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, by a Ḥanafī judge of the 8th century AH, became the standard reference in Atharī circles?
o: The commentary of Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz
aq-097.e: Ṣadr al-Dīn Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz al-Ḥanafī wrote a commentary on the Ṭaḥāwiyya drawing heavily on Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn al-Qayyim; it became the most used commentary in Atharī teaching. Other commentaries on the Ṭaḥāwiyya follow the Māturīdī reading.

aq-098.q: Which Ḥanbalī scholar wrote in Lawāmiʿ al-Anwār al-Bahiyya that Ahl al-Sunna wa-l-Jamāʿa comprise three groups: the Athariyya, the Ashʿariyya and the Māturīdiyya?
aq-098.e: Al-Saffārīnī, in his commentary on his own poem al-Durra al-Muḍiyya, names three groups of Ahl al-Sunna: the Athariyya with Imām Aḥmad as their imam, the Ashʿariyya and the Māturīdiyya. The statement is often cited when describing the scope of Sunni creed.

aq-099.src: Ibn ʿAsākir, Tabyīn Kadhib al-Muftarī, on al-Ashʿarī's early life
aq-099.q: Under which Muʿtazilī teacher did Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī study before he left the Muʿtazila?
aq-099.e: Al-Ashʿarī studied for years under Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī, head of the Basran Muʿtazila, before publicly leaving them. Wāṣil and al-Naẓẓām lived earlier, and al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār later.

aq-100.src: Ibn ʿAsākir, Tabyīn Kadhib al-Muftarī, list of al-Ashʿarī's works
aq-100.q: Which work of al-Ashʿarī is a survey of the doctrines of the various Muslim groups?
aq-100.e: Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn wa-Ikhtilāf al-Muṣallīn records the views of the various groups, and is a key early source for the history of theology. Al-Ibāna and al-Lumaʿ present his own creed and arguments, and the Risāla ilā Ahl al-Thaghr is a creed sent to scholars of a frontier region.

aq-101.src: Ibn Quṭlūbughā, Tāj al-Tarājim, entries on the Nasafīs
aq-101.q: Several scholars bear the nisba al-Nasafī. Which work is by Abū al-Muʿīn Maymūn al-Nasafī, a major Māturīdī theologian?
aq-101.e: Abū al-Muʿīn al-Nasafī wrote Tabṣirat al-Adilla, a detailed Māturīdī summa. Al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya is by Najm al-Dīn ʿUmar al-Nasafī, while Madārik al-Tanzīl (tafsīr) and Kanz al-Daqāʾiq (Ḥanafī fiqh) are by Abū al-Barakāt al-Nasafī.

aq-102.src: al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd sharḥ Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, introduction
aq-102.q: Who composed the didactic poem Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, widely taught in Ashʿarī circles and commented on by al-Bayjūrī?
aq-102.e: Jawharat al-Tawḥīd is the poem of the Egyptian Mālikī scholar Ibrāhīm al-Laqānī; al-Bayjūrī's Tuḥfat al-Murīd is one of its best-known commentaries. Al-Sanūsī wrote Umm al-Barāhīn, and Ibn ʿĀshir wrote al-Murshid al-Muʿīn.

aq-103.src: al-Sanūsī, Umm al-Barāhīn, on the necessary attributes
aq-103.q: In al-Sanūsī's Umm al-Barāhīn, how many attributes are listed in detail as necessary (wājib) for Allah?
aq-103.e: Al-Sanūsī lists twenty necessary attributes: one nafsiyya (existence), five salbiyya, seven of maʿānī and seven maʿnawiyya. Those who do not count the maʿnawiyya separately arrive at thirteen; seven is the number of the maʿānī alone.

aq-104.src: al-Sanūsī, Umm al-Barāhīn, on the salbī attributes
aq-104.q: In al-Sanūsī's classification, which attribute is counted among the five salbī (negating) attributes?
aq-104.e: The five salbī attributes negate something unfitting: beginninglessness (qidam), everlastingness (baqāʾ), dissimilarity to created things, self-subsistence and oneness. Wujūd is the nafsiyya attribute, ʿilm is one of the maʿānī, and being All-Hearing is one of the maʿnawiyya.

aq-105.src: Abū al-Muʿīn al-Nasafī, Tabṣirat al-Adilla, on takwīn; al-Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya
aq-105.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between Māturīdīs and Ashʿarīs regarding takwīn (bringing into being)?
o: Māturīdīs: a distinct eternal attribute; Ashʿarīs: a relation of power, not a separate attribute
Ashʿarīs: a distinct eternal attribute; Māturīdīs: they deny any attribute of this kind
Both schools: takwīn is created in time together with each created thing
Both schools: takwīn is simply another name for the attribute of knowledge
aq-105.e: Māturīdīs affirm takwīn as an eternal attribute subsisting in Allah, distinct from power, whose effects occur at their appointed times. Ashʿarīs do not count it as a separate eternal attribute but explain it through the actualising relations of power.

aq-106.src: al-Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya, on the attribute of speech
aq-106.q: What term do Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs use for Allah's eternal speech subsisting in His essence, as distinct from the recited and written expressions?
aq-106.e: Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs distinguish the eternal speech subsisting in Allah (al-kalām al-nafsī) from the expressions that are recited, written and memorised (al-kalām al-lafẓī), while both call the Quran the uncreated speech of Allah. The Atharī tradition formulates the attribute of speech differently.

aq-107.src: Ibn al-Jawzī, Dafʿ Shubah al-Tashbīh; Ibn Qudāma, Dhamm al-Taʾwīl
aq-107.q: Regarding texts such as the one shown, which approach consigns the precise meaning to Allah while negating likeness, and is held by many Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs as the way of the early generations?
aq-107.e: Tafwīḍ affirms the text, negates likeness and leaves its precise meaning to Allah. Taʾwīl interprets it by a meaning supported by Arabic usage, an approach found among many later Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs; Atharīs affirm the apparent meaning while leaving the 'how' to Allah. All three reject tashbīh.

aq-108.src: Ibn Taymiyya, al-ʿAqīda al-Wāsiṭiyya; Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on irāda
aq-108.q: In Atharī terminology, what is the name of Allah's will by which everything that occurs comes to be, including what He does not love?
aq-108.e: Atharīs distinguish al-irāda al-kawniyya (creative will), which necessarily occurs and includes what Allah dislikes, from al-irāda al-sharʿiyya or dīniyya (legislative will), which is tied to His love and may not be obeyed. Ashʿarīs and Māturīdīs express the same point through the distinction between will and command or pleasure.

aq-109.src: al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd sharḥ Jawharat al-Tawḥīd, on kasb
aq-109.q: Which term do the Ashʿarīs use for the human being's connection to the voluntary acts that Allah creates?
aq-109.e: Ashʿarīs teach that Allah creates the acts of servants and the servant acquires them (kasb), which is the basis of moral responsibility. Jabr denies human choice, ikhtirāʿ (the servant originating his acts independently) is the Muʿtazilī formulation, and tawallud is a Muʿtazilī notion.

aq-110.src: al-Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya, on istithnāʾ; Ibn Taymiyya, Kitāb al-Īmān
aq-110.q: On saying "I am a believer, in shāʾ Allāh" (istithnāʾ in īmān), which description of the positions is correct?
o: Many Atharīs and Ashʿarīs permit it, not as doubt; Ḥanafī-Māturīdīs generally disapprove
All Sunni schools forbid it, since it expresses doubt in one's present faith
Ḥanafī-Māturīdīs make it obligatory, while Atharīs and Ashʿarīs forbid it
Only the Ashʿarīs discussed the issue; the other schools never addressed it
aq-110.e: Atharīs permit it with reference to the completeness of faith and avoiding self-praise, and Ashʿarīs with reference to one's final state (al-muwāfāt). Ḥanafī-Māturīdīs generally disapprove of it because it may sound like doubt in present faith. All agree that doubt in faith itself is not acceptable.

aq-111.src: Ibn Rajab, Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam, hadith 2
aq-111.q: Which principle do many scholars, such as Ibn Rajab, state about the terms islām and īmān?
o: Together they differ in meaning; apart, each includes the other
They always mean exactly the same thing, wherever they occur
Islām always refers to the heart, and īmān always to the limbs
They are never both applied to one and the same person
aq-111.e: In the hadith of Jibrīl, where both are mentioned together, islām refers to outward acts and īmān to inward belief. Where one is mentioned alone, it includes the meaning of the other. Scholars summarise this in the formula: when they come together they separate, and when they separate they come together.

aq-112.src: Ibn Rajab, Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam, hadith 2
aq-112.q: Ibn Rajab explains that the definition of iḥsān in the hadith of Jibrīl contains two levels. What is the lower of the two?
o: Worshipping with awareness that Allah sees you
Worshipping as though you see Allah
aq-112.e: The higher level is to worship as though one sees Allah (often called mushāhada). The second is to worship knowing that Allah sees you (murāqaba); whoever finds the first hard can rely on the second.

aq-113.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (account of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar)
aq-113.q: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Ibn ʿUmar narrates the hadith of Jibrīl after being asked about people in Basra who denied qadar. Who is named as the first to speak about this there?
aq-113.e: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar reports that the first to speak about (denying) qadar in Basra was Maʿbad al-Juhanī. He and Ḥumayd then asked Ibn ʿUmar, who disavowed that view and narrated the hadith of Jibrīl with its sixth pillar.

aq-114.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Ṣuhayb on the vision)
aq-114.q: In the hadith of Ṣuhayb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, the Prophet recited the verse shown after mentioning what, so that the highlighted word is explained by it?
o: The lifting of the veil and the vision of their Lord
The doubling of the reward for spending in charity
The wide spaces of the palaces of the believers
The water of the Prophet's basin on that Day
aq-114.e: Ṣuhayb reports that when the people of Paradise enter it, the veil is lifted and nothing they were given is dearer to them than looking at their Lord; then the Prophet recited this verse. Many exegetes therefore explain the 'more' (ziyāda) as the vision of Allah.

aq-115.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 7:8–9 and 21:47; Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on the mīzān
aq-115.q: Which statement correctly describes the scholarly discussion about what is placed on the scale?
o: Texts mention deeds, records and the doer; some say all three are weighed
There is agreement that only the person's body is weighed
There is agreement that only the intentions are weighed
There is agreement that nothing is weighed, as it is a metaphor
aq-115.e: Scholars mention three views based on different texts: the deeds themselves given form, the records of deeds (as in the hadith of the card), or the doer himself (as in the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd's legs). Ibn Kathīr and others consider that all three may be weighed.

aq-116.src: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, al-Shifā, section on minor sins of the prophets; Ibn Taymiyya, Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā
aq-116.q: Which statement correctly describes the scholarly positions on the prophets and minor sins?
o: Disputed: many allow minor slips that are promptly corrected; others affirm full protection
Consensus that prophets fall into minor sins habitually, as other people do
Consensus that protection began only after revelation and covers only major sins
The question was never discussed by any scholar of the early or later periods
aq-116.e: There is agreement on protection in conveying the message and from major sins. On minor sins not involving baseness, many scholars held they could occur but are not persisted in and are corrected at once, while al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and others held that the prophets are protected from them too.

aq-117.src: al-Nawawī, Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Kitāb al-Dhikr (on the ninety-nine names)
aq-117.q: How do the scholars, as reported by al-Nawawī, understand the hadith that Allah has ninety-nine names?
o: It does not limit His names to ninety-nine; it praises enumerating these
Allah has exactly ninety-nine names and no other names at all
Only the names mentioned in Āyat al-Kursī are intended by it
The number refers to the angels who are named after the names
aq-117.e: Al-Nawawī reports agreement that the hadith does not limit Allah's names to this number; it informs that whoever enumerates these ninety-nine enters Paradise. Another hadith speaks of names Allah has kept in the knowledge of the unseen with Him.

aq-118.src: Ibn al-Qayyim, Badāʾiʿ al-Fawāʾid, on the names being tawqīfī; al-Bayjūrī, Tuḥfat al-Murīd
aq-118.q: According to the majority of Ahl al-Sunna, how are the divine names established?
o: Only by revelation (tawqīfī): no name without a text
By any word whose meaning is praiseworthy
By the consensus of the people of each language
By the intellect, independently of revelation
aq-118.e: The majority hold that the names of Allah are tawqīfī: one only names Him by what the Quran or the Sunna has named Him. Some theologians allowed names based on sound meaning, and many distinguish naming from describing or informing about Him (ikhbār), which is wider.

aq-119.src: al-Shahrastānī, al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal, chapter on the Muʿtazila
aq-119.q: The doctrine that a Muslim who commits a major sin is in "a station between the two stations" (neither believer nor disbeliever) is associated with whom?
o: The Muʿtazila, from Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ
The Murjiʾa, from Jahm ibn Ṣafwān
The Atharīs, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal
aq-119.e: Al-Shahrastānī and others report that Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ held this view and separated from the circle of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and it became one of the five principles of the Muʿtazila. Ahl al-Sunna hold that such a person remains a believer with deficient faith.

aq-120.src: Ibn Rajab, Dhayl Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābila, biography of Ibn Qudāma
aq-120.q: Besides Lumʿat al-Iʿtiqād, which creedal treatise was written by Ibn Qudāma al-Maqdisī?
o: Taḥrīm al-Naẓar fī Kutub Ahl al-Kalām
aq-120.e: Ibn Qudāma wrote Taḥrīm al-Naẓar fī Kutub Ahl al-Kalām, a critique of studying kalām books, as well as Dhamm al-Taʾwīl. Al-Wāsiṭiyya is by Ibn Taymiyya, al-Ibāna by al-Ashʿarī, and al-Tabṣīr fī al-Dīn by Abū al-Muẓaffar al-Isfarāyīnī.

aq-121.src: Ibn ʿAbd al-Hādī, al-ʿUqūd al-Durriyya, on the Wāsiṭiyya
aq-121.q: Which creed did Ibn Taymiyya write at the request of a judge from Wāsiṭ?
aq-121.e: Ibn Taymiyya wrote al-Wāsiṭiyya for a judge from Wāsiṭ who asked for a concise creed. Al-Ḥamawiyya answered a question from Ḥamāh, al-Tadmuriyya one from Tadmur (Palmyra), and Lumʿat al-Iʿtiqād is by Ibn Qudāma.

aq-122.q: A widely cited explanation distinguishes the name in the highlighted word from the name after it. Which distinction is meant?
o: Al-Raḥmān: mercy for all creation; al-Raḥīm: mercy specific to believers
Al-Raḥmān is mercy in this world only; al-Raḥīm mercy for the angels
Al-Raḥmān is an attribute of action; al-Raḥīm a name without meaning
Al-Raḥmān may be used of humans; al-Raḥīm is used only of Allah
aq-122.e: Many exegetes explain al-Raḥmān as the One whose mercy encompasses all creatures, and al-Raḥīm as the One whose mercy is specific to the believers, citing 33:43. Al-Raḥmān is a name used only for Allah, whereas raḥīm is also used of people (9:128).

aq-123.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:255; Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz, Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya, on negation in the attributes
aq-123.q: The verse negates of Allah what the highlighted word names, and sleep. Following the principle that a negation in the attributes implies an affirmed perfection, which perfection is shown?
o: The perfection of His life and His sustaining
The perfection of His mercy toward sinners
The perfection of His speech and His command
The perfection of His wisdom in legislation
aq-123.e: The highlighted word means drowsiness. Negating drowsiness and sleep shows the perfection of His being al-Ḥayy al-Qayyūm, named at the start of the verse: His life never weakens and His sustaining of creation never lapses. Scholars note that pure negation without an implied perfection is not praise.

fqz-001.q: In which month is fasting obligatory for every adult, sane Muslim who is able, as the verse shown states?
fqz-001.e: The verse shown names the month of Ramaḍān, in which the Quran was sent down, as the month of obligatory fasting. Fasting in Shaʿbān and Muḥarram is recommended, not obligatory.

fqz-002.q: According to the verse shown, from when to when does the daily fast last?
o: From true dawn until nightfall at sunset
From the ʿIshāʾ prayer until the ʿAṣr prayer
fqz-002.e: The verse permits eating and drinking until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black, then commands completing the fast until night, which begins at sunset. The fast therefore starts at true dawn (al-fajr al-ṣādiq), not at sunrise.

fqz-003.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, on the traveller and the sick
fqz-003.q: Which person does the verse shown allow to leave the fast of Ramaḍān and make up the days later?
o: A person with a long working day
A person who simply feels hungry
fqz-003.e: The verse names the sick and the traveller: they may break the fast and make up the same number of days afterwards. Ordinary hardship such as work, study or hunger is not an excuse.

fqz-004.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām
fqz-004.q: According to the majority (Ḥanafīs, Shāfiʿīs, Ḥanbalīs), what is the ruling on someone who eats out of forgetfulness during an obligatory fast?
o: The fast remains valid and no make-up is due
The fast is void and must be made up
The fast is void and an expiation is due
The fast is valid but a fidya is due
fqz-004.e: The majority rely on the hadith of Abū Hurayra in al-Bukhārī and Muslim that whoever forgets and eats or drinks should complete his fast, for Allah fed him. The Mālikīs hold that in an obligatory fast he must make it up, but without sin or expiation.

fqz-005.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥayḍ; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām
fqz-005.q: A woman menstruates during Ramaḍān. What is the agreed ruling?
o: She does not fast and makes up the missed days, but not the missed prayers
She fasts and makes up the days afterwards as a precaution
She does not fast and pays a fidya instead of making up
She does not fast and makes up both the fasts and the prayers
fqz-005.e: By consensus, fasting is not valid during menstruation. ʿĀʾisha reported in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that they were ordered to make up the fasts but not the prayers.

fqz-006.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām (hadith of Abū Qatāda)
fqz-006.q: According to the hadith of Abū Qatāda in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, fasting the Day of ʿArafa (for one not on ḥajj) is hoped to expiate what?
o: The sins of the previous year and the coming year
The sins of the previous year only
The sins of the past month
fqz-006.e: In that hadith the Prophet ﷺ said he hoped that fasting the Day of ʿArafa expiates the year before and the year after, and that fasting ʿĀshūrāʾ expiates the year before.

fqz-007.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ṣawm (hadith of Abū Saʿīd); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-007.q: On which days is fasting prohibited by consensus?
fqz-007.e: The Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on the day of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr and the day of ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā, and the scholars agree that fasting them is forbidden. Singling out Friday alone is disliked, not forbidden in the same way.

fqz-008.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar)
fqz-008.q: In the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, how much did the Prophet ﷺ prescribe as Zakāt al-Fiṭr from dates or barley per person?
fqz-008.e: Ibn ʿUmar reported that the Prophet ﷺ prescribed Zakāt al-Fiṭr as one ṣāʿ of dates or one ṣāʿ of barley for every Muslim, young or old. The Ḥanafīs accept half a ṣāʿ when it is paid in wheat.

fqz-009.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Zakāt al-Fiṭr
fqz-009.q: By what time did the Prophet ﷺ command Zakāt al-Fiṭr to be handed over?
o: Before the people go out to the ʿĪd prayer
Before the last ten nights of Ramaḍān
Any time before the next Ramaḍān
fqz-009.e: In the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar the Prophet ﷺ ordered that it be paid before the people go out to the prayer. Delaying it past the day of ʿĪd without excuse is sinful according to the scholars, though it remains a debt to be paid.

fqz-010.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ṣawm (hadith of Sahl ibn Saʿd)
fqz-010.q: According to the hadith of Sahl ibn Saʿd in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, people remain in goodness as long as they do what?
o: Delay breaking the fast until the stars appear
Break the fast only after the Maghrib prayer
fqz-010.e: The Prophet ﷺ said that people will remain in goodness as long as they hasten the ifṭār. Hastening the ifṭār once sunset is certain and delaying the suḥūr are among the sunan of fasting.

fqz-011.src: Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, Kitāb al-Ṣawm (hadith of Abū Hurayra); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-011.q: According to the majority, what is the difference between vomiting deliberately and being overcome by vomit while fasting?
o: Deliberate vomiting breaks the fast and requires make-up; involuntary vomiting does not
Both break the fast and require make-up
Involuntary vomiting breaks the fast; deliberate vomiting only reduces the reward
fqz-011.e: The hadith of Abū Hurayra in Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī states that whoever is overcome by vomit owes no make-up, while whoever makes himself vomit must make up the day. The majority of jurists act on this distinction.

fqz-012.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, until when may the intention for a Ramaḍān fast be made if it was not made at night?
o: Until before the midpoint of the day, counted from dawn
Only before dawn, never during the day
fqz-012.e: Al-Hidāya permits the intention for Ramaḍān, a vow tied to a specific day and voluntary fasts from the night until before the middle of the sharʿī day. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require an obligatory fast to be intended during the night.

fqz-013.src: Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ṣiyām; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām
fqz-013.q: Which school holds that a single intention at the start of Ramaḍān suffices for the whole month, as long as the fast is not interrupted?
fqz-013.e: The Mālikīs treat the consecutive fast of Ramaḍān as one act of worship, so one night intention covers it unless it is broken, for example by travel or illness. The Shāfiʿīs and the relied Ḥanbalī view require a fresh intention every night.

fqz-014.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ṣawm (hadith of Abū Hurayra); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-014.q: Following the hadith of the man who had intercourse during a day of Ramaḍān, what is the order of the expiation according to the majority?
o: Freeing a slave, then fasting two consecutive months, then feeding sixty poor people
Feeding sixty poor people, then fasting two months, then freeing a slave
Fasting three days, then feeding ten poor people, then a sacrifice
Fasting thirty days, then feeding thirty poor people, then charity
fqz-014.e: In the hadith of Abū Hurayra in al-Bukhārī and Muslim the Prophet ﷺ asked the man in this order: can he free a slave, can he fast two consecutive months, can he feed sixty poor people. The majority treat this order as binding; the Mālikīs allow a free choice.

fqz-015.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, on the elderly; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:184
fqz-015.q: The highlighted word names a compensation. According to the majority, what is due from a very old person who cannot fast and has no hope of becoming able?
o: Feeding one poor person for each day missed
Making up the days whenever possible
Nothing at all, since the duty has lapsed
fqz-015.e: The highlighted word is the fidya: feeding a poor person. Ibn ʿAbbās explained the verse as applying to the elderly who cannot fast, and the majority oblige them to feed a poor person for each day. The Mālikīs regard this feeding for the very old as recommended rather than obligatory.

fqz-016.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Iʿtikāf; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 2:187
fqz-016.q: The highlighted word is the place the verse links with iʿtikāf. Where, according to the majority, must a man perform iʿtikāf?
o: At the graves of righteous people
fqz-016.e: The verse speaks of those in iʿtikāf in the mosques, so the majority hold that iʿtikāf is only valid in a mosque. The Ḥanafīs allow a woman to perform it in the prayer place of her home.

fqz-017.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām (hadith of Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī)
fqz-017.q: According to the hadith of Abū Ayyūb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, fasting Ramaḍān followed by six days of Shawwāl is like what?
fqz-017.e: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever fasts Ramaḍān and follows it with six days of Shawwāl, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime, which the scholars explain as a whole year, each good deed counting tenfold.

fqz-018.src: al-Nasāʾī and al-Tirmidhī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām (hadith of Abū Dharr); al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Bāb Ṣawm al-Taṭawwuʿ
fqz-018.q: Which days of the lunar month are known as the White Days (ayyām al-bīḍ), on which fasting is recommended?
fqz-018.e: The White Days are the 13th, 14th and 15th of the lunar month, when the nights are lit by the full moon. Fasting three days of every month is recommended, and these days are the preferred ones.

fqz-019.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, on the expiation
fqz-019.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about deliberately eating or drinking during a day of Ramaḍān?
o: Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs require make-up and expiation; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require make-up only
Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require make-up and expiation; Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs require make-up only
All four schools require make-up and expiation
All four schools require make-up only, without expiation
fqz-019.e: The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs extend the expiation to any deliberate violation of the Ramaḍān fast, reasoning from its sanctity. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs restrict it to intercourse, the case named in the hadith, so deliberate eating requires make-up, repentance and no expiation.

fqz-020.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, on cupping; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-020.q: Which school holds that cupping (ḥijāma) breaks the fast of both the one who is cupped and the one who performs it?
fqz-020.e: The Ḥanbalīs act on the hadith that the cupper and the cupped have both broken their fast. The other three schools hold that it does not break the fast, citing the report that the Prophet ﷺ was cupped while fasting, though it is disliked for someone it weakens.

fqz-021.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-021.q: Someone delays making up Ramaḍān days without excuse until the next Ramaḍān arrives. Which statement describes the positions correctly?
o: The majority require make-up plus feeding a poor person per day; the Ḥanafīs require make-up only
The Ḥanafīs require make-up plus feeding; the majority require make-up only
All schools say the days lapse and only repentance is due
All schools require two consecutive months as expiation
fqz-021.e: Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad require the make-up together with feeding one poor person for each day, following reports from Companions such as Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās. Abū Ḥanīfa requires only the make-up, since the verse mentions make-up without a time limit.

fqz-022.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Iʿtikāf; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Iʿtikāf
fqz-022.q: Which schools make fasting a condition of iʿtikāf (at least of an iʿtikāf that has been vowed)?
fqz-022.e: The Mālikīs require fasting for every iʿtikāf, and the Ḥanafīs require it for a vowed iʿtikāf. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs do not make it a condition, citing ʿUmar's vow to spend a night in iʿtikāf, since a night has no fast.

fqz-023.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭr; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Zakāt al-Fiṭr
fqz-023.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about paying Zakāt al-Fiṭr in money instead of food?
o: The Ḥanafīs permit paying its value; the Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require the foodstuffs named in the hadith
The Shāfiʿīs permit paying its value; the other three schools require food
All four schools prefer money and permit food only as a substitute
All four schools forbid food and require money
fqz-023.e: The Ḥanafīs see the purpose as enriching the poor on the day of ʿĪd and so accept the value. The majority hold to the wording of the hadith, which specifies a ṣāʿ of food, and do not accept value in its place in their relied positions.

fqz-024.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭr; al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Bāb Zakāt al-Fiṭr
fqz-024.q: At what moment does Zakāt al-Fiṭr become obligatory?
o: Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: at sunset on the last day of Ramaḍān; Ḥanafīs: at dawn on the day of ʿĪd
Ḥanafīs: at sunset on the last day of Ramaḍān; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: at dawn on the day of ʿĪd
All schools: at the start of Ramaḍān
All schools: after the ʿĪd prayer
fqz-024.e: The disagreement matters for a child born or a person who dies in the night before ʿĪd. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs link the obligation to the end of Ramaḍān at sunset, the Ḥanafīs to the dawn of the day of breaking the fast; the Mālikīs have two narrations.

fqz-025.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām; Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ṣiyām
fqz-025.q: A pregnant woman and a nursing mother break the fast fearing only for the child. Which statement describes the schools correctly?
o: Ḥanafīs: make-up only; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: make-up and feeding; Mālikīs: feeding for the nursing mother but not the pregnant woman
Ḥanafīs: make-up and feeding for both; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: make-up only; Mālikīs: feeding for the pregnant woman only
All four schools: feeding only, with no make-up
All four schools: make-up only, with no feeding
fqz-025.e: Ibn Rushd explains the disagreement by whether such women resemble the sick (make-up only) or those able to fast with hardship (feeding). The Ḥanafīs treat both like the sick; the Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require both make-up and feeding when the fear is for the child; the Mālikīs class pregnancy as illness but require feeding from the nursing mother.

fqz-026.src: Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ṣiyām, on the expiation; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-026.q: How does the Mālikī school treat the three options of the Ramaḍān expiation?
o: As a free choice, with feeding sixty poor people the best option
As a strict order beginning with freeing a slave
As a strict order beginning with fasting two months
As a free choice, with fasting two months the only valid option today
fqz-026.e: Khalīl's Mukhtaṣar treats the expiation as a choice between feeding sixty poor people, fasting two consecutive months and freeing a slave, and names feeding as the best because its benefit reaches many. The majority read the hadith as prescribing a fixed order.

fqz-027.src: Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ṣiyām; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, on the intention
fqz-027.q: A person decides in the late morning to begin a voluntary fast, having eaten nothing since dawn. Which school does NOT consider this fast valid?
fqz-027.e: The Mālikīs require the intention to be made during the night for every fast, voluntary or obligatory, applying the general hadith of Ḥafṣa. The other three schools accept a daytime intention for a voluntary fast, citing ʿĀʾisha's report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that the Prophet ﷺ, finding no food, said he would then fast.

fqz-028.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣawm, on fasting the days of tashrīq
fqz-028.q: According to the report of ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿUmar in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, who was granted a concession to fast on the days of tashrīq?
o: A pilgrim on tamattuʿ or qirān who finds no sacrificial animal
A person making up missed Ramaḍān days
Anyone who has vowed to fast
A person observing the six days of Shawwāl
fqz-028.e: They reported that no concession was given to fast the days of tashrīq except for someone who finds no hady. This is why the Mālikīs and one narration from Aḥmad allow the pilgrim without hady to fast the three days of ḥajj then, while the Ḥanafīs and the new Shāfiʿī view do not.

fqz-029.src: Mālik, al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-029.q: Which imam is reported in his own work to have disliked fasting the six days of Shawwāl, fearing that people would think them part of Ramaḍān?
o: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal in his Musnad
fqz-029.e: Mālik stated in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ that he had not seen the people of knowledge fast them and disliked it lest they be joined to Ramaḍān. Later Mālikīs restricted the dislike to fasting them immediately and publicly, while the Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs consider them recommended based on the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

fqz-030.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ṣawm (hadith of Anas); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-030.q: What do the hadith of the Companions' travels with the Prophet ﷺ show about fasting on a journey?
o: Both fasting and breaking the fast are permitted, and neither group blamed the other
Fasting on a journey is invalid and must be repeated
Breaking the fast on a journey requires an expiation
Only those travelling on foot may break the fast
fqz-030.e: Anas reported in al-Bukhārī and Muslim that on journeys with the Prophet ﷺ some fasted and some did not, and neither criticised the other. The majority therefore hold that the traveller may choose, while differing on which is better in a given situation.

fqz-031.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Zakāt, on gold and silver
fqz-031.q: What is the rate of zakāt on gold, silver and cash savings that reach the niṣāb and complete a year?
fqz-031.e: Zakāt on gold, silver and money is a quarter of a tenth, i.e. one fortieth. Ten and five per cent apply to crops, and one fifth to buried treasure (rikāz).

fqz-032.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Zakāt, on the ḥawl
fqz-032.q: What is the ḥawl in the law of zakāt?
o: The full lunar year that wealth must remain in one's ownership
The minimum amount of wealth on which zakāt is due
The share given to zakāt collectors
The day of harvest for crops
fqz-032.e: The ḥawl is the passing of one lunar year over the niṣāb in one's ownership; it is a condition for money, trade goods and livestock. The minimum amount is the niṣāb, and crops are due at harvest without a ḥawl.

fqz-033.q: How many categories of zakāt recipients does the verse shown list?
fqz-033.e: The verse names eight categories: the poor, the needy, those employed to collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, the freeing of captives, debtors, the cause of Allah and the stranded traveller.

fqz-034.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 9:60; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Ahl al-Zakāt
fqz-034.q: The highlighted word, together with the word after it, names one of the categories of zakāt. Who is meant?
o: A traveller cut off from his wealth
A wealthy merchant on a business trip
A pilgrim who has enough provisions
A guest staying in the payer's house
fqz-034.e: Ibn al-sabīl is the traveller who has run out of means on his journey, even if he is wealthy at home; he receives what brings him to his destination. A traveller with sufficient means is not included.

fqz-035.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Zakāt, on the niṣāb of gold; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-035.q: In the classical units used by the jurists, what is the niṣāb of gold?
fqz-035.e: The jurists state the niṣāb of gold as twenty mithqāls and that of silver as two hundred dirhams (five ūqiyas). Forty is the niṣāb of sheep and five the niṣāb of camels.

fqz-036.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar)
fqz-036.q: According to the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, what is due on crops watered by rain or springs, compared with crops watered with effort and cost?
fqz-036.e: The hadith gives a tenth for land watered by the sky or springs and half a tenth for land irrigated by drawing water. The lower rate reflects the labour and cost of irrigation.

fqz-037.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zakāt (letter of Abū Bakr, hadith of Anas)
fqz-037.q: According to the letter of Abū Bakr in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, what is the niṣāb of sheep and goats and what is due on it?
o: Forty head, on which one sheep is due
Thirty head, on which one sheep is due
Twenty head, on which one sheep is due
Fifty head, on which two sheep are due
fqz-037.e: The letter states that on grazing sheep from forty to one hundred and twenty one sheep is due. Thirty is the niṣāb of cattle, not of sheep.

fqz-038.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zakāt (letter of Abū Bakr, hadith of Anas)
fqz-038.q: What is the niṣāb of camels, and what is due at that number?
o: Five camels, on which one sheep is due
Five camels, on which one young she-camel is due
Ten camels, on which one camel is due
Twenty-five camels, on which one sheep is due
fqz-038.e: From five camels one sheep is due, and one more sheep for every further five up to twenty-four. At twenty-five the due becomes a camel, a bint makhāḍ.

fqz-039.src: Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Muʿādh); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Ṣadaqat al-Baqar
fqz-039.q: According to the hadith of Muʿādh, what is due on thirty head of cattle?
fqz-039.e: Muʿādh was sent to Yemen with the instruction to take a tabīʿ or tabīʿa from every thirty cattle and a musinna from every forty. The musinna is therefore the due on forty, not thirty.

fqz-040.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 6:141; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Zakāt al-Zurūʿ wa-l-Thimār
fqz-040.q: The verse shown commands giving the due of produce on the day of its harvest. What follows for the zakāt of crops?
o: No full year (ḥawl) is required; it is due at harvest
It is due only after a full lunar year
It is due only at the end of Ramaḍān
It is due only if the crop is sold
fqz-040.e: Jurists cite this verse to show that crops and fruits are not subject to the ḥawl: zakāt is due when they are harvested and ripe. The ḥawl applies to money, trade goods and livestock.

fqz-041.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Abū Saʿīd); Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-041.q: According to the majority, based on the hadith of Abū Saʿīd in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, what is the niṣāb of grain and dates?
fqz-041.e: The hadith states that nothing is due on less than five awsuq; a wasq is sixty ṣāʿs, so the niṣāb is three hundred ṣāʿs. Abū Ḥanīfa held that the tithe is due on the land's produce whether little or much.

fqz-042.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of Abū Hurayra)
fqz-042.q: What is due on rikāz (treasure buried in pre-Islamic times) found by someone?
fqz-042.e: The Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith of Abū Hurayra in al-Bukhārī and Muslim that on rikāz the fifth is due. No ḥawl is required, since it comes to the finder without labour over time.

fqz-043.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Ahl al-Zakāt; Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijmāʿ
fqz-043.q: To whom may a person NOT give his own zakāt, by agreement of the scholars?
o: His parents and children whom he is obliged to support
fqz-043.e: One may not give zakāt to one's ascendants and descendants whose maintenance one owes, because the benefit would return to oneself. A poor neighbour, an insolvent debtor and a stranded traveller belong to the eight categories.

fqz-044.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zakāt (hadith of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿa); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-044.q: Which group is excluded from receiving zakāt according to the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that ṣadaqa is not fitting for them?
o: The family of the Prophet ﷺ (Banū Hāshim)
fqz-044.e: The Prophet ﷺ said that ṣadaqa is not fitting for the family of Muḥammad, being the impurities of people's wealth. The majority therefore exclude Banū Hāshim from obligatory zakāt.

fqz-045.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Zakāt; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-045.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about zakāt on gold and silver jewellery worn by a woman in a permissible way?
o: The Ḥanafīs require zakāt on it; the Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs do not
The Mālikīs require zakāt on it; the other three schools do not
All four schools require zakāt on it
No school requires zakāt on it
fqz-045.e: The Ḥanafīs treat gold and silver as zakatable in themselves, whatever their use. The majority liken jewellery in permitted use to personal belongings such as clothes, which are not zakatable; jewellery hoarded or used in a forbidden way remains subject to zakāt.

fqz-046.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Ahl al-Zakāt; al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb Man Yajūz Dafʿ al-Ṣadaqa Ilayh
fqz-046.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about whether the faqīr or the miskīn named in the verse shown is in greater need?
o: Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: the faqīr is worse off; Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs: the miskīn is worse off
