Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs: the faqīr is worse off; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: the miskīn is worse off
All four schools: the two words mean exactly the same
All four schools: the miskīn has wealth above the niṣāb
fqz-046.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs note that the verse begins with the faqīr, and that elsewhere the Quran calls people miskīn who own a ship. The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs define the miskīn as the one who owns nothing at all. Both categories receive zakāt in every school.

fqz-047.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Kitāb Qasm al-Ṣadaqāt; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-047.q: Which school holds that zakāt must be divided among all the categories of the verse shown that are present, rather than given to one category?
fqz-047.e: The Shāfiʿīs read the verse as allocating zakāt to the eight categories jointly, so it must be spread over all those present, at least three persons from each. The Ḥanafīs, Mālikīs and the relied Ḥanbalī view hold that the verse names who is eligible and allow giving all of it to one category.

fqz-048.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Zakāt; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-048.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about zakāt on the wealth of a child or an insane person?
o: The majority make it due, paid by the guardian; the Ḥanafīs do not, except the tithe on crops and Zakāt al-Fiṭr
The Ḥanafīs make it due on all wealth; the majority exempt it entirely
All four schools make it due only after the child reaches puberty, for all past years
All four schools exempt all their wealth, including crops
fqz-048.e: The majority view zakāt as a right attached to the wealth itself, so the guardian pays it. The Ḥanafīs view it as an act of worship requiring legal capacity, so they exempt the money and livestock of a child, while still requiring the tithe on crops and Zakāt al-Fiṭr.

fqz-049.src: Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Zakāt; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Zakāt
fqz-049.q: Which school does NOT make free grazing (sawm) a condition for zakāt on livestock, and so requires it also on fodder-fed and working animals?
fqz-049.e: Khalīl states that zakāt is due on livestock even if fed with fodder or used for work, following the general texts on camels, cattle and sheep. The other three schools restrict it to animals that graze freely for most of the year, because the hadith qualifies sheep as grazing (sāʾima).

fqz-050.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Zakāt, on the niṣāb of gold; modern conversions of the mithqāl
fqz-050.q: Modern writers commonly convert the gold niṣāb of twenty mithqāls into roughly how many grams of gold?
fqz-050.e: Taking a mithqāl as roughly 4.25 grams gives about 85 grams; conversions differ slightly with the estimate of the mithqāl. About 595 grams is the commonly cited conversion for the silver niṣāb of two hundred dirhams.

fqz-051.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Zakāt (letter of Abū Bakr, hadith of Anas)
fqz-051.q: A herd of 130 freely grazing sheep completes the year. How many sheep are due?
fqz-051.e: According to the letter of Abū Bakr, one sheep is due from forty to one hundred and twenty, two from one hundred and twenty-one to two hundred, and three from two hundred and one to three hundred. 130 therefore falls into the bracket of two.

fqz-052.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb Man Yajūz Dafʿ al-Ṣadaqa Ilayh; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-052.q: The highlighted word begins the category of those whose hearts are to be reconciled. Which school holds that this share has lapsed?
o: The Mālikī school according to Khalīl
fqz-052.e: The Ḥanafīs hold that the share lapsed because Islam became strong, citing ʿUmar's refusal to continue the payments in the time of Abū Bakr without objection from the Companions. The Ḥanbalīs keep the share when there is need, and Khalīl states that its ruling remains.

fqz-053.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb Zakāt al-Zurūʿ wa-l-Thimār
fqz-053.q: On the tithe of agricultural produce, how did Abū Ḥanīfa differ from his two companions Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad?
o: He required it on little and much of almost all produce; they required a niṣāb of five awsuq and produce that keeps
He required a niṣāb of five awsuq; they required it on little and much
He limited it to wheat and barley; they extended it to all produce
He required a full year after harvest; they required it at harvest
fqz-053.e: Al-Hidāya reports that Abū Ḥanīfa required the tithe on whatever the land produces, little or much, except things like firewood, reeds and grass, while Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad required five awsuq and limited it to produce that lasts a year, in line with the hadith of Abū Saʿīd.

fqz-054.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Bāb Zakāt al-Nabāt
fqz-054.q: According to the Shāfiʿī school as stated in Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, which produce is subject to the tithe?
o: Staple foods eaten by choice, such as wheat, barley, rice and lentils, plus dates and grapes
Everything the land produces except firewood, grass and reeds
Only wheat, barley, dates and raisins, as named in some reports
All fruits and vegetables that are sold at market
fqz-054.e: Al-Nawawī restricts the zakāt of plants to staples (qūt) eaten in normal circumstances, and among fruits to fresh dates and grapes. The second option is Abū Ḥanīfa's view, and the third is a view reported from some early authorities.

fqz-055.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Zakāt; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, on the conditions of zakāt
fqz-055.q: Which of the following is a condition for zakāt to be due on money according to the jurists?
o: Complete ownership of a niṣāb for a full year
That the owner has performed the ḥajj
That the money is held in a bank account
That the owner has no living parents
fqz-055.e: The conditions commonly listed are Islam, freedom, complete ownership (milk tāmm) of a niṣāb and the passing of a ḥawl on money, livestock and trade goods. The other options have no basis in the law of zakāt.

fqz-056.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Abū Hurayra); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj
fqz-056.q: Based on the verse shown and the Sunna, how often is ḥajj obligatory?
o: Once in a lifetime, for whoever is able
Every year, for every adult Muslim
Once every five years, for whoever is able
Once in a lifetime, for everyone whether able or not
fqz-056.e: The verse makes ḥajj a duty on whoever is able to find a way to it. When asked whether it is every year, the Prophet ﷺ indicated that it is not (hadith of Abū Hurayra in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim); by consensus it is obligatory once in a lifetime.

fqz-057.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on the standing at ʿArafa
fqz-057.q: On which day do the pilgrims stand at ʿArafa?
fqz-057.e: The Day of ʿArafa is the 9th of Dhū al-Ḥijja. The 8th is the Day of Tarwiya, when pilgrims go to Minā, and the 10th is the Day of Sacrifice.

fqz-058.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-058.q: How is ṭawāf around the Kaʿba performed?
o: Seven circuits, starting at the Black Stone, with the Kaʿba on one's left
Seven circuits, starting at the Yemeni corner, with the Kaʿba on one's right
Three circuits, starting at the door of the Kaʿba
Five circuits, starting at the Station of Ibrāhīm
fqz-058.e: Ṭawāf consists of seven circuits that begin and end at the Black Stone, moving with the Kaʿba on one's left, as in the description of the Prophet's ḥajj by Jābir in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

fqz-059.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir); Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:158
fqz-059.q: The highlighted word names a hill of the saʿy. What is its role?
o: The saʿy ends at it after the seventh lap
fqz-059.e: In Jābir's hadith the Prophet ﷺ approached al-Ṣafā and said he would begin with what Allah began with, then started the saʿy from it. Each passage between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa counts as one lap, so the seventh lap ends at al-Marwa.

fqz-060.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās on the mawāqīt)
fqz-060.q: Which mīqāt did the Prophet ﷺ appoint for the people of Medina?
fqz-060.e: In the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās the Prophet ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfa for Medina, al-Juḥfa for al-Shām, Qarn al-Manāzil for Najd and Yalamlam for Yemen.

fqz-061.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-061.q: On the Day of Sacrifice (10th Dhū al-Ḥijja), at which pillar do the pilgrims throw pebbles?
o: Only Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, with seven pebbles
All three jamarāt, seven pebbles each
Only the small jamra, with seven pebbles
Only Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, with three pebbles
fqz-061.e: On the 10th the Prophet ﷺ threw only at Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, seven pebbles, saying takbīr with each. All three jamarāt are stoned on the days of tashrīq that follow.

fqz-062.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar on what the muḥrim wears)
fqz-062.q: Which of the following is forbidden for a man in the state of iḥrām?
fqz-062.e: The Prophet ﷺ named shirts, turbans, trousers, hooded cloaks and leather socks as garments the muḥrim does not wear. The man wears a waist wrap and an upper wrap, and sandals and washing are permitted.

fqz-063.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on the three types; al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn
fqz-063.q: What is the name of the type of ḥajj in which the pilgrim enters iḥrām for ʿumra and ḥajj together and stays in iḥrām until the Day of Sacrifice?
fqz-063.e: Qirān joins ʿumra and ḥajj in one iḥrām. In tamattuʿ the pilgrim completes ʿumra, leaves iḥrām and then enters it again for ḥajj; in ifrād he enters iḥrām for ḥajj alone. Iḥṣār is being prevented from completing the rites.

fqz-064.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on tamattuʿ
fqz-064.q: Which description fits tamattuʿ, mentioned in the verse shown?
o: ʿUmra in the months of ḥajj, leaving iḥrām, then ḥajj in the same year
ʿUmra after the ḥajj, in the month of Muḥarram
ʿUmra and ḥajj together in one iḥrām
fqz-064.e: Tamattuʿ means performing ʿumra in the months of ḥajj, enjoying the release from iḥrām, then entering iḥrām for ḥajj in the same year. The verse makes a sacrificial animal due for it from those who are not residents of the Sacred Mosque.

fqz-065.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:196; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-065.q: According to the verse shown, what must a pilgrim on tamattuʿ do if he cannot find a sacrificial animal?
o: Fast three days during the ḥajj and seven after returning
Fast ten days before entering iḥrām
fqz-065.e: The verse prescribes three days of fasting during the ḥajj and seven upon return, ten complete days, for the one who finds no hady.

fqz-066.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās on the mawāqīt)
fqz-066.q: Which mīqāt did the Prophet ﷺ appoint for the people of Yemen?
fqz-066.e: Yalamlam is the mīqāt of the people of Yemen in the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās. Qarn al-Manāzil is for Najd, Dhū al-Ḥulayfa for Medina and al-Juḥfa for al-Shām.

fqz-067.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, bāb Dhāt ʿIrq li-ahl al-ʿIrāq
fqz-067.q: According to a report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, who designated Dhāt ʿIrq as the mīqāt for the people of Iraq?
fqz-067.e: Al-Bukhārī reports from Ibn ʿUmar that when Basra and Kufa were founded, their people came to ʿUmar, who fixed Dhāt ʿIrq for them as level with Qarn al-Manāzil. A report in Muslim attributes it to the Prophet ﷺ with the narrator expressing doubt.

fqz-068.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-068.q: What do the pilgrims do with the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers on the night they reach Muzdalifa?
o: They combine them at Muzdalifa in the time of ʿIshāʾ
They pray Maghrib at ʿArafa and ʿIshāʾ at Muzdalifa
They combine them at ʿArafa before leaving
They pray each in its own time at Minā
fqz-068.e: Following the Sunna, the pilgrims delay Maghrib and pray it with ʿIshāʾ upon reaching Muzdalifa, as Jābir describes the Prophet ﷺ doing.

fqz-069.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Jazāʾ al-Ṣayd (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar)
fqz-069.q: Which two items does the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī forbid to a woman in iḥrām?
fqz-069.e: The hadith states that the woman in iḥrām does not wear the niqāb or gloves. Unlike a man, she may wear stitched clothing, cover her head and wear shoes.

fqz-070.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra); Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:196
fqz-070.q: A pilgrim in iḥrām shaves his head because of an ailment. According to the verse shown and the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, what is due?
o: A choice between fasting three days, feeding six poor people, or sacrificing a sheep
Only a sheep, with no alternative
Nothing, since he had an excuse
fqz-070.e: The verse gives the options of fasting, charity or a sacrifice, and the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra explains them as three days of fasting, feeding six poor people (half a ṣāʿ each) or one sheep. The pilgrim may choose, because the excuse lifts the sin but not the compensation.

fqz-071.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 5:95; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Bāb Jazāʾ al-Ṣayd
fqz-071.q: What does the verse shown forbid to those in the state of iḥrām?
o: Eating meat bought in the market
fqz-071.e: The verse forbids killing game while in iḥrām and sets a compensation for doing so deliberately. Sea game is permitted to the muḥrim by a following verse, and slaughtering domestic livestock is not hunting.

fqz-072.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās); Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijmāʿ
fqz-072.q: A child performs ḥajj with his parents and later reaches puberty. What is the ruling?
o: His ḥajj was valid and rewarded, but he must perform the obligatory ḥajj after puberty
His ḥajj was invalid and brings no reward
His ḥajj fulfils the obligation, so he owes no further ḥajj
His parents must perform a second ḥajj on his behalf
fqz-072.e: When a woman lifted up a child and asked whether he had a ḥajj, the Prophet ﷺ said yes, and that she would have a reward (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim). The scholars agree that it does not replace the obligatory ḥajj, which becomes due once he is adult and able.

fqz-073.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on the first taḥallul
fqz-073.q: After the first release from iḥrām (al-taḥallul al-awwal) on the Day of Sacrifice, what remains forbidden by agreement until ṭawāf al-ifāḍa?
fqz-073.e: After the first release the pilgrim may wear ordinary clothes and cut hair and nails, but the scholars agree that marital intercourse remains forbidden until the second release, which comes with ṭawāf al-ifāḍa.

fqz-074.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar on ramal); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-074.q: What is ramal, and in which circuits of the ṭawāf of arrival or ʿumra is it performed?
o: Brisk walking with short steps, in the first three circuits, for men
Running at full speed, in all seven circuits, for men and women
Walking slowly, in the last three circuits, for men
Uncovering the right shoulder, in the last four circuits, for men
fqz-074.e: Ramal is a brisk walk with short steps, done by men in the first three circuits of a ṭawāf followed by saʿy, as Ibn ʿUmar described. Uncovering the right shoulder is a different sunna, iḍṭibāʿ.

fqz-075.src: Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah, Kitāb al-Manāsik (hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmar)
fqz-075.q: The highlighted word names the place of the central rite of ḥajj. Which short prophetic statement expresses its importance?
fqz-075.e: The hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmar, reported in the Sunan, states that ḥajj is ʿArafa: whoever misses the standing there has missed the ḥajj. All schools treat it as a pillar that cannot be repaired by a sacrifice.

fqz-076.src: al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 2:198; Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir)
fqz-076.q: The highlighted word, with the one after it, names a landmark where Allah is remembered after leaving ʿArafa. In which station of ḥajj does it lie?
fqz-076.e: Al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is in Muzdalifa; in Jābir's hadith the Prophet ﷺ came to it after the dawn prayer and remained in supplication until it was very bright. Some scholars use the name for the whole of Muzdalifa.

fqz-077.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:203; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, on the early departure
fqz-077.q: The verse shown allows hastening in two days. According to the majority, what does this mean for the pilgrim at Minā?
o: He may leave Minā on the 12th after stoning, if he leaves before sunset
He may skip the stoning on the 11th and 12th
He may leave Minā on the 10th after the sacrifice
He may leave on the 13th without stoning that day
fqz-077.e: The two days are the 11th and 12th of Dhū al-Ḥijja. Whoever stones on both and leaves Minā before sunset on the 12th is free of the third day; if the sun sets while he is still there, the majority require him to stay and stone on the 13th.

fqz-078.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, how many pillars (arkān) does ḥajj have, and what are they?
o: Two: the standing at ʿArafa and ṭawāf al-ziyāra
Four: iḥrām, the standing, ṭawāf and saʿy
Five: iḥrām, the standing, ṭawāf, saʿy and shaving
Three: iḥrām, the standing and ṭawāf
fqz-078.e: The Ḥanafīs count only the standing at ʿArafa and (most of) ṭawāf al-ziyāra as pillars; iḥrām is a condition and saʿy a wājib. The Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs count four, and al-Nawawī's Minhāj counts five including shaving.

fqz-079.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ḥajj; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, on the saʿy
fqz-079.q: Which school regards the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa as a wājib, whose omission is repaired by a sacrifice, rather than a pillar?
fqz-079.e: The Ḥanafīs argue that the verse on al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa only lifts blame, which does not establish a pillar, so they rank saʿy as wājib with a sacrifice for omitting it. The Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and the relied Ḥanbalī view make it a pillar without which ḥajj is incomplete.

fqz-080.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ḥajj; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-080.q: Which statement correctly describes the schools' preference among the three types of ḥajj?
o: Ḥanafīs prefer qirān, Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs ifrād, Ḥanbalīs tamattuʿ
Ḥanafīs prefer tamattuʿ, Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs qirān, Ḥanbalīs ifrād
Ḥanafīs prefer ifrād, Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs tamattuʿ, Ḥanbalīs qirān
fqz-080.e: The disagreement goes back to the reports about how the Prophet ﷺ performed his ḥajj. The Ḥanafīs prefer qirān, the Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs ifrād (for the Shāfiʿīs when ʿumra is done the same year), and the Ḥanbalīs tamattuʿ, citing the Prophet's wish to have done it.

fqz-081.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on the ʿumra; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-081.q: What is the ruling of ʿumra once in a lifetime according to the schools?
o: Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: obligatory; Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs: an emphasised sunna
Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs: obligatory; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs: an emphasised sunna
All four schools: obligatory every year
fqz-081.e: The Shāfiʿīs (in the more evident view) and Ḥanbalīs make ʿumra obligatory once, arguing from the command to complete ḥajj and ʿumra. The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs hold it to be an emphasised sunna, since the verse obliging ḥajj on those able does not mention it.

fqz-082.src: al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās); Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-082.q: A woman's menstruation begins after she has performed ṭawāf al-ifāḍa, and her group is leaving Makka. What does the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās say about the farewell ṭawāf?
o: She is excused from it and may leave without it
She must wait in Makka until she is pure
She must offer a sacrifice in its place
fqz-082.e: Ibn ʿAbbās reported that people were commanded to make their last act at the House, except that it was lightened for the menstruating woman. The Prophet ﷺ also allowed Ṣafiyya to depart once he learned she had already done ṭawāf al-ifāḍa.

fqz-083.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ḥajj; Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar; al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn
fqz-083.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about a woman travelling for her obligatory ḥajj without a maḥram?
o: Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs accept trustworthy company in its place; Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs require a maḥram or husband
Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs accept trustworthy company; Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs require a maḥram
All four schools accept travelling entirely alone
All four schools forbid her ḥajj in every case
fqz-083.e: The Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs make a maḥram or husband part of her ability (istiṭāʿa), following the hadith forbidding a woman to travel without a maḥram. The Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs allow her, for the obligatory ḥajj, to travel with a safe and trustworthy group, such as reliable women.

fqz-084.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Ibn ʿUmar); Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ (hadith of Jābir on the time of stoning)
fqz-084.q: On the days of tashrīq, in what order and from what time are the three jamarāt stoned according to the Sunna?
o: The small, then the middle, then Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, after the sun passes the meridian
Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, then the middle, then the small, after dawn
The middle, then the small, then Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, after sunrise
The small, then Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, then the middle, after ʿAṣr
fqz-084.e: Ibn ʿUmar described stoning the jamra nearest the mosque of al-Khayf first, then the middle one, then Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, standing in supplication after the first two, and attributed this to the Prophet ﷺ. Jābir reported that on these days the Prophet ﷺ stoned after the sun had declined.

fqz-085.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ḥajj; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:197
fqz-085.q: The verse shown speaks of the known months of ḥajj. Which school counts the whole of Dhū al-Ḥijja among them, rather than only its first ten days?
fqz-085.e: All agree that Shawwāl and Dhū al-Qaʿda are months of ḥajj. The Mālikīs include the whole of Dhū al-Ḥijja, taking the plural literally, while the Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs count its first ten days and the Shāfiʿīs its first ten nights up to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice.

fqz-086.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj (hadith of Jābir on sharing); Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-086.q: According to the majority, based on the hadith of Jābir in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, how many people may share one camel or one cow as hady?
fqz-086.e: Jābir reported that at al-Ḥudaybiya they sacrificed a camel for seven and a cow for seven. The majority therefore allow a seventh of a camel or cow to replace a sheep, while Mālik did not permit sharing in an obligatory hady.

fqz-087.src: Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ḥajj; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-087.q: In the Mālikī school, which part of the standing at ʿArafa is the pillar, and what is the status of the daytime standing?
o: Presence at ʿArafa for a moment of the night before the Day of Sacrifice is the pillar; the daytime standing is wājib
The daytime standing after the meridian is the pillar; the night standing is a sunna
Both day and night together form the pillar, neither alone suffices
Standing from the dawn of the 9th is the pillar; the night is not counted
fqz-087.e: Khalīl defines the pillar as being present at ʿArafa for a moment on the night of the Day of Sacrifice, following the Prophet's practice of leaving only after sunset; the daytime standing is wājib and its omission is repaired by a sacrifice. For the majority, standing at any time between the 9th (from the meridian, or from dawn for the Ḥanbalīs) and the dawn of the 10th suffices.

fqz-088.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb al-Jināyāt; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, on intercourse in iḥrām
fqz-088.q: A pilgrim has intercourse with his wife after the standing at ʿArafa but before any release from iḥrām. Which statement correctly describes the disagreement?
o: Ḥanafīs: the ḥajj is not invalidated but a camel (badana) is due; the majority: the ḥajj is invalidated
Ḥanafīs: the ḥajj is invalidated; the majority: only a sheep is due
All schools: the ḥajj is valid and nothing is due
All schools: the ḥajj is valid and only fasting is due
fqz-088.e: Al-Hidāya holds that intercourse after the standing does not invalidate the ḥajj, since its main pillar is already done, but requires a badana. The Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs hold that intercourse before the first release invalidates the ḥajj, which must still be completed and made up, with a badana due.

fqz-089.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ḥajj and Bāb al-Jināyāt; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-089.q: How does the Ḥanafī school classify ritual purity (ṭahāra) for ṭawāf, in contrast to the majority?
o: As a wājib: ṭawāf without it is valid but requires a sacrifice or repetition
As a condition: ṭawāf without it is void
As merely recommended, with no consequence
As a condition for men only
fqz-089.e: The majority make purity a condition of ṭawāf, likening it to prayer. The Ḥanafīs make it wājib: the ṭawāf counts, but a sheep is due (a badana for ṭawāf al-ziyāra in major impurity) unless it is repeated in purity.

fqz-090.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Bāb al-Jināyāt fī al-Ṣayd; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-090.q: The verse shown sets a compensation, judged by two just men, for game killed in iḥrām. How did Abū Ḥanīfa understand it, in contrast to the majority?
o: As the value of the game, which may then be spent on a sacrifice, food or fasting
As a livestock animal resembling the game in form
As a fixed sum of money set by the ruler
As fasting only, with no sacrifice
fqz-090.e: The majority, following the Companions' judgements, require a livestock animal resembling the game (mithl), e.g. a camel for an ostrich. Abū Ḥanīfa understood the equivalent as the value assessed by two just men, with which a sacrifice is bought or food given, or the person fasts in its place.

fqz-091.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Nikāḥ (hadith of ʿUthmān); al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Nikāḥ; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid
fqz-091.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about a marriage contract concluded by a person in iḥrām?
o: The majority hold it invalid, citing the hadith of ʿUthmān in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Ḥanafīs hold it valid, citing Ibn ʿAbbās's report about Maymūna
The Ḥanafīs hold it invalid; the majority hold it valid but disliked
All four schools hold it valid without dislike
All four schools hold it valid only if the bride is not in iḥrām
fqz-091.e: The hadith of ʿUthmān states that the muḥrim neither marries nor is given in marriage, so the Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs void such a contract. The Ḥanafīs rely on Ibn ʿAbbās's report that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūna while in iḥrām, which others answer with Maymūna's own report that he married her out of iḥrām.

fqz-092.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, on ending the talbiya; Khalīl, al-Mukhtaṣar, Bāb al-Ḥajj
fqz-092.q: According to the Ḥanafīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs, when does the pilgrim on ḥajj stop reciting the talbiya?
o: When he begins stoning Jamrat al-ʿAqaba on the Day of Sacrifice
When he reaches the boundary of the Ḥaram
When he arrives at ʿArafa on the morning of the 9th
fqz-092.e: They follow the report of al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ continued the talbiya until he stoned Jamrat al-ʿAqaba. The Mālikī school ends it earlier, when the pilgrim sets out for the place of prayer at ʿArafa after the sun passes the meridian; the talbiya of ʿumra ends on reaching the Ḥaram or starting ṭawāf, depending on the school.

fqz-093.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Bāb Arkān al-Ḥajj wa-l-ʿUmra
fqz-093.q: Al-Nawawī's Minhāj lists five pillars of ḥajj. Which one appears there that the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs do not count as a pillar?
o: Shaving or shortening the hair, on the view that it is a rite
fqz-093.e: The Minhāj names iḥrām, the standing, ṭawāf, saʿy and shaving, the last on the view that shaving is a rite (nusuk) and not merely a permission. These pillars cannot be replaced by a sacrifice. The Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs count shaving among the wājibāt, and stoning and staying at Muzdalifa are wājibāt in all of these schools.

fqz-094.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Bāb al-Mawāqīt; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī
fqz-094.q: Someone enters iḥrām for ḥajj in Ramaḍān, before the months of ḥajj. What is the position of the Shāfiʿī school?
o: The iḥrām does not count for ḥajj but turns into an iḥrām for ʿumra
The iḥrām for ḥajj is valid but disliked
The iḥrām is void and he leaves it without any rite
The iḥrām is valid and he must perform qirān
fqz-094.e: Al-Nawawī states that iḥrām for ḥajj outside its time is not valid as ḥajj but takes effect as ʿumra, on the sound view, because the time of ḥajj is like the time of prayer. The Ḥanafīs, Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs hold that it is valid for ḥajj though disliked.

fqs-001.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, bāb al-miyāh
fqs-001.q: What is water called that is pure in itself and can also purify other things, for example for wuḍūʾ?
fqs-001.e: Ṭahūr water is pure and purifying, so it lifts ritual impurity and removes najāsa. Water that is only ṭāhir is pure but cannot be used for wuḍūʾ, and najis water is impure.

fqs-002.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, nawāqiḍ al-wuḍūʾ
fqs-002.q: Which of the following breaks wuḍūʾ by agreement of all the schools?
fqs-002.e: Anything exiting from the front or back passage, including wind, nullifies wuḍūʾ by consensus. Touching a spouse and bleeding are matters of disagreement, and eating cooked food does not break wuḍūʾ according to the schools.

fqs-003.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on repeating the washing
fqs-003.q: In wuḍūʾ, how many times must each limb be washed, and what is the sunna?
o: Once is obligatory, three times is sunna
Three times is obligatory, five is sunna
Twice is obligatory, three is sunna
Once is obligatory, seven times is sunna
fqs-003.e: Washing each limb once fulfils the obligation; the Prophet ﷺ also washed twice and three times, and three is the sunna. Going beyond three is disliked.

fqs-004.q: Which parts of the body does the verse shown name for wuḍūʾ?
fqs-004.e: The verse orders washing the face, the arms up to the elbows and the feet up to the ankles, and wiping the head. Rinsing the mouth, the ears and the neck are not named in it.

fqs-005.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ghusl
fqs-005.q: Which of the following makes ghusl obligatory by agreement of the schools?
fqs-005.e: The end of ḥayḍ obliges a woman to perform ghusl by consensus. Ghusl for Jumuʿa and ʿĪd is sunna according to the majority, and ghusl after washing a corpse is recommended.

fqs-006.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥayḍ, hadith of ʿĀʾisha on making up fasts
fqs-006.q: What must a woman make up after her menstruation ends?
o: The missed fasts, but not the prayers
The missed prayers, but not the fasts
Both the prayers and the fasts
Neither the prayers nor the fasts
fqs-006.e: According to the report of ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, women were told to make up the fasts but not the prayers. This is agreed upon, and it spares her a heavy burden since prayers recur daily.

fqs-007.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, hadith of ʿAlī on the duration of wiping
fqs-007.q: According to the majority of scholars, for how long may a traveller wipe over leather socks (khuffayn)?
fqs-007.e: In the hadith of ʿAlī in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ set three days and nights for the traveller and one day and night for the resident. The Ḥanafī, Shāfiʿī and Ḥanbalī schools follow this; the well-known Mālikī view sets no fixed limit.

fqs-008.src: Abū Dāwūd, Sunan, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, report of ʿAlī on wiping the top of the khuff
fqs-008.q: Which part of the khuff is wiped in masḥ?
o: The top of the foot covering
fqs-008.e: Masḥ is done on the top of the khuff, as ʿAlī reported, noting that reason alone would have suggested the underside. The obligatory part is the top; the schools do not require wiping the sole.

fqs-009.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, bāb al-istinjāʾ
o: Cleaning after relieving oneself with stones or similar
Washing the private parts with water only
fqs-009.e: Istijmār is cleaning the exit with stones or other suitable dry, pure material; istinjāʾ with water is the other method. Combining both is best.

fqs-010.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra min al-najas
fqs-010.q: Which of these is impure (najis) by agreement of the scholars?
fqs-010.e: Human urine and faeces are najis by consensus. Sweat, saliva and tears of a living human are pure.

fqs-011.q: According to the verse shown, when is tayammum (dry purification) allowed?
o: When water is not found or cannot be used
Only on the day of Jumuʿa
Whenever one is in a hurry
fqs-011.e: The verse permits tayammum for the sick and the traveller and whoever finds no water. Lack of water or inability to use it (illness, harm) is the basis; haste or mere discomfort is not.

fqs-012.q: Someone who performed tayammum because no water was available later finds water before praying. What is the ruling?
o: His tayammum is void; he must use the water
He may pray with his tayammum anyway
He must perform both wuḍūʾ and tayammum
He waits until the next prayer time
fqs-012.e: Tayammum is a substitute that ends once water can be used. Finding water before starting the prayer voids it by agreement.

fqs-013.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, hadith of the Night Journey
fqs-013.q: How many obligatory prayers are there in a day and night?
fqs-013.e: Five prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Miʿrāj: Fajr, Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ. This is known by necessity in the religion.

fqs-014.q: How many rakʿas does the Maghrib prayer have?
fqs-014.e: Maghrib has three rakʿas, both at home and on a journey; it is never shortened.

fqs-015.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Masājid, hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr on the prayer times
fqs-015.q: When does the time of Ẓuhr begin?
o: When the sun passes its zenith
When the shadow equals the object
fqs-015.e: Ẓuhr begins at zawāl, when the sun has passed the middle of the sky. The shadow equalling the object marks the start of ʿAṣr according to the majority.

fqs-016.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, waqt al-ṣubḥ
fqs-016.q: With which dawn does the time of Fajr begin?
o: The true dawn spreading across the horizon
The last third of the night
fqs-016.e: Fajr begins with the true dawn (al-fajr al-ṣādiq), the light spreading along the horizon. The earlier vertical glow, the false dawn, has no ruling for prayer or fasting.

fqs-017.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb shurūṭ al-ṣalāt
fqs-017.q: Which of these is a condition (sharṭ) of the prayer rather than a pillar inside it?
fqs-017.e: Conditions must exist before and throughout the prayer: purity, covering the ʿawra, the time having entered, and facing the qibla. Rukūʿ, sujūd and recitation are acts within the prayer.

fqs-018.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, on the institution of the adhān
fqs-018.q: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ first and best-known muʾadhdhin in Medina?
fqs-018.e: Bilāl was the first to call the adhān in Medina. Ibn Umm Maktūm also called, especially for Fajr; Abū Maḥdhūra was muʾadhdhin in Mecca and Saʿd al-Qaraẓ at Qubāʾ.

fqs-019.src: Abū Dāwūd, Sunan, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb kayfa al-adhān
fqs-019.q: Which phrase is added in the adhān of Fajr only?
fqs-019.e: In the Fajr adhān, 'prayer is better than sleep' is said twice after ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥ (al-tathwīb). Qad qāmati al-ṣalāh belongs to the iqāma, and the other phrases are in every adhān.

fqs-020.src: Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijmāʿ, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, ṣalāt al-musāfir
fqs-020.q: Which prayers may be shortened (qaṣr) on a journey?
fqs-020.e: Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr and ʿIshāʾ are shortened from four to two rakʿas. Fajr and Maghrib are never shortened, by consensus.

fqs-021.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Adhān, hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās praying with the Prophet ﷺ at night
fqs-021.q: Where does a single male follower stand when praying behind an imam?
fqs-021.e: Ibn ʿAbbās stood at the Prophet's ﷺ left and was moved to his right. The schools therefore hold that one male follower stands at the imam's right.

fqs-022.q: How many rakʿas is the Friday prayer (Jumuʿa)?
fqs-022.e: Jumuʿa is two rakʿas, preceded by two sermons, and it takes the place of Ẓuhr for those who pray it.

fqs-023.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Jumuʿa, on who is obliged
fqs-023.q: On whom is the Friday prayer not obligatory according to the four schools?
o: A man living near the mosque
fqs-023.e: Jumuʿa is obligatory on the free, adult, sane, resident male without an excuse. A traveller is not obliged, though his Jumuʿa is valid if he attends, and it replaces his Ẓuhr.

fqs-024.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz
fqs-024.q: Which of these is not part of the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāza)?
fqs-024.e: The funeral prayer is performed standing with takbīrs and supplications; it has no rukūʿ and no sujūd.

fqs-025.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, number of takbīrs
fqs-025.q: How many takbīrs does the funeral prayer have according to the four schools?
fqs-025.e: The four schools hold that the funeral prayer has four takbīrs. Some Companions are reported to have said five, but the practice settled on four.

fqs-026.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, how many obligatory acts (farāʾiḍ) does wuḍūʾ have?
fqs-026.e: For the Ḥanafīs the farāʾiḍ are exactly the four acts in the verse: washing the face, the arms with the elbows, the feet with the ankles, and wiping a quarter of the head. Intention, order and continuity are sunna for them.

fqs-027.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, bāb al-wuḍūʾ
fqs-027.q: According to the Shāfiʿī school, which two acts are added to the four of the verse to make six farāʾiḍ of wuḍūʾ?
fqs-027.e: Al-Nawawī lists six: intention, face, arms, wiping part of the head, feet, and tartīb. Rubbing (dalk) and continuity are obligatory for the Mālikīs, and rinsing mouth and nose is sunna for the Shāfiʿīs.

fqs-028.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, farāʾiḍ al-wuḍūʾ
fqs-028.q: Which act is an obligatory part of wuḍūʾ in the Mālikī school but not in the other three?
fqs-028.e: Khalīl lists seven farāʾiḍ, including dalk, passing the hand over the washed limb, and fawr (continuity). Dalk is not obligatory in wuḍūʾ for the Ḥanafīs, Shāfiʿīs or Ḥanbalīs.

fqs-029.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on the amount of the head to be wiped
fqs-029.q: The schools differ on how much of the head must be wiped, partly over the highlighted word. Which school holds that wiping any small part of the head suffices?
fqs-029.e: The Shāfiʿīs require only what can be called wiping, even a few hairs within the head. The Ḥanafīs require a quarter, and the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs (in their relied-upon views) the whole head.

fqs-030.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ṭahārāt, sunan al-wuḍūʾ
fqs-030.q: Which school holds that intention (niyya) is a sunna of wuḍūʾ and not a condition of its validity?
fqs-030.e: The Ḥanafīs regard water as purifying by its nature, so wuḍūʾ without intention lifts the ḥadath, though without reward. The other three schools make intention obligatory for wuḍūʾ.

fqs-031.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on order in wuḍūʾ
fqs-031.q: Which pair of schools holds that keeping the order of the limbs (tartīb) is obligatory in wuḍūʾ?
fqs-031.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs make tartīb a farḍ, following the order of the verse. For the Ḥanafīs and in the well-known Mālikī view it is a sunna.

fqs-032.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, bāb asbāb al-ḥadath
fqs-032.q: The highlighted word is central to a disagreement. Which school holds that skin contact between an adult man and a non-maḥram woman breaks wuḍūʾ even without desire?
fqs-032.e: The Shāfiʿīs read the 'touching' in the verse literally, so direct skin contact breaks wuḍūʾ. The Ḥanafīs understand it as intercourse; the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs (relied-upon view) make it break wuḍūʾ only with desire.

fqs-033.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on what exits from other than the two passages
fqs-033.q: Which pair of schools holds that blood flowing from a wound does not break wuḍūʾ, whatever its amount?
fqs-033.e: For the Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs, only what exits from the two passages (and a few named causes) breaks wuḍūʾ. The Ḥanafīs count flowing blood as a nullifier, and the Ḥanbalīs a large, offensive amount.

fqs-034.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on eating camel meat
fqs-034.q: Which school holds that eating camel meat breaks wuḍūʾ?
fqs-034.e: The Ḥanbalīs act on the hadith of Jābir ibn Samura in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim ordering wuḍūʾ after camel meat. The other three schools understand it as abrogated or as recommendation.

fqs-035.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥayḍ, on ghusl when the two circumcised parts meet
fqs-035.q: According to the four schools, does intercourse without ejaculation require ghusl?
o: Only if it happens at night
fqs-035.e: The hadith that ghusl is due when the two circumcised parts meet, even without emission, is acted upon by the four schools. The early view 'water only from water' is held to be abrogated.

fqs-036.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ghusl, hadith of ʿAlī on madhy
fqs-036.q: What does the emission of madhy (pre-seminal fluid) require?
o: Wuḍūʾ and washing the area, not ghusl
Ghusl, like the emission of semen
Nothing at all, since it is pure
fqs-036.e: In the hadith of ʿAlī the Prophet ﷺ ordered washing the private part and performing wuḍūʾ for madhy. It is impure and breaks wuḍūʾ, but does not oblige ghusl.

fqs-037.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Tayammum, on the limbs and the strikes
fqs-037.q: Which pair of schools holds that tayammum obligatorily needs two strikes, with the arms wiped up to the elbows?
fqs-037.e: The Ḥanafīs and Shāfiʿīs require one strike for the face and one for the arms to the elbows. The Ḥanbalīs hold one strike for face and hands to the wrists; the Mālikīs make the wrists obligatory and the elbows and second strike sunna.

fqs-038.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ṭahārāt, bāb al-anjās wa-taṭhīrihā
fqs-038.q: Into which two main classes does Ḥanafī fiqh divide najāsa for the amount that is excused?
fqs-038.e: The Ḥanafīs divide najāsa into mughallaẓa, excused up to the size of a dirham, and mukhaffafa, excused if less than a quarter of the garment or limb. Visible and invisible matter for how it is washed, not for this classification.

fqs-039.src: Abū Dāwūd, Sunan, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb kayfa al-adhān
fqs-039.q: Which Companion saw the words of the adhān in a dream, which the Prophet ﷺ then approved?
fqs-039.e: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih saw the adhān in a dream; the Prophet ﷺ called it a true vision and had him teach it to Bilāl, who had the stronger voice. ʿUmar reported a similar dream.

fqs-040.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb al-mawāqīt
fqs-040.q: According to the view of Abū Ḥanīfa, when does the time of ʿAṣr begin?
o: When an object's shadow becomes twice its length
When the shadow equals the object's length
fqs-040.e: Abū Ḥanīfa held that Ẓuhr lasts until the shadow is twice the object (besides the zenith shadow). The majority, including his two companions, start ʿAṣr when the shadow equals the object.

fqs-041.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Mawāqīt al-Ṣalāt, on not praying after ʿAṣr
fqs-041.q: Which of these is a time in which voluntary prayer without a particular cause is prohibited according to the four schools?
o: After the ʿAṣr prayer until sunset
fqs-041.e: The hadith forbids prayer after ʿAṣr until sunset and after Fajr until sunrise, as well as at sunrise, zenith and sunset. The schools differ about prayers that have a cause, but not about this basic time.

fqs-042.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb ṣalāt al-witr
fqs-042.q: Who held that the witr prayer is wājib, a level between farḍ and sunna?
fqs-042.e: Abū Ḥanīfa considered witr wājib; his two companions and the other three schools hold it to be an emphasised sunna. This is why Ḥanafī texts treat missing it more severely.

fqs-043.q: Which school holds that shortening the four-rakʿa prayers on a journey is obligatory, not merely permitted?
fqs-043.e: For the Ḥanafīs the traveller's prayer is two rakʿas as its original form ('azīma). The Mālikīs call qaṣr an emphasised sunna, and the Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs a concession that may be left.

fqs-044.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, when may two prayers be combined in one time (jamʿ)?
o: Only at ʿArafa and Muzdalifa during Ḥajj
On any journey of the shortening distance
For illness and for any need
fqs-044.e: The Ḥanafīs allow real combining only at ʿArafa (Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr) and Muzdalifa (Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ). Other reports of combining they read as apparent combining: the first prayer at the end of its time and the second at the start of its own.

fqs-045.q: In the Ḥanafī school, where are the prostrations of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) performed?
o: After one salām, then tashahhud and salām again
Before salām for omissions, after for additions
After the prayer is fully ended and one has stood up
fqs-045.e: The Ḥanafīs give one salām to the right, make two prostrations, then repeat the tashahhud and close with salām. The Shāfiʿīs place them before salām, and the Mālikīs distinguish omission and addition.

fqs-046.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Sahw, hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buḥayna
fqs-046.q: A person forgets the first tashahhud and has already stood up fully for the third rakʿa. What do the schools generally hold?
o: He continues and prostrates for forgetfulness
He must sit back down for the tashahhud
His prayer is void and must be restarted
fqs-046.e: In the hadith of Ibn Buḥayna the Prophet ﷺ stood up after two rakʿas, did not return, and prostrated for forgetfulness before the salām. The schools hold that one who has fully stood does not go back; the Ḥanbalīs call returning disliked, the Shāfiʿīs forbidden.

fqs-047.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, on catching the rakʿa
fqs-047.q: A latecomer joins the imam while he is still in rukūʿ and settles in it with him. According to the four schools, what is the result?
o: He must repeat that rakʿa at the end
He has caught only the sujūd
fqs-047.e: The four schools hold that whoever catches the rukūʿ with the imam has caught the rakʿa, even though he missed the recitation. He makes the opening takbīr standing, then goes into rukūʿ.

fqs-048.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tahajjud, hadith of ʿĀʾisha on the two rakʿas of Fajr
fqs-048.q: According to ʿĀʾisha, which voluntary prayer did the Prophet ﷺ keep up more consistently than any other?
fqs-048.e: ʿĀʾisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ was not more regular in any voluntary prayer than the two rakʿas before Fajr. He kept them even on journeys.

fqs-049.q: In Ḥanafī fiqh, what is the consequence of leaving a wājib of the prayer by mistake?
o: It is made good by sujūd al-sahw
The prayer is void and must be repeated
Nothing, since wājib acts are only recommended
The rakʿa must be repeated at once
fqs-049.e: For the Ḥanafīs, a wājib left by oversight is compensated with the prostrations of forgetfulness. Leaving a farḍ voids the prayer; leaving a wājib deliberately makes repeating the prayer necessary.

fqs-050.src: Ibn Quṭlūbughā, Tāj al-Tarājim, entry on al-Qudūrī
fqs-050.q: al-Mukhtaṣar of al-Qudūrī, a classic primer covering ṭahāra and ṣalāh, belongs to which school?
fqs-050.e: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Qudūrī (d. 428 AH) wrote the Mukhtaṣar, which al-Marghīnānī later combined with al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr in Bidāyat al-Mubtadī, the base of al-Hidāya.

fqs-051.q: Who wrote Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, a central text of the Shāfiʿī school?
fqs-051.e: Al-Nawawī wrote the Minhāj as an abridgement of al-Muḥarrar by al-Rāfiʿī. Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī later wrote the commentary Tuḥfat al-Muḥtāj on it.

fqs-052.src: Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī, al-Risāla, introduction
fqs-052.q: Who wrote al-Risāla, the well-known Mālikī primer that opens with creed and then treats ṭahāra and ṣalāh?
fqs-052.e: Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī (d. 386 AH) wrote al-Risāla for teaching the young. Khalīl wrote the later Mukhtaṣar, and Saḥnūn compiled al-Mudawwana.

fqs-053.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-ʿĪdayn, on the prayer before the sermon
fqs-053.q: How does the order of prayer and sermon in the ʿĪd prayer differ from Jumuʿa?
o: In ʿĪd the prayer comes first, then the sermon
In ʿĪd the sermon comes first, as in Jumuʿa
ʿĪd has a sermon before and after the prayer
ʿĪd has no sermon at all
fqs-053.e: The Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar prayed the ʿĪd prayer before the sermon. In Jumuʿa the two sermons precede the prayer and are a condition of its validity.

fqs-054.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on rinsing the mouth and nose
fqs-054.q: In the Ḥanbalī school, rinsing the mouth and nose is obligatory in wuḍūʾ as part of washing the face. What is its status in Ḥanafī wuḍūʾ?
fqs-054.e: The Ḥanbalīs count the mouth and nose as part of the face, so rinsing them is obligatory in both wuḍūʾ and ghusl. The Ḥanafīs make them sunna in wuḍūʾ but obligatory in ghusl.

fqs-055.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on continuity in wuḍūʾ
fqs-055.q: Which pair of schools makes continuity (muwālāt), washing the limbs without a long break, obligatory in wuḍūʾ?
fqs-055.e: The Mālikīs (with remembering and ability) and the Ḥanbalīs make muwālāt a farḍ. The Ḥanafīs and the Shāfiʿīs, in the new view of al-Shāfiʿī, consider it a sunna.

fqs-056.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, Kitāb al-Ṭahārāt, nawāqiḍ al-wuḍūʾ
fqs-056.q: Which school holds that loud laughter (qahqaha) of an adult during a prayer with rukūʿ and sujūd breaks wuḍūʾ as well as the prayer?
fqs-056.e: The Ḥanafīs act on a report about Companions who laughed in prayer and were ordered to repeat wuḍūʾ and prayer. The other schools hold that laughter voids the prayer but not wuḍūʾ, and the Ḥanafīs do not apply it outside prayer or in the funeral prayer.

fqs-057.src: al-Qudūrī, al-Mukhtaṣar, bāb al-ghusl; Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, bāb al-ghusl
fqs-057.q: Which pair of schools holds that rinsing the mouth and nose is obligatory in ghusl?
fqs-057.e: For the Ḥanafīs ghusl requires washing everything that can be reached, including mouth and nose; the Ḥanbalīs require them in both purifications. The Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs make them sunna in ghusl.

fqs-058.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra min al-najas, on semen
fqs-058.q: Which pair of schools holds that human semen (manī) is pure?
fqs-058.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs consider manī pure, citing ʿĀʾisha scraping it off the Prophet's ﷺ garment. The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs hold it impure; the Ḥanafīs allow rubbing off when dry.

fqs-059.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Tayammum, on what tayammum is made with
fqs-059.q: The schools differ over the meaning of the highlighted word. Which pair holds that tayammum is valid only with dust (turāb) that has powder?
fqs-059.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs restrict ṣaʿīd to pure dust with powder that clings. The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs allow anything of the earth's surface, such as stone or sand.

fqs-060.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, faṣl al-masḥ ʿalā al-khuffayn
fqs-060.q: Which school, in its well-known view, sets no fixed time limit for wiping over the khuffayn?
fqs-060.e: The well-known Mālikī position allows masḥ without a time limit, while recommending removal once a week, on Friday. The other three schools apply one day and night for the resident and three for the traveller.

fqs-061.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, what are the minimum and maximum lengths of menstruation?
o: One day and night and fifteen days
fqs-061.e: The Ḥanafīs set three days as the minimum and ten as the maximum. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs hold a day and night and fifteen days; the Mālikīs have no minimum for worship and fifteen days as maximum.

fqs-062.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ḥayḍ, on the length of nifās
fqs-062.q: Which pair of schools gives sixty days as the maximum length of post-natal bleeding (nifās)?
fqs-062.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Mālikīs set sixty days as the maximum. The Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs set forty, following the report of Umm Salama.

fqs-063.q: In the Shāfiʿī school, which najāsa is 'light' (mukhaffafa) and purified by sprinkling water over it?
o: Urine of a boy under two who has only had milk
Urine of any child under seven
fqs-063.e: The Shāfiʿīs class the urine of a male infant under two, fed only on milk, as mukhaffafa and purify it by sprinkling, as in the hadith of Umm Qays. A girl's urine must be washed.

fqs-064.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, faṣl al-ṭāhir; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, on the dog
fqs-064.q: Which school holds that a living dog is pure and that washing a vessel seven times after it licks is an act of worship (taʿabbudī)?
fqs-064.e: The Mālikīs consider every living animal pure, so the sevenfold washing is worship, not removal of najāsa. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs consider the dog najis and require seven washes, one with earth; the Ḥanafīs treat its saliva like other najāsa.

fqs-065.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on water mixed with impurity
fqs-065.q: Which pair of schools uses the measure of 'two qullas' to decide whether still water becomes impure on contact with najāsa?
fqs-065.e: Following the hadith of the two qullas, the Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs hold that water of that amount is not made impure unless a quality changes. The Ḥanafīs judge by whether the impurity spreads through the water, and the Mālikīs by change only.

fqs-066.q: Which of these is a wājib, not a farḍ, of the prayer in the Ḥanafī school?
o: Sitting at the end for the length of the tashahhud
fqs-066.e: For the Ḥanafīs the farḍ is reciting some Quran; specifically reciting al-Fātiḥa is wājib, so omitting it by mistake is repaired with sujūd al-sahw. Standing, rukūʿ and the final sitting are farḍ.

fqs-067.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, bāb ṣifat al-ṣalāt
fqs-067.q: Which school holds that a follower must recite al-Fātiḥa in every rakʿa, even when the imam recites aloud?
fqs-067.e: The Shāfiʿīs make al-Fātiḥa a pillar for imam, follower and individual alike. The Ḥanafīs say the follower does not recite; the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs say he listens in loud prayers and recites (recommended) in quiet ones.

fqs-068.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, on raising the hands
fqs-068.q: Which pair of schools holds it sunna to raise the hands when going into rukūʿ and when rising from it?
fqs-068.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs follow the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar on raising the hands at rukūʿ and rising. The Ḥanafīs, and the Mālikīs in the well-known view, raise them only at the opening takbīr.

fqs-069.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, on qunūt
fqs-069.q: Which pair of schools regards qunūt in the Fajr prayer as a regular recommended practice, not only at times of calamity?
fqs-069.e: The Mālikīs (quietly, before rukūʿ) and the Shāfiʿīs (after rising from rukūʿ in the second rakʿa) make qunūt in Fajr regular. The Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs limit qunūt in obligatory prayers to calamities (nawāzil).

fqs-070.q: How is witr prayed in the Ḥanafī school?
o: Three rakʿas with one salām, qunūt before rukūʿ in the third, all year
One rakʿa alone, qunūt after rukūʿ in Ramaḍān only
Three rakʿas with two salāms, no qunūt
Any odd number up to eleven, qunūt optional
fqs-070.e: The Ḥanafīs pray witr as three rakʿas with one salām and a sitting after the second; before the rukūʿ of the third they say takbīr and recite qunūt throughout the year.

fqs-071.src: Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī, al-Risāla, bāb sujūd al-sahw
fqs-071.q: What is the Mālikī rule on where sujūd al-sahw is placed?
o: Before salām for an omission, after salām for an addition
Before salām only if the imam forgot
fqs-071.e: The Mālikīs prostrate before salām when something is lacking and after salām when something was added, and before salām if both occurred. The Shāfiʿīs always prostrate before salām, the Ḥanafīs after it.

fqs-072.q: How do the Ḥanafīs define the minimum distance of a journey that allows shortening?
o: Three days' travel at a moderate pace
One day and night of travel
Any journey that people call travel
fqs-072.e: The Ḥanafīs set the minimum at a journey of three days at a moderate pace. The other three schools set four burud (sixteen farsakhs), roughly two days' travel; later scholars give approximate kilometre equivalents.

fqs-073.q: According to the Ḥanafī school, an intention to stay in a town for how long makes the traveller a resident who prays in full?
fqs-073.e: The Ḥanafīs make an intention of fifteen days or more end the journey's concession. The Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs set four days (not counting arrival and departure), and the Ḥanbalīs more than twenty prayers.

fqs-074.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Jumuʿa, on the number required
fqs-074.q: Which pair of schools requires forty men of those obliged for the Friday prayer to be valid?
fqs-074.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require forty obliged men including the imam. Abū Ḥanīfa required three besides the imam, and the Mālikīs twelve besides the imam.

fqs-075.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, bāb ṣalāt al-ʿīdayn
fqs-075.q: Which school holds that the ʿĪd prayer is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāya)?
fqs-075.e: The Ḥanbalīs make the ʿĪd prayer farḍ kifāya. The Ḥanafīs hold it wājib on those obliged to attend Jumuʿa, and the Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs an emphasised sunna.

fqs-076.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, on recitation in the funeral prayer
fqs-076.q: Which pair of schools makes reciting al-Fātiḥa after the first takbīr a pillar of the funeral prayer?
fqs-076.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs cite Ibn ʿAbbās reciting al-Fātiḥa in the funeral prayer and calling it sunna. The Ḥanafīs say it is not recited as Quran (only as praise), and the Mālikīs consider it disliked.

fqs-077.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb ṣalāt al-jamāʿa
fqs-077.q: Which school holds that praying the obligatory prayers in congregation is an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) on capable men?
fqs-077.e: The Ḥanbalīs make congregation farḍ ʿayn, though a prayer alone is still valid. The Shāfiʿīs (soundest view) say farḍ kifāya, and the Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs an emphasised sunna, which many later Ḥanafīs call wājib.

fqs-078.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, faṣl sunan al-ṣalāt wa-mandūbātihā
fqs-078.q: Which school is known, in its well-known view, for letting the arms hang at the sides (sadl) in the obligatory prayer?
fqs-078.e: The well-known Mālikī view is sadl in obligatory prayers, with placing the hands allowed in voluntary ones. The Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs place the right hand over the left below the navel, the Shāfiʿīs below the chest.

fqs-079.q: Which school holds that the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwa) is wājib?
fqs-079.e: The Ḥanafīs make it wājib on the reciter and the listener. The other three schools hold it sunna, citing ʿUmar, who said on the minbar that Allah had not made it obligatory unless one wishes.

fqs-080.src: al-Ḥajjāwī, Zād al-Mustaqniʿ, bāb farḍ al-wuḍūʾ wa-ṣifatih; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, on the tasmiya
fqs-080.q: Which school, in its relied-upon position, holds that saying bismillāh at the start of wuḍūʾ is obligatory when one remembers it?
fqs-080.e: The later Ḥanbalī relied-upon view makes the tasmiya wājib, dropping it if forgotten, based on the hadith 'no wuḍūʾ for one who does not mention Allah's name'. Al-Mughnī reports another narration from Aḥmad that it is sunna, the view of the other three schools.

fqs-081.q: Which school treats tayammum as a full substitute for wuḍūʾ, so that one tayammum remains valid for several obligatory prayers, even across prayer times, until water is found or a nullifier occurs?
fqs-081.e: For the Ḥanafīs tayammum lifts the ḥadath until water is found, so it acts like wuḍūʾ. The Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs require a new tayammum for each obligatory prayer, and the Ḥanbalīs hold it ends when the prayer time leaves.

fqs-082.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, bāb masḥ al-khuff; al-Qudūrī, al-Mukhtaṣar, bāb al-masḥ ʿalā al-khuffayn
fqs-082.q: In the relied-upon views of the Ḥanafī, Shāfiʿī and Ḥanbalī schools, from when is the masḥ period counted?
o: From the first ḥadath after putting them on
From the moment they are put on
From the start of the next prayer time
fqs-082.e: The period runs from the first ḥadath after wearing the khuffs in purity, since that is when masḥ becomes possible. A narration from Aḥmad counts from the first wiping, a view some later scholars preferred, but it is not the relied-upon position of these schools.

fqs-083.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, bāb al-masḥ ʿalā al-khuffayn
fqs-083.q: A man washes his right foot and puts on the right khuff, then washes the left foot and puts on the left khuff, completing his wuḍūʾ. Which school allows him to wipe over both after a later ḥadath?
fqs-083.e: The Ḥanafīs require only that the purity be complete at the time of the first ḥadath, which it is. The Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs require complete purity before putting on the khuffs, so the first khuff must be removed and put on again.

fqs-084.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, faṣl al-ḥayḍ
fqs-084.q: Which school, in its well-known view, permits a menstruating woman to recite the Quran from memory while the bleeding continues?
fqs-084.e: The Mālikīs permit it during the bleeding, as she cannot remove her state at will, but not after the blood stops and before ghusl. The Ḥanafīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs forbid her to recite, like the junub.

fqs-085.src: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq, al-Mukhtaṣar, bāb al-ṭahāra; Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, on used water
fqs-085.q: Which school holds that water already used to lift a ḥadath (māʾ mustaʿmal) remains purifying, though its use is disliked?
fqs-085.e: The Mālikīs keep used water ṭahūr with dislike when other water exists. The Ḥanafīs (the view given fatwā), Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs consider it pure but no longer purifying; the latter two apply this when it is less than two qullas.

fqs-086.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṭahāra, on water mixed with impurity
fqs-086.q: Which school holds, in its well-known view, that water, small or large, becomes impure only if its colour, taste or smell changes from the najāsa?
fqs-086.e: The Mālikīs rely on the hadith that water is pure and nothing makes it impure, and apply only the criterion of change, while disliking small water that a little najāsa fell into. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs distinguish by two qullas, and the Ḥanafīs by large and small water.

fqs-087.q: How do the Ḥanafīs classify the closing salām of the prayer, unlike the other three schools?
o: As a condition of the prayer
fqs-087.e: For the Ḥanafīs the word al-salām is wājib, so the prayer is complete once the final sitting is done, even if something else ends it, though leaving the salām is sinful. The other schools make the taslīm a pillar.

fqs-088.src: al-Marghīnānī, al-Hidāya, bāb ṣifat al-ṣalāt, on ṭumaʾnīna
fqs-088.q: Which jurists held that stillness (ṭumaʾnīna) in rukūʿ and sujūd is not a pillar of the prayer but below it in rank?
fqs-088.e: Abū Ḥanīfa and Muḥammad did not make ṭumaʾnīna a farḍ; later Ḥanafīs class it as wājib. Abū Yūsuf, with al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad, made it a farḍ, citing the hadith of the man who prayed badly.

fqs-089.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, bāb ṣalāt al-nafl
fqs-089.q: In the Shāfiʿī school, when is qunūt in the witr prayer a sunna?
o: In the second half of Ramaḍān
Only in the last ten nights of Ramaḍān
fqs-089.e: Al-Nawawī states that qunūt in witr is recommended in the second half of Ramaḍān, after rising from rukūʿ in the last rakʿa. The Ḥanafīs make qunūt in witr all year, before rukūʿ.

fqs-090.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb al-adhān
fqs-090.q: Which pair of schools holds tarjīʿ in the adhān as sunna, saying the two testimonies quietly first and then aloud, following the adhān taught to Abū Maḥdhūra?
fqs-090.e: The Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs follow the adhān of Abū Maḥdhūra with tarjīʿ. The Ḥanafīs and Ḥanbalīs follow the adhān of Bilāl without it.

fqs-091.q: Which jurists held that an adhān for Fajr given before its time is not valid and must be repeated after dawn?
fqs-091.e: Abū Ḥanīfa and Muḥammad allow no adhān before the time for any prayer. Abū Yūsuf, with Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad, permits it for Fajr, citing Bilāl's call at night followed by Ibn Umm Maktūm's.

fqs-092.src: al-Nawawī, Minhāj al-Ṭālibīn, bāb ṣalāt al-musāfir, on combining for rain
fqs-092.q: Which school allows combining Ẓuhr with ʿAṣr, and not only Maghrib with ʿIshāʾ, because of rain?
fqs-092.e: The Shāfiʿīs allow rain-combining for both pairs, only in the time of the first prayer and for those praying in a congregation reached with difficulty. The Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs restrict it to Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ; the Ḥanafīs do not allow it.

fqs-093.q: In the Ḥanafī school, how many additional takbīrs (zawāʾid) are said in each rakʿa of the ʿĪd prayer?
o: Seven in the first, five in the second
Six in the first, five in the second
fqs-093.e: The Ḥanafīs follow Ibn Masʿūd: three extra takbīrs in each rakʿa, before recitation in the first and after it in the second. The Shāfiʿīs say seven and five, and the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs six and five.

fqs-094.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, on praying over the absent
fqs-094.q: Which pair of schools permits the funeral prayer in absentia (ṣalāt al-ghāʾib), citing the Prophet's ﷺ prayer for the Negus (al-Najāshī)?
fqs-094.e: The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs allow praying over an absent body, based on the prayer for al-Najāshī. The Ḥanafīs and Mālikīs do not, treating that event as particular to him.

fqs-095.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, on the martyr
fqs-095.q: A martyr killed in battle is not washed, by agreement. Which school holds that the funeral prayer is nevertheless performed over him?
fqs-095.e: The Ḥanafīs pray over the battlefield martyr, citing reports of prayer over the martyrs of Uḥud. The Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs (relied-upon view) do not, citing Jābir's report that they were neither washed nor prayed over.

fqs-096.src: Ibn Qudāma, ʿUmdat al-Fiqh, bāb al-imāma; Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, hadith of Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī
fqs-096.q: Which school, taking the hadith of Abū Masʿūd ('the one who best recites leads') at face value, gives precedence in leading the prayer to the best reciter over the most learned in fiqh?
fqs-096.e: The Ḥanbalīs put the best reciter who knows the rulings of prayer first. The relied-upon views of the Ḥanafīs, Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs put the most learned in fiqh first, since the needs of the prayer depend more on fiqh.

fqs-097.src: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, on praying alone behind the row
fqs-097.q: A man prays a full rakʿa alone behind the row without an excuse. Which school holds that his prayer is invalid?
fqs-097.e: The Ḥanbalīs act on the hadith of Wābiṣa, in which the Prophet ﷺ ordered such a man to repeat his prayer. The other three schools consider the prayer valid but disliked.

fqs-098.src: Mālik, al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, bāb al-tashahhud
fqs-098.q: Which wording of the tashahhud did Imam Mālik choose, recording it in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ?
o: The tashahhud of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
The tashahhud of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī
fqs-098.e: Mālik chose the tashahhud that ʿUmar taught people from the minbar. Abū Ḥanīfa and Aḥmad preferred that of Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Shāfiʿī that of Ibn ʿAbbās in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; all are valid.

fqs-099.src: Ibn Rushd, Bidāyat al-Mujtahid, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, on the manner of sitting
fqs-099.q: Which school holds that tawarruk (sitting on the left hip with the left foot under the right shin) is the sunna for every sitting of the prayer?
fqs-099.e: The Mālikīs sit in tawarruk in all sittings. The Ḥanafīs sit in iftirāsh in all (for men), the Shāfiʿīs use tawarruk in the last sitting of every prayer, and the Ḥanbalīs only in the last sitting of prayers with two tashahhuds.

fqs-100.q: A latecomer catches the imam of Jumuʿa only in the final tashahhud. Which jurists held that he completes two rakʿas as Jumuʿa rather than praying Ẓuhr?
fqs-100.e: Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf held that catching any part of the imam's prayer is catching Jumuʿa. Muḥammad, with Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad, requires catching a full rakʿa; otherwise he prays four for Ẓuhr.

hdb-001.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy
hdb-001.e: Al-Bukhārī opened his Ṣaḥīḥ with the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that actions are judged by their intentions, reminding the reader to seek knowledge sincerely for Allah.

hdb-002.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of Abū Hurayra
hdb-002.q: Which Companion narrated the largest number of hadith?
hdb-002.e: Abū Hurayra is by common agreement the most prolific narrator among the Companions. Anas, Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir are also among the prolific narrators, but with fewer reports.

hdb-003.src: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Muqaddima, on the ṣaḥīḥ
hdb-003.q: Which two books are meant by "al-Ṣaḥīḥān" (the two Ṣaḥīḥs)?
o: The collections of al-Bukhārī and Muslim
The collections of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī
The Muwaṭṭaʾ and the Musnad of Aḥmad
The collections of al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah
hdb-003.e: "Al-Ṣaḥīḥān" are the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī and the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, regarded by the scholars as the most authentic books after the Quran.

hdb-004.src: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, Tartīb al-Madārik, biography of Mālik
hdb-004.e: Al-Muwaṭṭaʾ is the work of Imam Mālik ibn Anas, the imam of Medina. Al-Shāfiʿī studied it with him.

hdb-005.q: Which founder of a school of law compiled al-Musnad, one of the largest hadith collections?
hdb-005.e: Imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal compiled al-Musnad, arranged by Companion; his son ʿAbd Allāh transmitted it and added further reports.

hdb-006.q: Who compiled the famous collection known as "the Forty Hadith" (al-Arbaʿūn)?
hdb-006.e: Al-Nawawī collected these foundational hadith in al-Arbaʿūn al-Nawawiyya; despite the name it contains forty-two hadith.

hdb-007.q: Who is the author of Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn?
hdb-007.e: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn (The Gardens of the Righteous) was compiled by al-Nawawī from authoritative collections, on character, worship and good conduct.

hdb-008.q: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, which Companion narrates the hadith of Jibrīl (about Islam, īmān and iḥsān)?
hdb-008.e: Muslim opens Kitāb al-Īmān with this hadith, which Ibn ʿUmar narrates from his father ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Al-Bukhārī has a version from Abū Hurayra.

hdb-009.q: Which three levels of the religion does the hadith of Jibrīl explain?
hdb-009.e: Jibrīl asked about Islām, īmān and iḥsān (and the Hour); at the end the Prophet said he had come to teach the people their religion.

hdb-010.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Hady al-Sārī, biography of al-Bukhārī
hdb-010.q: In which city was Imam al-Bukhārī born?
hdb-010.e: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl was born in Bukhara, from which his nisba comes. Nishapur was the city of Imam Muslim.

hdb-011.src: al-Nawawī, al-Minhāj Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, introduction
hdb-011.q: Which scholar compiled the Ṣaḥīḥ that is usually ranked second after Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī?
hdb-011.e: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, by Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Qushayrī al-Naysābūrī, is ranked by most scholars directly after Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.

hdb-012.q: Which prolific narrator served the Prophet in Medina for about ten years as a boy?
hdb-012.e: Anas ibn Mālik was brought to the Prophet by his mother and served him for about ten years, as he himself reports. Abū Hurayra accompanied him only in his last years.

hdb-013.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of ʿĀʾisha
hdb-013.q: Which wife of the Prophet narrated the most hadith?
hdb-013.e: ʿĀʾisha is among the most prolific narrators of all Companions and by far the most prolific woman. Khadīja died before the Hijra.

hdb-014.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of Ibn ʿAbbās
hdb-014.q: Which prolific narrator is known as "Turjumān al-Qurʾān" (interpreter of the Quran)?
hdb-014.e: Ibn ʿAbbās, for whom the Prophet prayed that he be given understanding of the religion, is called the interpreter of the Quran and is among the prolific narrators.

hdb-015.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Bulūgh al-Marām min Adillat al-Aḥkām, introduction
hdb-015.q: Who compiled Bulūgh al-Marām, a widely taught collection of legal hadith?
hdb-015.e: Ibn Ḥajar gathered the hadith used as evidence for legal rulings in Bulūgh al-Marām min Adillat al-Aḥkām, noting who narrated each and often its grading.

hdb-016.q: In common usage, a hadith described as "muttafaq ʿalayh" is one that …
o: all four imams of fiqh accepted
hdb-016.e: In general usage, followed for example in Bulūgh al-Marām, "muttafaq ʿalayh" means narrated by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim (from the same Companion).

hdb-017.src: al-Kattānī, al-Risāla al-Mustaṭrafa, section on the masānīd
hdb-017.q: Which collection is arranged by Companion, gathering each Companion's narrations together?
o: The Musnad of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal
hdb-017.e: A musnad is ordered by the Companion who narrates, not by subject. Musnad Aḥmad is the best-known example; the other three are arranged by topics.

hdb-018.src: Ibn Ṭāhir al-Maqdisī, Shurūṭ al-Aʾimma al-Sitta
hdb-018.q: Besides the two Ṣaḥīḥs, which four works are, in the most common count, the remaining books of "the six books"?
o: The Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah
The Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and al-Dārimī
The Musnad of Aḥmad, the Muwaṭṭaʾ, al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī
The Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Bayhaqī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah
hdb-018.e: The common count of al-Kutub al-Sitta is al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and the four Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah. Some scholars placed al-Muwaṭṭaʾ or al-Dārimī in the sixth place instead of Ibn Mājah.

hdb-019.src: Abū Dāwūd, Risāla ilā Ahl Makka
hdb-019.q: For what is the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd especially known?
o: Gathering the hadith used for legal rulings
Arranging hadith by the narrating Companion
Including only hadith meeting al-Bukhārī's terms
Collecting the narrations on Quranic exegesis
hdb-019.e: Abū Dāwūd focused on the hadith that jurists use as evidence (aḥkām), as he explains in his letter to the people of Mecca; for this reason his Sunan is a basic reference for fiqh.

hdb-020.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-ʿIlm, chapter on how knowledge is taken away
hdb-020.q: Which caliph wrote to the scholars ordering that the hadith of the Prophet be sought out and written down, fearing that knowledge would vanish?
hdb-020.e: Al-Bukhārī reports (without a full chain) that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm to write down the hadith, fearing the loss of knowledge and the passing of the scholars. This is seen as the start of official compilation (tadwīn).

hdb-021.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb al-ʿIlm; al-Dhahabī, Siyar, biography of al-Zuhrī
hdb-021.q: Which Successor is commonly named as the first to compile hadith officially, at the order of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz?
hdb-021.e: Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī is commonly called the first to compile hadith (awwal man dawwana) by official order. Mālik was one of his students, from the following generation.

hdb-022.q: Under which title is al-Tirmidhī's main collection known, besides "Sunan al-Tirmidhī"?
hdb-022.e: Al-Tirmidhī's collection is known as al-Jāmiʿ because it covers all the main subjects, though it is also called Sunan al-Tirmidhī. Al-Mujtabā is al-Nasāʾī's Sunan.

hdb-023.src: al-Suyūṭī, Zahr al-Rubā ʿalā al-Mujtabā, introduction
hdb-023.q: Which work of al-Nasāʾī is the one counted among the six books?
hdb-023.e: Al-Nasāʾī wrote a large work, al-Sunan al-Kubrā; the shorter selection al-Mujtabā (al-Sunan al-Ṣughrā) is the one meant when "Sunan al-Nasāʾī" is counted among the six books.

hdb-024.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī bi-Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, introduction
hdb-024.q: Fatḥ al-Bārī by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī is a commentary on which book?
hdb-024.e: Fatḥ al-Bārī bi-Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī is the most famous commentary on al-Bukhārī; its introduction is called Hady al-Sārī.

hdb-025.src: al-Nawawī, al-Minhāj Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj
hdb-025.q: al-Nawawī's well-known commentary al-Minhāj explains which book?
hdb-025.e: Al-Minhāj Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj, often simply called Sharḥ al-Nawawī ʿalā Muslim, is the most widely read commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Al-Nawawī began a commentary on al-Bukhārī but did not complete it.

hdb-026.q: Which hadith is the second in al-Nawawī's Forty Hadith?
o: The hadith of Jibrīl on Islām, īmān and iḥsān
The hadith that Islam is built on five
The hadith that actions are judged by intentions
The hadith that the lawful is clear
hdb-026.e: Al-Nawawī begins with the hadith of intentions, then places the hadith of Jibrīl second and "Islam is built on five" third.

hdb-027.q: Besides the Prophet's hadith, what else does al-Muwaṭṭaʾ contain to a large extent?
o: Sayings of Companions and Successors and Medinan practice
Long chapters of Quranic exegesis by Mālik
Biographies and gradings of hadith narrators
Only the hadith with complete connected chains
hdb-027.e: Al-Muwaṭṭaʾ mixes marfūʿ hadith with reports from Companions and Successors, Mālik's own opinions and the practice of the people of Medina (ʿamal ahl al-Madīna), and includes mursal reports.

hdb-028.src: al-Nawawī, al-Arbaʿūn, hadith 3; al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Kitāb al-Īmān
hdb-028.q: Which Companion narrates the hadith "Islam is built on five" in al-Bukhārī and Muslim?
hdb-028.e: The hadith that Islam is built on five pillars is narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and is recorded by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

hdb-029.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of Nāfiʿ
hdb-029.q: Nāfiʿ, the famous freed slave (mawlā) and transmitter, narrated mainly from which Companion?
hdb-029.e: Nāfiʿ was the mawlā of Ibn ʿUmar and the main transmitter of his narrations; the chain Mālik from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar is famous. Ibn ʿAbbās' well-known mawlā was ʿIkrima.

hdb-030.src: Ibn Ḥajar, al-Iṣāba fī Tamyīz al-Ṣaḥāba, biography of Abū Hurayra
hdb-030.q: Around which event did Abū Hurayra come to the Prophet and accept Islam, according to the common account?
o: The campaign of Khaybar in 7 AH
The battle of Badr in 2 AH
The conquest of Mecca in 8 AH
hdb-030.e: Abū Hurayra came to Medina around the time of Khaybar (7 AH) and stayed close to the Prophet for his remaining years, which explains how he could narrate so much in a short time.

hdb-031.src: al-Nawawī, al-Minhāj Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, introduction
hdb-031.q: Imam Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj is linked by his nisba al-Naysābūrī to which city?
hdb-031.e: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Qushayrī was from Nishapur in Khurasan, where he lived and died. Al-Bukhārī was from Bukhara.

hdb-032.q: Which feature especially distinguishes al-Tirmidhī's Jāmiʿ among the six books?
o: He grades hadith and reports the jurists' opinions
He arranges the hadith by the narrating Companion
He includes only hadith that al-Bukhārī accepted
He records only hadith qudsī and Companion sayings
hdb-032.e: After many hadith al-Tirmidhī states his grading (e.g. ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) and mentions which scholars acted on it, making his Jāmiʿ valuable for both hadith criticism and comparative fiqh.

hdb-033.src: al-Nawawī, al-Arbaʿūn, hadith 7; Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān
hdb-033.q: Which Companion narrates the hadith that the religion is sincere counsel (naṣīḥa), recorded with a full chain in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim?
hdb-033.e: The hadith of naṣīḥa is narrated by Tamīm al-Dārī in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; al-Bukhārī uses its wording only as a chapter heading.

hdb-034.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of al-Ḥākim
hdb-034.e: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Naysābūrī, commonly said to have died in 405 AH, compiled al-Mustadrak. Al-Bayhaqī was one of his students.
