xuf-026.e: The Ḥanafī manuals distinguish ahliyyat al-wujūb, based on the human soul (dhimma) and thus held by every human being including the foetus in limited form, from ahliyyat al-adāʾ, based on discernment and reason, which is incomplete in the discerning child and complete at puberty with sound reason. Impediments (ʿawāriḍ) such as madness, forgetfulness, sleep and compulsion affect them. The majority use similar ideas with different terms.

xuf-027.src: al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā; al-Shāṭibī, al-Muwāfaqāt; Ibn ʿĀshūr, Maqāṣid al-Sharīʿa al-Islāmiyya
xuf-027.q: Which classification of the Sharia’s purposes (maqāṣid) did al-Ghazālī and al-Shāṭibī develop?
o: Necessities (ḍarūriyyāt), needs (ḥājiyyāt) and refinements (taḥsīniyyāt), with the five necessities protecting religion, life, intellect, lineage and property
Rights of God, rights of rulers and rights of animals
xuf-027.e: Al-Ghazālī presented the five necessities as the preserved goals of the Sharia, and al-Shāṭibī in al-Muwāfaqāt arranged the purposes in three levels: ḍarūriyyāt (necessities), ḥājiyyāt (needs) and taḥsīniyyāt (embellishments). Some later scholars add the protection of honour (ʿirḍ). Ibn ʿĀshūr later widened the study in the 20th century.

xuf-028.src: al-Shāfiʿī, al-Risāla; al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā; al-Suyūṭī, al-Radd ʿalā man Akhlada ilā al-Arḍ; Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Adab al-Muftī
xuf-028.q: What disagreement exists about the 'closing of the gate of ijtihād'?
o: Some later jurists held that independent ijtihād ended with the founding imams, while others, such as al-Suyūṭī and Ibn Taymiyya, rejected that and held that every age must have its mujtahids
All scholars agree it was closed in 300 AH
All scholars agree it can never be closed
xuf-028.e: The idea that unrestricted ijtihād ceased in the fourth century is the position of some late jurists who feared disorder and promoted taqlīd to the four schools. Many scholars rejected it, among them Ibn Taymiyya and al-Suyūṭī, who wrote a treatise against those who clung to the earth, claiming that the earth is never empty of a mujtahid. Modern historians also question whether it was ever formally closed.

xuf-029.src: al-Sarakhsī, Uṣūl; al-Shīrāzī, al-Lumaʿ; al-Shāfiʿī, al-Risāla; al-Shāṭibī, al-Muwāfaqāt
xuf-029.q: How did the schools differ on using a single-narrator report (khabar al-wāḥid) in law?
o: The majority accept it as evidence for rulings; the Ḥanafīs set conditions, such as that it does not contradict a more widely known practice, and some Mālikīs preferred Madinan practice when it conflicts
All schools accept it for creed only
xuf-029.e: The jurists, with scholars like al-Shāfiʿī, accepted the sound single-narrator report as proof of legal rulings. The Ḥanafīs required that it not contradict the Quran’s apparent meaning, a widely known sunna or the narrator’s own contrary practice, and concerning matters of general concern they asked for widespread transmission. The Mālikīs in cases of conflict with the practice of Madīna gave weight to the practice.

xuf-030.src: al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā; al-Shīrāzī, al-Lumaʿ; al-Āmidī, al-Iḥkām
xuf-030.q: What is the debate on whether every mujtahid is correct (taṣwīb al-mujtahidīn)?
o: Whether all mujtahids are correct (al-muṣawwiba) or only one is correct and the other is mistaken but rewarded; most jurists held that only one is correct in God’s knowledge, with the mistaken still rewarded once
xuf-030.e: The Muṣawwiba (including some Ashʿarīs and Muʿtazilīs) held that every mujtahid is correct since God’s ruling follows the mujtahid’s result. The majority hold that there is one correct answer with God, so the right one gets two rewards and the mistaken one gets one, as in the well-known Prophetic statement about the judge. The hadith is reported with differing wording but is widely used in this discussion.

xuf-031.src: Ḥājjī Khalīfa, Kashf al-Ẓunūn; al-Zuḥaylī, Uṣūl al-Fiqh al-Islāmī; Ibn Khaldūn, Muqaddima
xuf-031.q: Which of these correctly distinguishes the two methods of writing uṣūl al-fiqh?
o: The way of the theologians (mutakallimūn) builds rules by proof independent of branch rulings (e.g. al-Mustaṣfā); the Ḥanafī way derives rules from the branch rulings of the founders (e.g. Uṣūl al-Sarakhsī)
One is written in prose and the other only in poetry
One is for men and the other for women
One is for prayer and the other for trade
xuf-031.e: Ibn Khaldūn and others describe two methods: the Shāfiʿī path of the mutakallimūn, writing rules abstractly through proofs (al-Mustaṣfā, al-Burhān, al-Iḥkām), and the Ḥanafī path of the fuqahāʾ, extracting rules from the rulings of Abū Ḥanīfa and his students (Uṣūl al-Sarakhsī and al-Bazdawī). Later works like Ibn al-Sāʿātī’s Badīʿ al-Niẓām combined both.

xuf-032.src: al-Shāfiʿī, al-Risāla; al-Juwaynī, al-Burhān; al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā; al-Rāzī, al-Maḥṣūl
xuf-032.q: Which sequence of works marks the development of Shāfiʿī and theological uṣūl?
o: al-Shāfiʿī’s al-Risāla, al-Juwaynī’s al-Burhān, al-Ghazālī’s al-Mustaṣfā and al-Rāzī’s al-Maḥṣūl
al-Ṭabarī’s Jāmiʿ, al-Bukhārī’s Ṣaḥīḥ, Muslim’s Ṣaḥīḥ and Abū Dāwūd’s Sunan
al-Mubarrad’s al-Kāmil, Sībawayh’s al-Kitāb, al-Zamakhsharī’s al-Mufaṣṣal and Ibn Mālik’s Alfiyya
Ibn Isḥāq’s Sīra, al-Wāqidī’s Maghāzī, Ibn Hishām’s Sīra and al-Ṭabarī’s Taʾrīkh
xuf-032.e: Al-Shāfiʿī’s al-Risāla is usually called the first book of uṣūl al-fiqh. Al-Juwaynī’s al-Burhān, his student al-Ghazālī’s al-Mustaṣfā and Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī’s al-Maḥṣūl represent the developed theological method. Al-Āmidī’s al-Iḥkām and al-Isnawī’s Nihāyat al-Sūl follow it. These works shaped later textbooks.

xuf-033.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Ashbāh wa-l-Naẓāʾir; Ibn Nujaym, al-Ashbāh wa-l-Naẓāʾir; Majallat al-Aḥkām al-ʿAdliyya
xuf-033.q: What are the 'five great maxims' (al-qawāʿid al-kubrā) of legal maxims commonly listed in al-Suyūṭī’s al-Ashbāh wa-l-Naẓāʾir?
o: Matters are judged by their intentions; certainty is not removed by doubt; hardship brings ease; harm is to be removed; custom is a basis for judgement
Prayer is a pillar; fasting is a shield; zakāt purifies; ḥajj once; jihād by the ruler
The Quran first; the Sunna second; consensus third; analogy fourth; custom fifth
The oath on the denier; the proof on the claimant; the witness two; the judge one; the court open
xuf-033.e: Legal maxims summarise many branch rulings. The five commonly listed major maxims are: al-umūr bi-maqāṣidihā (actions by their intentions), al-yaqīn lā yazūl bi-l-shakk (certainty is not removed by doubt), al-mashaqqa tajlib al-taysīr (hardship brings ease), al-ḍarar yuzāl (harm is removed) and al-ʿāda muḥakkama (custom is authoritative). Al-Suyūṭī, Ibn Nujaym and the Ottoman Majalla use them.

xuf-034.src: Ibn ʿĀbidīn, Nashr al-ʿArf; al-Qarāfī, al-Iḥkām fī Tamyīz al-Fatāwā ʿan al-Aḥkām; Ibn al-Qayyim, Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn
xuf-034.q: What is the role of custom (ʿurf) in legal reasoning, and what did al-Qarāfī and Ibn al-Qayyim say about fatwā?
o: Custom may specify general texts and determine undefined matters when it does not contradict a text; both said fatwās change with place, time and customs when the basis was custom
xuf-034.e: ʿUrf, a recognised habit of a people, is accepted by most schools as a means to interpret undefined terms and measure obligations (such as the amount of maintenance) if it does not contradict a text. Al-Qarāfī and Ibn al-Qayyim stressed that fatwās founded on custom must be changed when customs change, while the text-based ruling stays. Ibn ʿĀbidīn wrote the treatise Nashr al-ʿArf on it.

xuf-035.src: al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā; Ibn al-Qayyim, Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn; al-Sarakhsī, Uṣūl
xuf-035.q: What is istiṣḥāb (presumption of continuity) and where do the schools differ?
o: Presuming that a state known to have existed continues until proven otherwise; Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs use it widely as proof, while Ḥanafīs generally accept it only to maintain an existing state, not to establish a new right
xuf-035.e: Istiṣḥāb is the continuation of a previous ruling or state in the absence of evidence of change, as in the presumption of purity or innocence. Most Shāfiʿīs, Ḥanbalīs and Mālikīs use it as proof; the Ḥanafīs said it is a proof for repelling a claim (daf‘) but not for establishing a new claim (ithbāt), a distinction often cited in the case of the missing person.

xuf-036.src: Ibn al-Qayyim, Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn; al-Shāṭibī, al-Muwāfaqāt; al-Shaybānī, Kitāb al-Makhārij fī al-Ḥiyal
xuf-036.q: What was the main objection of scholars like Ibn al-Qayyim to legal devices (ḥiyal)?
o: That they use lawful forms to reach a forbidden result, which defeats the purpose of the Sharia; the Ḥanafīs, with works on makhārij, allowed some forms, while the Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs opposed them strongly
That they are written in Persian
That they use the Quran as a poem
xuf-036.e: Ḥiyal are legal stratagems that reach an aim by a form that avoids the apparent prohibition. Ibn al-Qayyim devoted long sections of Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn to refuting them, citing the Prophet’s criticism of those who used tricks to evade God’s limits, and arguing that the intention defines the act. Ḥanafī works such as al-Shaybānī’s al-Makhārij fī al-Ḥiyal allowed those used to escape hardship, with conditions.

xuf-037.src: Ibn Khallikān, Wafayāt al-Aʿyān; al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ; Ibn Farḥūn, al-Dībāj al-Mudhahhab
xuf-037.q: Which statement correctly pairs the founders of the four Sunni schools with their works or transmitted books?
o: Abū Ḥanīfa: al-Fiqh al-Akbar (attributed); Mālik: al-Muwaṭṭaʾ; al-Shāfiʿī: al-Umm and al-Risāla; Aḥmad: al-Musnad
Abū Ḥanīfa: al-Umm; Mālik: al-Musnad; al-Shāfiʿī: al-Muwaṭṭaʾ; Aḥmad: al-Risāla
Abū Ḥanīfa: al-Risāla; Mālik: al-Fiqh al-Akbar; al-Shāfiʿī: al-Musnad; Aḥmad: al-Muwaṭṭaʾ
All four wrote exactly the same book
xuf-037.e: Abū Ḥanīfa’s school is built on the transmissions of his students (al-Shaybānī’s Zāhir al-Riwāya), and the creed al-Fiqh al-Akbar is attributed to him. Mālik’s al-Muwaṭṭaʾ is a hadith and fiqh book. Al-Shāfiʿī wrote al-Risāla (uṣūl) and al-Umm (fiqh, with transmission through al-Rabīʿ). Aḥmad’s Musnad is a hadith compilation rather than a fiqh text; his fiqh was recorded by his students.

xuf-038.src: Ibn ʿĀbidīn, Radd al-Muḥtār; al-Qarāfī, al-Iḥkām; al-Zuḥaylī, al-Fiqh al-Islāmī wa-Adillatuhu
xuf-038.q: What is talfīq, and how do jurists view it?
o: Combining the opinions of different schools in one act in a way that none of the schools would accept as valid; many jurists restrict or forbid it, while others allow it in cases of need
A way of reciting the Quran
xuf-038.e: Talfīq arises when a person follows one school for one part of an act and another for another part, so the combination is valid under none (for example, taking ablution rules from one school and a touching rule from another so that neither would accept the prayer). Some jurists forbid it; others, especially later ones, allow it for need or ease, with conditions of sincerity and not chasing concessions (tatabbuʿ al-rukhaṣ).

xuf-039.src: Ibn Taymiyya, Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā and Raf‘ al-Malām ʿan al-Aʾimma al-Aʿlām; Ibn al-Qayyim, Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn
xuf-039.q: What is Ibn Taymiyya’s Raf‘ al-Malām ʿan al-Aʾimma al-Aʿlām about?
o: It explains ten reasons why the jurist-imams may differ from a sound hadith, to defend them from blame while insisting that a sound hadith must be followed
It rules that the imams are infallible
It is a book of poetry in praise of the imams
It ranks the schools by age
xuf-039.e: Raf‘ al-Malām lists reasons that a respected mujtahid may not have acted by a sound hadith (the hadith did not reach him, he held it weak, he understood it differently, he held it abrogated and so on). The treatise defends the imams from reproach but affirms that once a sound hadith is known its meaning must be followed. It is a classic on the ethics of disagreement.

xuf-040.src: al-Mardāwī, al-Inṣāf; al-Nawawī, al-Majmūʿ, introduction; Ibn ʿĀbidīn, Radd al-Muḥtār, introduction
xuf-040.q: How do later jurists identify the 'preferred opinion' of a school (al-muʿtamad) when it has more than one opinion?
o: By the tarjīḥ of the school’s verifiers, such as al-Nawawī and al-Rāfiʿī for the Shāfiʿīs (the two shaykhs), Ibn ʿĀbidīn for the Ḥanafīs, Khalīl’s commentators for the Mālikīs and al-Mardāwī for the Ḥanbalīs
By the opinion of the ruler of the time
By the number of pages in a book
xuf-040.e: Each school has a body of conventions to identify its reliable view. In the Shāfiʿī school, the agreement of al-Nawawī and al-Rāfiʿī (al-shaykhān) is the basis, with al-Nawawī preferred when they differ; in the Ḥanafī school Ibn ʿĀbidīn’s Radd al-Muḥtār sets rules for tarjīḥ; in the Mālikī school Mukhtaṣar Khalīl with its commentators; in the Ḥanbalī school al-Mardāwī’s al-Inṣāf. These regulate fatwā within each school.

srm-001.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, lineage of the Prophet
srm-001.q: What was the name of the Prophet Muḥammad's father?
srm-001.e: His father was ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was his grandfather, Abū Ṭālib his uncle and Hāshim his great-grandfather.

srm-002.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, lineage of the Prophet
srm-002.q: Who was the mother of the Prophet Muḥammad?
srm-002.e: His mother was Āmina bint Wahb of the clan of Zuhra. Ḥalīma was his wet nurse, Khadīja his first wife and Fāṭima bint Asad the wife of Abū Ṭālib.

srm-003.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, lineage of the Prophet
srm-003.q: To which tribe did the Prophet Muḥammad belong?
srm-003.e: He was from the clan of Hāshim within Quraysh, the tribe that guarded the Kaʿba in Mecca. Thaqīf lived in al-Ṭāʾif, the Khazraj in Yathrib.

srm-004.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Fīl
srm-004.q: The verse shown opens a sūra about an event in the year the Prophet was born. Which army does it refer to?
srm-004.e: Sūrat al-Fīl recalls how Abraha marched on Mecca with an elephant to destroy the Kaʿba and was turned back. The Prophet was born in that same year, the Year of the Elephant.

srm-005.src: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Kitāb al-Ṣiyām, fasting on Mondays
srm-005.q: On which day of the week was the Prophet born?
srm-005.e: When asked about fasting on Monday, the Prophet said it was the day on which he was born and on which revelation came to him (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim).

srm-006.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the nursing in Banū Saʿd
srm-006.q: Ḥalīma, the Prophet's wet nurse, belonged to which tribe?
srm-006.e: Ḥalīma bint Abī Dhuʾayb was from Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr, a Bedouin tribe of Hawāzin. Meccan families sent infants to the desert for its healthy air and pure Arabic.

srm-007.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the story of Baḥīrā
srm-007.q: Who was Baḥīrā, whom the young Muḥammad met on a journey with Abū Ṭālib?
o: A Christian monk near Buṣrā in Syria
srm-007.e: On a trade journey to Syria with his uncle Abū Ṭālib, the caravan stopped near the hermitage of the monk Baḥīrā at Buṣrā, who recognised signs of prophethood in the boy.

srm-008.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the rebuilding of the Kaʿba
srm-008.q: By which title did the people of Mecca know Muḥammad before his prophethood?
srm-008.e: Quraysh called him al-Amīn because of his honesty and reliability. al-Fārūq became the title of ʿUmar, al-Ṣiddīq of Abū Bakr and Sayf Allāh of Khālid ibn al-Walīd.

srm-009.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, marriage to Khadīja
srm-009.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet?
srm-009.e: Khadīja was his first wife, and he married no one else while she lived. Sawda and ʿĀʾisha were married after her death, Ḥafṣa later in Medina.

srm-010.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the rebuilding of the Kaʿba
srm-010.q: When the Prophet was about thirty-five, Quraysh rebuilt a building in Mecca. Which one?
srm-010.e: Commonly dated to when he was thirty-five, Quraysh rebuilt the Kaʿba after damage by flooding; it was during this rebuilding that the dispute over the Black Stone arose.

srm-011.q: In which cave did the first revelation come to the Prophet?
srm-011.e: He used to retreat to the cave of Ḥirāʾ on the mountain later called Jabal al-Nūr, where Jibrīl came to him. Thawr is the cave of the Hijra.

srm-012.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, the sending of the Prophet
srm-012.q: How old was the Prophet, according to most biographers, when revelation began?
srm-012.e: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that he was sent at forty (al-Bukhārī). At twenty-five he married Khadīja and at about thirty-five the Kaʿba was rebuilt.

srm-013.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the first to accept Islam
srm-013.q: Who was the very first person to believe in the Prophet's message?
srm-013.e: Khadīja believed at once when he returned from Ḥirāʾ and comforted him. Abū Bakr was the first free adult man, ʿAlī the first boy and Zayd the first freedman.

srm-014.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Masad
srm-014.q: The sūra that opens with the verse shown was revealed about the Prophet's uncle who rejected him at al-Ṣafā. Who was he?
srm-014.e: When the Prophet called the clans of Quraysh from al-Ṣafā, his uncle Abū Lahab cursed him, and Sūrat al-Masad was revealed (al-Bukhārī). Abū Jahl was of Makhzūm, not his uncle.

srm-015.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the persecution of the weak Muslims
srm-015.q: What did Bilāl keep repeating while he was tortured in the heat of Mecca?
srm-015.e: Pinned under a heavy rock in the burning sun, Bilāl affirmed the oneness of God with the single word “Aḥad”, refusing to praise the idols as his tormentors demanded.

srm-016.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the emigration to Abyssinia
srm-016.q: What was the title of the Christian king of Abyssinia who sheltered the Muslim emigrants?
srm-016.e: The ruler of Abyssinia bore the title al-Najāshī; the Prophet described him as a king under whom no one is wronged. Qayṣar ruled Byzantium, Kisrā Persia and Tubbaʿ was the title of the old Yemeni kings.

srm-017.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the deaths of Abū Ṭālib and Khadīja
srm-017.q: The “Year of Sorrow” (ʿĀm al-Ḥuzn) is named after the deaths of which two people?
srm-017.e: In the tenth year of prophethood the Prophet lost his protecting uncle Abū Ṭālib and his wife Khadīja within a short time. Āmina and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had died in his childhood; Ḥamza and Jaʿfar fell later in battle.

srm-018.q: The verse shown describes the Night Journey from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām. To which mosque was the Prophet taken?
o: The mosque of al-Khayf in Minā
srm-018.e: al-Isrāʾ was the journey by night from Mecca to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā in Jerusalem, followed by the ascension (al-Miʿrāj). Qubāʾ and the Prophet's Mosque were built only after the Hijra.

srm-019.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the Hijra
srm-019.q: In which cave did the Prophet and Abū Bakr hide during the Hijra?
srm-019.e: They hid for three nights in the cave of Thawr, south of Mecca, while Quraysh searched the routes north toward Yathrib. Ḥirāʾ is the cave of the first revelation.

srm-020.q: The verse shown speaks of the Prophet and his companion in the cave during the Hijra. Who was that companion?
srm-020.e: The verse refers to the second of two in the cave of Thawr, and the exegetes agree that the companion was Abū Bakr. ʿAlī stayed behind in Mecca in the Prophet's bed.

srm-021.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the death of Āmina
srm-021.q: Who took charge of the Prophet immediately after the death of his mother?
srm-021.e: After Āmina died, his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him in and treated him with special affection. Only after ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's death did Abū Ṭālib become his guardian.

srm-022.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the death of Āmina
srm-022.q: Where did Āmina, the Prophet's mother, die?
o: At al-Abwāʾ, between Mecca and Yathrib
In Mecca, in the house of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib
srm-022.e: Returning from a visit to relatives of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's mother in Yathrib, Āmina fell ill and died at al-Abwāʾ when the Prophet was about six years old.

srm-023.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, account of Umm Ayman
srm-023.q: Which woman accompanied Āmina and the young Muḥammad on the journey to Yathrib and brought him back to Mecca?
srm-023.e: Umm Ayman, the Abyssinian servant inherited from his father, was with them and brought the orphaned boy home after Āmina's death at al-Abwāʾ. He later honoured her as a second mother.

srm-024.src: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Kitāb al-Īmān, the Isrāʾ and the opening of the chest
srm-024.q: Which event took place while the Prophet was a child among Banū Saʿd?
o: Jibrīl opened and cleansed his chest
He joined the pact of Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl
srm-024.e: Anas reports in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that Jibrīl came to him while he was playing with other boys, opened his chest and washed his heart. Baḥīrā and Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl came later in his youth.

srm-025.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat Quraysh
srm-025.q: The verse shown mentions the winter and summer journeys of Quraysh. According to the exegetes, where did they lead?
o: Winter to Yemen, summer to Syria
Winter to Syria, summer to Yemen
Winter to Iraq, summer to Egypt
Winter to Abyssinia, summer to Iraq
srm-025.e: Ibn Kathīr and others explain that Quraysh travelled to warm Yemen in winter and to Syria in summer. Their security as guardians of the Sanctuary made these caravans possible.

srm-026.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the idols of the Arabs
srm-026.q: Which idol was regarded as the chief idol of Quraysh at the Kaʿba?
srm-026.e: Hubal stood at the Kaʿba and divining arrows were cast before it. al-Lāt was worshipped at al-Ṭāʾif, al-ʿUzzā at Nakhla and Manāt near Qudayd on the coast.

srm-027.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the story of Baḥīrā
srm-027.q: What did the monk Baḥīrā advise Abū Ṭālib to do with his nephew?
o: Take him back home and guard him well
Leave him with the monks to study scripture
Take him on to Jerusalem to be blessed
Present him to the governor of Syria
srm-027.e: Having recognised the signs of prophethood, Baḥīrā warned that the boy could come to harm and urged Abū Ṭālib to return him quickly to Mecca. The journey is commonly placed when he was about twelve.

srm-028.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl
srm-028.q: What was the purpose of Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl, which the Prophet attended as a young man?
o: To defend anyone wronged in Mecca until justice was done
To unite Quraysh against the army of Abraha
To divide the offices of the Kaʿba among the clans
To boycott the clan of Banū Hāshim
srm-028.e: Several clans of Quraysh pledged to stand by any victim of injustice in Mecca, whether local or a stranger, until his right was restored. The boycott of Banū Hāshim came decades later.

srm-029.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, marriage to Khadīja
srm-029.q: According to the commonly stated account, how old were the Prophet and Khadīja when they married?
srm-029.e: Most biographers state that he was twenty-five and she forty; some reports give her a younger age, so the figure is the common, not the only, view.

srm-030.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, marriage to Khadīja
srm-030.q: Which servant of Khadīja accompanied the Prophet on her trade journey to Syria and reported his conduct to her?
srm-030.e: Maysara travelled with him, saw his honesty and the success of the trade, and told Khadīja, which moved her to propose marriage. Zayd came into the household later as a gift to Khadīja.

srm-031.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the rebuilding of the Kaʿba
srm-031.q: How did the Prophet settle the dispute over who would set the Black Stone back in place?
o: He placed it on a cloak and had a leader of each clan lift it together
He cast lots among the clans of Quraysh
He set it in place alone without consulting anyone
He gave the honour to the eldest man of Quraysh
srm-031.e: He laid the stone on a cloak, let a representative of every clan hold an edge and raise it, then set it in place with his own hands, so that every clan shared the honour.

srm-032.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy, hadith of ʿĀʾisha
srm-032.q: According to ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, how did revelation first begin for the Prophet?
o: With true dreams that came like the break of dawn
With a voice calling him from the Kaʿba
With a written scroll brought by an angel
With a vision during a trade journey
srm-032.e: ʿĀʾisha reports that it began with true dreams, each one coming true like daybreak; then seclusion was made dear to him and he retreated to Ḥirāʾ.

srm-033.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy, hadith of ʿĀʾisha
srm-033.q: Who was Waraqa ibn Nawfal, to whom Khadīja took the Prophet after the first revelation?
o: Her cousin, a Christian who knew the earlier scriptures
Her brother, a merchant of Quraysh
Her servant, who had travelled with the Prophet
srm-033.e: Waraqa was the son of Khadīja's paternal uncle; he had become a Christian in the time before Islam, wrote from the Gospel and was by then old and blind.

srm-034.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy, hadith of ʿĀʾisha
srm-034.q: When the Prophet came home frightened from Ḥirāʾ, which quality of his did Khadīja mention to reassure him?
o: That he kept the ties of kinship
That he led the caravans of Quraysh
That he was the finest poet of Mecca
That he owned great wealth from trade
srm-034.e: Khadīja said God would never disgrace him, because he kept ties of kinship, bore the burden of the weak, helped the destitute, honoured guests and supported people in true hardship.

srm-035.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the first to accept Islam
srm-035.q: Who is counted as the first boy to accept Islam?
srm-035.e: ʿAlī was living in the Prophet's household as a child and believed early on. Ibn ʿAbbās and Usāma were born later, around or after the Hijra period.

srm-036.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the secret phase of the call
srm-036.q: Which house near al-Ṣafā served as a meeting place for the early Muslims during the secret phase?
o: The house of ʿAbdullāh ibn Judʿān
srm-036.e: The Prophet met his followers to teach them in the house of al-Arqam ibn Abī al-Arqam. Dār al-Nadwa was the council house of Quraysh where the Hijra plot was later hatched.

srm-037.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ
srm-037.q: After the verse shown was revealed, where did the Prophet stand to call the clans of Quraysh?
srm-037.e: The verse commanded him to warn his nearest kinsfolk; he climbed al-Ṣafā and called the clans by name, asking whether they would believe him if he warned of an army behind the hill (al-Bukhārī).

srm-038.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the persecution of the weak Muslims
srm-038.q: Who is known as the first martyr in Islam?
o: Sumayya bint Khayyāṭ, mother of ʿAmmār
srm-038.e: Sumayya, wife of Yāsir and mother of ʿAmmār, was killed in Mecca for refusing to renounce Islam. Bilāl survived his torture; Ḥamza and Muṣʿab fell later at Uḥud.

srm-039.src: Musnad Aḥmad, hadith of Umm Salama on the emigration to Abyssinia
srm-039.q: Who spoke on behalf of the Muslim emigrants before al-Najāshī?
srm-039.e: In the report of Umm Salama, the emigrants chose Jaʿfar to answer the king; he described their former ignorance, the message of the Prophet and the persecution they suffered.

srm-040.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the boycott document
srm-040.q: Where were Banū Hāshim confined during the boycott imposed by Quraysh?
srm-040.e: Quraysh agreed not to marry, trade or deal with Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib, who withdrew into the ravine of Abū Ṭālib in Mecca and suffered great hunger there.

srm-041.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the journey to al-Ṭāʾif
srm-041.q: Who accompanied the Prophet on his journey to al-Ṭāʾif?
srm-041.e: Most biographers name Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, his freedman and adopted son, who shielded him from the stones thrown by the people of al-Ṭāʾif.

srm-042.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, how prayer was prescribed on the Night Journey
srm-042.q: What was prescribed for the Muslims during the Miʿrāj?
srm-042.e: The prayers were first prescribed as fifty and reduced, at the Prophet's repeated request, to five, keeping the reward of fifty (al-Bukhārī). Fasting, zakāt and ḥajj were prescribed later in Medina.

srm-043.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the first pledge of al-ʿAqaba
srm-043.q: How many men from Yathrib took the first pledge of al-ʿAqaba?
srm-043.e: The year before, six men of Khazraj had accepted Islam; the following season twelve men took the first pledge. About seventy-three men and two women came to the second pledge.

srm-044.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, the Hijra of the Prophet
srm-044.q: What happened to Surāqa ibn Mālik when he pursued the Prophet during the Hijra?
o: His horse's legs sank into the ground
He was captured by Banū Aslam
He lost the trail in the cave of Thawr
His horse threw him into a well
srm-044.e: Surāqa set out for the reward Quraysh had offered; as he drew near, his horse's forelegs sank into the ground more than once, and he asked for a written assurance of safety and turned back (al-Bukhārī).

srm-045.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the affair of the Elephant
srm-045.q: In whose name did Abraha govern Yemen when he marched on Mecca?
srm-045.e: Abraha was an Abyssinian commander ruling Yemen as viceroy of the Negus after Aksum had conquered the Ḥimyarite kingdom. Persia took Yemen only some years later.

srm-046.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the digging of Zamzam
srm-046.q: For which deed is ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib especially remembered in the history of Mecca?
o: He rediscovered and re-dug the well of Zamzam
He founded the council house Dār al-Nadwa
He introduced the two seasonal caravan journeys
He was the first to place a covering on the Kaʿba
srm-046.e: Guided by a dream, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib located and re-dug the long-buried well of Zamzam. Dār al-Nadwa is attributed to Quṣayy and the caravan journeys to Hāshim.

srm-047.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Nikāḥ, foster relations through nursing
srm-047.q: Before Ḥalīma, which woman briefly nursed the infant Prophet?
o: Thuwayba, a freedwoman of Abū Lahab
Fāṭima bint Asad, wife of Abū Ṭālib
srm-047.e: Thuwayba nursed him for a short time; she had also nursed Ḥamza and Abū Salama, which made them his foster brothers (al-Bukhārī). Umm Ayman cared for him but did not nurse him.

srm-048.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the children of the Prophet
srm-048.q: Which of the Prophet's children was NOT born to Khadīja?
srm-048.e: All his children were from Khadīja except Ibrāhīm, who was born to Māriya in Medina and died in infancy. al-Qāsim, after whom he was called Abū al-Qāsim, was Khadīja's son.

srm-049.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, the virtue of Mecca and its building
srm-049.q: Why did Quraysh leave part of the original Kaʿba (the Ḥijr) outside the walls when they rebuilt it?
o: Their lawful funds were not enough to complete it
The ground there was too rocky to build on
An idol stood there that they would not move
Abraha's army had destroyed that part beyond repair
srm-049.e: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet told her Quraysh ran short of means (al-Bukhārī); the biographers add that they had resolved to use only wealth of good origin. So the semicircular Ḥijr remained outside.

srm-050.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy, hadith of ʿĀʾisha
srm-050.q: How did Waraqa ibn Nawfal identify the being who had come to the Prophet in Ḥirāʾ?
o: As the same Nāmūs (angel of revelation) sent to Mūsā
As a jinn of the kind that inspires poets
As the spirit of an earlier king of Mecca
As a vision caused by long fasting
srm-050.e: Waraqa said it was the Nāmūs that God had sent down to Moses, i.e. Jibrīl, the bearer of revelation. Quraysh later accused the Prophet of being a poet or possessed, which Waraqa's answer contradicts.

srm-051.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Muddaththir, hadith of Jābir
srm-051.q: According to the hadith of Jābir in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, when was the passage beginning with the verse shown revealed?
o: After a pause in revelation that followed the events of Ḥirāʾ
On the night of al-Isrāʾ wa-l-Miʿrāj
During the boycott in Shiʿb Abī Ṭālib
On the night of the second pledge of al-ʿAqaba
srm-051.e: Jābir reports that the Prophet saw the angel of Ḥirāʾ again between heaven and earth after the revelation had paused, and then the opening of al-Muddaththir came down. The majority hold that al-ʿAlaq preceded it.

srm-052.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, hadith of Jundub
srm-052.q: The verse shown reassured the Prophet. According to the report of Jundub in al-Bukhārī, what was the occasion?
o: A delay in revelation, after which a woman taunted that he had been abandoned
His rejection by the leaders of al-Ṭāʾif
The death of his uncle Abū Ṭālib
The hunger of the boycott in Shiʿb Abī Ṭālib
srm-052.e: Jundub reports that when the Prophet did not rise for prayer for a night or two and revelation was delayed, a woman of Quraysh mocked that his companion had left him; Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā then came down.

srm-053.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 15:94; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the open call
srm-053.q: In the sīra literature, the verse shown is commonly cited as marking which turning point?
o: The move from secret to open preaching
The order to emigrate to Abyssinia
srm-053.e: Ibn Isḥāq and the exegetes link the verse to the end of the roughly three-year secret phase, when the Prophet was commanded to proclaim the message openly. Fighting and the qibla change belong to the Medinan period.

srm-054.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 16:106; al-Wāḥidī, Asbāb al-Nuzūl
srm-054.q: The verse shown excuses one who is coerced into words of disbelief while his heart is firm in faith. Which Companion do the exegetes name as its occasion?
srm-054.e: Under torture after his parents were killed, ʿAmmār said what his tormentors demanded and came to the Prophet in distress; he was reassured, and the exegetes cite this verse in connection with him.

srm-055.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the conversion of ʿUmar
srm-055.q: In whose house was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb moved by hearing the Quran before he accepted Islam?
o: His sister Fāṭima and her husband Saʿīd ibn Zayd
srm-055.e: According to Ibn Isḥāq, ʿUmar burst into his sister's house, struck her, then read the opening of Sūrat Ṭā Hā from a sheet and went to the Prophet at Dār al-Arqam to accept Islam.

srm-056.src: Musnad Aḥmad, hadith of Umm Salama on the emigration to Abyssinia
srm-056.q: When al-Najāshī asked to hear something of the revelation, from which sūra did Jaʿfar recite?
srm-056.e: Jaʿfar recited the opening of Sūrat Maryam, about Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, Maryam and ʿĪsā; the king wept until his beard was wet, as did his bishops. Āl ʿImrān is a Medinan sūra.

srm-057.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, announcing a death and praying over the absent
srm-057.q: What did the Prophet do in Medina on the day al-Najāshī died?
o: He announced his death and led a funeral prayer for him in absentia
He sent Jaʿfar back to Abyssinia to bury him
He declared three days of mourning in Medina
He wrote to the new king demanding the Muslims' return
srm-057.e: al-Bukhārī reports that he announced the Negus's death on the day he died, went out with the Companions to the prayer place and prayed over him with four takbīrs.

srm-058.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the annulment of the boycott document
srm-058.q: What, according to the sīra reports, had happened to the boycott document hung in the Kaʿba when it was taken down?
o: Termites had eaten it except the words naming God
It had been stolen by a Hāshimite youth
Rain had washed the writing away completely
It had been burnt in a fire at the Kaʿba
srm-058.e: The Prophet told Abū Ṭālib that the document had been consumed except where God's name was written; when Quraysh checked, they found it so, which helped bring the boycott to an end.

srm-059.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the journey to al-Ṭāʾif
srm-059.q: Who was ʿAddās, whom the Prophet met in a garden outside al-Ṭāʾif?
o: A Christian servant from Nineveh who brought him grapes
A chief of Thaqīf who apologised to him
A Jewish scholar who recognised his description
A shepherd who guided him back to Mecca
srm-059.e: The sons of Rabīʿa sent their servant ʿAddās with grapes; when he learned that the Prophet knew of Yūnus of Nineveh, ʿAddās kissed his head and hands.

srm-060.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Khalq, hadith of ʿĀʾisha on the hardest day
srm-060.q: After al-Ṭāʾif, the angel of the mountains offered to crush its people between the two mountains. How did the Prophet answer?
o: He hoped God would bring from their descendants people who worship Him alone
He accepted and asked for a sign first
He asked that only their leaders be punished
He asked for the punishment to be delayed one year
srm-060.e: In ʿĀʾisha's report the Prophet called this his hardest day; yet he declined the offer, hoping their offspring would worship God without partners. Thaqīf did enter Islam in 9 AH.

srm-061.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt, how prayer was prescribed on the Night Journey
srm-061.q: During the Miʿrāj, which prophet urged the Prophet to return and ask for the number of prayers to be reduced?
srm-061.e: On his way back, Mūsā told him his community would not manage fifty prayers, drawing on his experience with the Children of Israel, and he returned repeatedly until they were five.

srm-062.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the first pledge of al-ʿAqaba
srm-062.q: Whom did the Prophet send to Yathrib after the first pledge of al-ʿAqaba to teach the Quran and Islam?
srm-062.e: Muṣʿab, a young man of Quraysh, taught in Yathrib and was called al-Muqriʾ; leading men such as Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr accepted Islam through him.

srm-063.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the arrival at Qubāʾ
srm-063.q: Which mosque did the Prophet found on arrival at the edge of Yathrib, before entering the town itself?
o: The mosque of the two qiblas
srm-063.e: He first stayed at Qubāʾ with Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf and founded its mosque, commonly called the first mosque built in Islam. The Prophet's Mosque was built after he moved into the town.

srm-064.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the council of Quraysh in Dār al-Nadwa
srm-064.q: Which plan against the Prophet did Quraysh adopt in Dār al-Nadwa shortly before the Hijra?
o: A young man from each clan would strike him together
He would be imprisoned in a locked house
He would be banished from Mecca for good
He would be handed over to Thaqīf
srm-064.e: On Abū Jahl's proposal, a strong youth from every clan was to strike him at once so that his blood would be spread among all the clans and Banū Hāshim could not take revenge. Imprisonment and exile were proposed and rejected.

srm-065.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's vow to sacrifice a son
srm-065.q: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had vowed to sacrifice one of his sons, and the lot fell on ʿAbdullāh. How, according to the sīra reports, was ʿAbdullāh ransomed?
o: With one hundred camels, after lots were cast repeatedly
With forty sheep slaughtered at the Kaʿba
With ten camels and a gift to the idol Hubal
With his weight in silver given to the poor
srm-065.e: Lots were cast between ʿAbdullāh and ten camels, and the number was raised by ten each time until the lot fell on the camels at one hundred. This is why the Prophet is sometimes called the son of the two sacrificial ones (Ismāʿīl and ʿAbdullāh).

srm-066.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the marriage of Hāshim and the birth of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib
srm-066.q: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's mother, Salmā bint ʿAmr, came from Yathrib. To which clan did she belong, giving the Prophet kinship ties there?
o: Banū ʿAdī ibn al-Najjār of the Khazraj
Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal of the Aws
Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf of the Aws
srm-066.e: Hāshim married Salmā of Banū ʿAdī ibn al-Najjār, and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib (Shayba) grew up in Yathrib. This is why Banū al-Najjār were called the maternal relatives of the Prophet's family.

srm-067.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Manāqib, the story of Khuzāʿa; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the idols of the Arabs
srm-067.q: Which man is described in the sīra as the first to alter the religion of Ibrāhīm in Mecca by introducing idols and the sāʾiba custom?
srm-067.e: Ibn Isḥāq reports that ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy of Khuzāʿa brought idols to Mecca, and al-Bukhārī records that he was the first to institute the sāʾiba (camels set free for idols). Quṣayy later took control of Mecca from Khuzāʿa.

srm-068.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, the account of Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl
srm-068.q: Which pre-Islamic seeker of the religion of Ibrāhīm refused to eat meat sacrificed to idols, died before the call began, and was the father of one of the ten promised Paradise?
srm-068.e: al-Bukhārī reports that Zayd ibn ʿAmr rejected idol sacrifices and sought the ḥanīf religion; his son Saʿīd ibn Zayd is among the ten. Waraqa became a Christian and lived to meet the Prophet after the first revelation.

srm-069.src: Ibn Kathīr, al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya, Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl; al-Suhaylī, al-Rawḍ al-Unuf
srm-069.q: Which incident is commonly reported as the trigger for Ḥilf al-Fuḍūl?
o: A merchant from Zabīd whose payment al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil withheld
The killing of a man of Thaqīf at the fair of ʿUkāẓ
A theft from the treasury of the Kaʿba
A quarrel between two clans over the well of Zamzam
srm-069.e: A trader from Zabīd in Yemen sold goods to al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who refused to pay; his appeal to Quraysh led several clans to meet in the house of ʿAbdullāh ibn Judʿān and pledge to uphold the rights of the wronged. The ʿUkāẓ killing belongs to the Fijār war.

srm-070.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the rebuilding of the Kaʿba
srm-070.q: When Quraysh feared to begin demolishing the old Kaʿba, who struck the first blow?
srm-070.e: Ibn Isḥāq reports that al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra of Makhzūm took up a pickaxe and began; the others waited a night, and when no harm befell him they joined in.

srm-071.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa's offer
srm-071.q: When ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa offered the Prophet wealth, leadership or a cure in return for abandoning his call, what was the Prophet's response?
o: He recited the opening of Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
He recited the whole of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn
He gave a speech on the unity of God
He walked away without a word
srm-071.e: According to Ibn Isḥāq, he listened to ʿUtba to the end and then recited the opening of Fuṣṣilat; ʿUtba returned to Quraysh shaken and advised them to leave him alone.

srm-072.src: Musnad Aḥmad, hadith of Umm Salama on the emigration to Abyssinia
srm-072.q: Which two envoys did Quraysh send to al-Najāshī to have the emigrants handed back?
o: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa
Abū Sufyān and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr
Abū Jahl and Umayya ibn Khalaf
Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl
srm-072.e: In Umm Salama's account, Quraysh sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa with gifts for the king and his patriarchs, but al-Najāshī refused to surrender the Muslims after hearing Jaʿfar.

srm-073.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, the first emigration to Abyssinia; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya
srm-073.q: Why did some of the first emigrants to Abyssinia return to Mecca after a few months?
o: They heard a false report that Quraysh had accepted Islam
Al-Najāshī expelled them under pressure from Quraysh
A war broke out between Abyssinia and Yemen
The Prophet called them back for the pledge of al-ʿAqaba
srm-073.e: The first emigration, commonly dated to Rajab of the fifth year of prophethood, was cut short by a rumour that Quraysh had embraced Islam. Finding it untrue, most returned, and a larger second emigration followed.

srm-074.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the annulment of the boycott document
srm-074.q: Which Meccan is credited by Ibn Isḥāq with starting the effort among Quraysh to annul the boycott document?
srm-074.e: Hishām ibn ʿAmr, who had secretly brought food into the ravine, won over Zuhayr ibn Abī Umayya, al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī, Abū al-Bakhtarī and Zamʿa ibn al-Aswad, and together they publicly demanded that the document be torn up.

srm-075.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the return from al-Ṭāʾif
srm-075.q: Under whose protection (jiwār) did the Prophet re-enter Mecca after returning from al-Ṭāʾif?
srm-075.e: al-Akhnas and Suhayl declined to grant protection; al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī agreed and stood armed with his sons at the Kaʿba while the Prophet performed ṭawāf. The Prophet later remembered this kindness.

srm-076.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, chapter on the Miʿrāj
srm-076.q: Which statement best describes the dating of al-Isrāʾ wa-l-Miʿrāj in the classical sources?
o: Its year and month are disputed; 27 Rajab is widespread but not agreed upon
Sound hadith fix it at 27 Rajab of the tenth year of prophethood
All scholars place it in Ramaḍān of the first year of prophethood
It took place in Medina in the year after the Hijra
srm-076.e: Ibn Ḥajar lists many different views on its year and month. The popular date of 27 Rajab has no agreement among the scholars. It certainly took place in Mecca before the Hijra.

srm-077.src: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Kitāb al-Īmān, on Sidrat al-Muntahā, hadith of Ibn Masʿūd
srm-077.q: According to Ibn Masʿūd's report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, besides the five prayers, what else was the Prophet given on the night of the Miʿrāj?
o: The closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqara
srm-077.e: Ibn Masʿūd reports three gifts: the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness of grave sins for those of his community who associate nothing with God.

srm-078.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the second pledge of al-ʿAqaba
srm-078.q: Who from the Prophet's family attended the second pledge of al-ʿAqaba while not yet a Muslim, to make sure his nephew would be protected?
srm-078.e: Ibn Isḥāq reports that al-ʿAbbās spoke first, telling the people of Yathrib to protect the Prophet fully or leave him among his own clan. Abū Ṭālib had already died, and Ḥamza was a Muslim by then.

srm-079.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the second pledge of al-ʿAqaba and the twelve leaders
srm-079.q: At the second pledge of al-ʿAqaba the Prophet asked for twelve representatives (nuqabāʾ). How were they divided between the two tribes of Yathrib?
o: Nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws
Six from the Khazraj and six from the Aws
Three from the Khazraj and nine from the Aws
Ten from the Khazraj and two from the Aws
srm-079.e: Ibn Isḥāq lists nine nuqabāʾ of the Khazraj, such as Asʿad ibn Zurāra, and three of the Aws, such as Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr. The split ten and two is the commonly reported make-up of the first pledge, not of the nuqabāʾ.

srm-080.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, the Hijra of the Prophet; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya
srm-080.q: Who guided the Prophet and Abū Bakr along the route to Yathrib after the cave of Thawr?
o: ʿAbdullāh ibn Urayqiṭ, a hired guide not yet Muslim
ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, who grazed the sheep
ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, who brought the news
Surāqa ibn Mālik, after he turned back
srm-080.e: al-Bukhārī describes a skilled guide of Banū al-Dīl who still followed the religion of Quraysh, hired and trusted with the two camels; Ibn Isḥāq names him ʿAbdullāh ibn Urayqiṭ (or Arqaṭ). ʿĀmir rode with them, but the guide led the way.

srd-001.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, arrival at Qubāʾ
srd-001.q: Which mosque did the Prophet establish first after his hijra, before entering Medina proper?
srd-001.e: The Prophet stayed some days at Qubāʾ on the outskirts of Medina and founded its mosque there; the Prophet's Mosque in the town centre was built after he moved on.

srd-002.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, arrival in Medina
srd-002.q: When the Prophet's camel knelt in Medina, in whose house did he stay until his own rooms were built?
srd-002.e: The camel knelt near the house of Abū Ayyūb Khālid ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī, and the Prophet lodged with him until the mosque and its rooms were completed.

srd-003.q: The verse shown commanded the change of the qibla. From which direction did the Muslims turn, and towards which?
srd-003.e: In Medina the Muslims first prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem); the verse shown ordered them to face al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, the Kaʿba in Mecca.

srd-004.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Badr
srd-004.q: In which year after the hijra did the Battle of Badr take place?
srd-004.e: Badr took place in Ramaḍān of the second year after the hijra; Uḥud followed in 3 AH.

srd-005.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat al-Khandaq
srd-005.q: Which companion is reported to have suggested digging a trench to defend Medina against the Confederates?
srd-005.e: Salmān, who came from Persia, knew the trench as a Persian defence; the battle took its name al-Khandaq (the Trench) from it.

srd-006.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb qatl Ḥamza
srd-006.q: Which uncle of the Prophet was martyred at the Battle of Uḥud?
srd-006.e: Ḥamza, called the Lion of Allah, was killed at Uḥud by Waḥshī's spear; al-ʿAbbās outlived the Prophet, and Abū Ṭālib had died in Mecca before the hijra.

srd-007.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, fatḥ Makka
srd-007.q: In which year after the hijra was Mecca conquered?
srd-007.e: The conquest of Mecca took place in Ramaḍān 8 AH, two years after the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya (6 AH).

srd-008.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, ḥadīth Jābir on the Prophet's Hajj
srd-008.q: In which year did the Prophet perform the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ)?
srd-008.e: The Prophet performed his only Hajj after the hijra in 10 AH and passed away a few months later, in 11 AH.

srd-009.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Manāqib, bāb wafāt al-Nabī
srd-009.q: According to the best-known report in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, at what age did the Prophet pass away?
srd-009.e: ʿĀʾisha and others report that he died aged sixty-three; reports of sixty or sixty-five exist but the majority follow sixty-three.

srd-010.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, bāb mā jāʾa fī qabr al-Nabī
o: At the foot of Mount Uḥud
srd-010.e: He was buried in the room of ʿĀʾisha where he died, next to the mosque; Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were later buried beside him.

srd-011.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the Anṣār
srd-011.q: The Anṣār (Helpers) of Medina came from which two Arab tribes?
srd-011.e: The Anṣār were the Aws and the Khazraj, the two Arab tribes of Yathrib who welcomed the Prophet and the emigrants.

srd-012.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, bad' al-adhān
srd-012.q: Who was the first muʾadhdhin of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina?
srd-012.e: Bilāl was chosen to call the adhān because of his strong voice; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd saw the wording in a dream, and Ibn Umm Maktūm also called the adhān later.

srd-013.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, Fāṭima bint Rasūl Allāh
srd-013.q: Whom did Fāṭima, the daughter of the Prophet, marry in Medina?
srd-013.e: Fāṭima married ʿAlī in the early Medinan years; ʿUthmān married her sisters Ruqayya and Umm Kulthūm, and Abū al-ʿĀṣ was the husband of her sister Zaynab.

srd-014.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, wives of the Prophet
srd-014.q: Which Mother of the Believers was the daughter of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq?
srd-014.e: ʿĀʾisha was the daughter of Abū Bakr; Ḥafṣa was the daughter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

srd-015.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, wives of the Prophet
srd-015.q: Ḥafṣa, a Mother of the Believers, was the daughter of which companion?
srd-015.e: Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar married the Prophet after her first husband died following Badr; the written ṣuḥuf of the Quran compiled under Abū Bakr were later kept with her.

srd-016.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, al-muʾākhāt bayn al-Muhājirīn wa-l-Anṣār
srd-016.q: What was the muʾākhāt that the Prophet established after arriving in Medina?
o: A pact of brotherhood pairing emigrants with Anṣār
A written treaty with the Jewish clans of Medina
A pledge of allegiance by the Anṣār at ʿAqaba
A military alliance with the tribes around Mecca
srd-016.e: In the muʾākhāt the Prophet paired individual Muhājirūn with individual Anṣār as brothers who supported one another; the treaty with the Jews was the Ṣaḥīfa, and the pledges before the hijra were the pledges of ʿAqaba.

srd-017.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Muʾta
srd-017.q: Which companion did the Prophet call 'one of the swords of Allah' when he took command at the Battle of Muʾta?
srd-017.e: After the three appointed commanders fell at Muʾta, Khālid took the banner and withdrew the army safely; the Prophet described him as a sword among the swords of Allah, as in al-Bukhārī.

srd-018.src: al-Tirmidhī, Jāmiʿ, Kitāb al-Manāqib, ḥadīth al-ʿashara
srd-018.q: Which of these companions is among the ten named together in the well-known hadith of those promised Paradise?
srd-018.e: The ten are Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Saʿīd ibn Zayd and Abū ʿUbayda; the others are great companions but not in this list.

srd-019.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-019.q: What happened at al-Ḥudaybiya in 6 AH?
o: A truce was agreed with Quraysh without fighting
The Muslims won a battle against Quraysh
Mecca opened its gates to the Muslims
The Muslims performed ʿumra that same year
srd-019.e: The Muslims set out for ʿumra but were stopped at al-Ḥudaybiya; instead of fighting, a truce was concluded, and the ʿumra was made up the following year.

srd-020.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Tabūk
srd-020.q: Against which power was the expedition of Tabūk (9 AH) directed?
o: The Byzantines and their Arab allies
The Persians of the Sasanian empire
srd-020.e: Tabūk lies on the route to Syria; the army marched against the Byzantines and their allied Arab tribes, but no battle took place.

srd-021.q: The highlighted word names a battle. Which one?
srd-021.e: The verse shown reminds the believers that Allah granted them victory at Badr while they were few and weak; it comes within the passage about Uḥud.

srd-022.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān
srd-022.q: Why was ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān called Dhū al-Nūrayn ('the possessor of two lights')?
o: He married two daughters of the Prophet
He emigrated to Abyssinia and Medina
He built two mosques in Medina
srd-022.e: ʿUthmān married Ruqayya, and after her death Umm Kulthūm, both daughters of the Prophet. He did emigrate twice, but the title refers to the two marriages.

srd-023.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn
srd-023.q: Who was the mother of the Prophet's grandsons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn?
srd-023.e: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn were the sons of ʿAlī and Fāṭima, the Prophet's youngest daughter.

srd-024.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, arrival in Medina
srd-024.q: According to Ibn Isḥāq, where did the Prophet lead the first Friday prayer after the hijra?
o: Among Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf, on the way from Qubāʾ
In the newly finished Prophet's Mosque in Medina
In the mosque of Qubāʾ, on the day he left it
At the house of Abū Ayyūb, where he lodged
srd-024.e: Ibn Isḥāq reports that the Friday caught the Prophet among Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf as he rode from Qubāʾ into Medina, and he led the Jumuʿa there in their valley; the Prophet's Mosque did not yet exist.

srd-025.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Manāqib al-Anṣār, bāb hijrat al-Nabī
srd-025.q: To whom did the plot of land on which the Prophet's Mosque was built belong?
o: Two orphan boys, Sahl and Suhayl
The Jewish clan of Banū Qaynuqāʿ
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl
srd-025.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that the site was a date-drying yard of two orphans, Sahl and Suhayl, in the care of Asʿad ibn Zurāra; the Prophet declined it as a gift and paid for it.

srd-026.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Buyūʿ, opening chapter
srd-026.q: With which of the Anṣār was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf paired in the muʾākhāt?
srd-026.e: Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ offered to share his wealth with him; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān thanked him and asked to be shown the market. Abū al-Dardāʾ was the brother of Salmān al-Fārisī.

srd-027.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, kitāb al-Nabī bayn al-Muhājirīn wa-l-Anṣār (the Ṣaḥīfa)
srd-027.q: According to the Ṣaḥīfa (Constitution) of Medina, to whom were serious disputes among its parties to be referred?
o: To a council of the tribal chiefs
To the rabbis of the Jewish clans
To the leader of the Khazraj
srd-027.e: The document states that any dispute feared to lead to corruption is to be referred to Allah and to Muḥammad, which made the Prophet the final arbiter in Medina.

srd-028.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, taḥwīl al-qibla
srd-028.q: Which mosque in Medina is known by a name recalling that a prayer there was turned from one qibla to the other?
srd-028.e: Al-Qiblatayn means 'the two qiblas'; it is associated in the sīra with Banū Salima, where the change of direction is reported to have reached the worshippers during prayer.

srd-029.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān, bāb al-ṣalāt min al-īmān (ḥadīth al-Barāʾ)
srd-029.q: According to the hadith of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib in al-Bukhārī, how long did the Muslims in Medina pray towards Jerusalem before the change of qibla?
srd-029.e: Al-Barāʾ reports sixteen or seventeen months, with the narrator unsure which; the change therefore falls in the second year after the hijra.

srd-030.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb ʿiddat aṣḥāb Badr
srd-030.q: Roughly how many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
srd-030.e: Al-Barāʾ reports that the people of Badr were three hundred and some ten men, the same number as the companions of Ṭālūt who crossed the river; Quraysh were around three times as many.

srd-031.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Badr
srd-031.q: What was the original aim of the Muslims when they set out in the events leading to Badr?
o: To intercept the Qurayshī caravan led by Abū Sufyān
To defend Medina against an approaching army
To perform ʿumra at the Kaʿba in Mecca
To punish the tribe of Ghaṭafān for a raid
srd-031.e: They went out to meet the trade caravan returning from Syria under Abū Sufyān; he changed route and called Quraysh to arms, so a battle took place instead.

srd-032.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Farḍ al-Khumus, bāb man lam yukhammis al-aslāb
srd-032.q: According to al-Bukhārī, who struck down Abū Jahl at Badr?
o: Two young Anṣārī men, both named Muʿādh
Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib in a duel
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib in single combat
Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ and a group of Anṣār
srd-032.e: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf reports that two Anṣārī youths, Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ, attacked Abū Jahl; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd found him dying afterwards. Bilāl killed Umayya ibn Khalaf.

srd-033.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Uḥud
srd-033.q: Whom did the Prophet put in command of the archers on the hill at Uḥud?
srd-033.e: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr commanded the fifty archers and was ordered not to leave the position whatever happened; most of them left when they thought the battle won, and he remained and was killed.

srd-034.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Uḥud
srd-034.q: What did ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy do on the way to Uḥud?
o: He withdrew with about a third of the army
He led the right wing of the Muslims
He warned Quraysh of the Muslim plan
He stayed in Medina from the start
srd-034.e: Ibn Isḥāq reports that he turned back with roughly a third of the men, objecting that his advice to fight from inside Medina had not been followed; about seven hundred continued with the Prophet.

srd-035.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Uḥud
srd-035.q: Which companion carried the Muslim banner at Uḥud and was martyred there, leaving so little that his shroud did not cover him fully?
srd-035.e: Muṣʿab, who had been the Prophet's first envoy to Medina, carried the banner and fell; al-Bukhārī reports that his garment covered either his head or his feet. Ḥanẓala is known as the one washed by the angels.

srd-036.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, amr Banī Qaynuqāʿ
srd-036.q: Which Jewish tribe of Medina was the first to be expelled, shortly after Badr?
srd-036.e: After Badr the Banū Qaynuqāʿ broke their covenant and were besieged; following the intercession of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy they were allowed to leave. Banū al-Naḍīr followed later, and Qurayẓa after al-Khandaq.

srd-037.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat al-Khandaq
srd-037.q: During the siege of al-Khandaq, which newly converted man of Ghaṭafān secretly sowed mistrust between Quraysh, Ghaṭafān and Banū Qurayẓa?
srd-037.e: Nuʿaym's Islam was not yet known, so both sides trusted him and he set them against each other. Ḥudhayfa was the scout sent into the enemy camp; Ḥuyayy had persuaded Qurayẓa to break their pact.

srd-038.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, marjiʿ al-Nabī min al-Aḥzāb
srd-038.q: Whose judgement did Banū Qurayẓa accept after the siege that followed al-Khandaq?
o: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, chief of the Aws
Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda, chief of the Khazraj
srd-038.e: Qurayẓa were allies of the Aws, so they agreed to the judgement of the Aws chief Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, who had been wounded at the Trench and died soon afterwards.

srd-039.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-039.q: Who negotiated and concluded the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya on behalf of Quraysh?
srd-039.e: Several envoys came, including ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd, but the treaty was concluded with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr. Abū Sufyān only came to Medina later, to try to renew the truce.

srd-040.q: The verse shown praises the pledge made under the tree (Bayʿat al-Riḍwān). What prompted this pledge?
o: A rumour that ʿUthmān had been killed in Mecca
News that Quraysh had seized the caravan
The death of the Prophet's envoy at Muʾta
srd-040.e: ʿUthmān had been sent to Quraysh as envoy and was delayed; when it was rumoured he had been killed, the companions pledged themselves to the Prophet under the tree.

srd-041.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, amr al-Ḥudaybiya
srd-041.q: For how long was fighting suspended under the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya, according to the sīra sources?
srd-041.e: Ibn Isḥāq gives the truce as ten years; it ended early when Quraysh's allies, Banū Bakr, attacked Khuzāʿa, the allies of the Muslims.

srd-042.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Khaybar
srd-042.q: Which group of emigrants returned and joined the Prophet at the time of the conquest of Khaybar?
o: Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and the emigrants to Abyssinia
The Muslims who had been held back in Mecca
The delegation of Thaqīf from al-Ṭāʾif
The Anṣār who had gone trading in Syria
srd-042.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that Jaʿfar and the last emigrants to Abyssinia, joined by Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī's people, reached the Prophet at Khaybar, and he was overjoyed at their arrival.

srd-043.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Muʾta
srd-043.q: Whom did the Prophet appoint as the first commander of the army sent to Muʾta?
srd-043.e: He appointed Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, and if he fell, Jaʿfar, and then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa; all three were martyred, and Khālid then took the banner without prior appointment.

srd-044.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, fatḥ Makka
srd-044.q: What event broke the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya and led to the conquest of Mecca?
o: Banū Bakr, aided by Quraysh, attacked Khuzāʿa
Quraysh killed the Muslim envoy to Mecca
Quraysh refused the Muslims' ʿumra of 7 AH
Banū Qurayẓa allied themselves with Quraysh
srd-044.e: Khuzāʿa had joined the Muslims' side and Banū Bakr the side of Quraysh; when Banū Bakr attacked Khuzāʿa with Qurayshī help, the truce was broken. The ʿumra of 7 AH took place as agreed.

srd-045.q: The highlighted word names a battle in which the Muslims at first were impressed by their own large numbers. Against which tribe was it chiefly fought?
srd-045.e: Ḥunayn (8 AH) was fought against Hawāzin, joined by Thaqīf; the Muslims, about twelve thousand, were first thrown back before Allah granted them victory, as the verse shown recalls.

srd-046.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Tabūk wa-hiya ghazwat al-ʿUsra
srd-046.q: By what name is the army of Tabūk known, because of the heat, distance and lack of means?
srd-046.e: Al-Bukhārī titles the chapter 'the expedition of Tabūk, which is the expedition of al-ʿUsra'; ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān is well known for equipping a large part of this army.

srd-047.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy, ḥadīth Abī Sufyān maʿa Hiraql
srd-047.q: Which companion carried the Prophet's letter to the Byzantine emperor Heraclius?
srd-047.e: Diḥya brought the letter to the governor of Buṣrā, who passed it to Heraclius. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfa went to Kisrā, ʿAmr ibn Umayya to the Negus, and Ḥāṭib to al-Muqawqis.

srd-048.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, sanat al-wufūd
srd-048.q: Which year is known as the 'Year of Delegations' (ʿĀm al-Wufūd)?
srd-048.e: After the conquest of Mecca and the return from Tabūk, delegations from across Arabia came to Medina, above all in 9 AH, which the sīra therefore calls the Year of Delegations.

srd-049.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Adhān, bāb ḥadd al-marīḍ an yashhad al-jamāʿa
srd-049.q: Whom did the Prophet instruct to lead the people in prayer during his final illness?
srd-049.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that the Prophet insisted that Abū Bakr lead the prayer, even when ʿĀʾisha suggested someone else; many companions later saw this as a sign of his precedence.

srd-050.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-050.q: At al-Ḥudaybiya the companions hesitated to sacrifice and shave. Which Mother of the Believers advised the Prophet to do it himself first without speaking to anyone?
srd-050.e: Umm Salama advised him to go out, slaughter his animal and call his barber; when the companions saw him do so, they all followed. Al-Bukhārī records this in the long hadith of the treaty.

srd-051.src: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām, Kitāb al-Amwāl; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya
srd-051.q: Besides the sīra of Ibn Isḥāq (in Ibn Hishām's recension), which classical work on public finance preserves a version of the Ṣaḥīfa of Medina?
srd-051.e: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām cites the document in Kitāb al-Amwāl with its own chain, independent of Ibn Isḥāq, which helps historians compare the two versions.

srd-052.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Badr
srd-052.q: According to Ibn Isḥāq, which companion asked at Badr whether the chosen camp was revelation or opinion, and then advised moving to the nearest well?
srd-052.e: Al-Ḥubāb asked whether the position was by revelation; told it was opinion and strategy, he proposed camping at the well nearest the enemy and stopping up the others, and the Prophet accepted. Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and al-Miqdād are known for their speeches pledging to fight.

srd-053.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Jihād, bāb mā yukrah min al-tanāzuʿ (ḥadīth al-Barāʾ)
srd-053.q: According to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib in al-Bukhārī, what were the losses of the Meccan polytheists at Badr?
o: One hundred killed and forty captured
srd-053.e: Al-Barāʾ reports that at Badr the polytheists lost one hundred and forty: seventy killed and seventy taken prisoner; fourteen is the commonly cited number of Muslim martyrs at Badr.

srd-054.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar, bāb al-imdād bi-l-malāʾika fī ghazwat Badr
srd-054.q: The verse shown was revealed concerning the prisoners of Badr. Which statement correctly describes the consultation that preceded it?
o: Abū Bakr advised ransom, ʿUmar advised execution
ʿUmar advised ransom, Abū Bakr advised execution
Both advised releasing them without ransom
The Anṣār alone were consulted and chose ransom
srd-054.e: In the report of Ibn ʿAbbās from ʿUmar in Muslim, Abū Bakr inclined to accepting ransom, hoping the captives might accept Islam, while ʿUmar advised executing the leaders; the Prophet took the ransom view and the verse shown was then revealed.

srd-055.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Uḥud
srd-055.q: At Uḥud, who led the Qurayshī cavalry that came round behind the Muslims once the archers had left the hill?
srd-055.e: Khālid, then still a polytheist, commanded the cavalry on the Qurayshī flank and exploited the gap left by the archers; Abū Sufyān was the overall leader of Quraysh.

srd-056.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad
srd-056.q: What was the expedition of Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad?
o: A pursuit of Quraysh the day after Uḥud
A raid on Banū Asad after al-Khandaq
A siege of a fortress of Khaybar
A patrol sent before the Battle of Badr
srd-056.e: The day after Uḥud the Prophet called out those who had fought, wounded as they were, and marched to Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad to show strength and deter Quraysh from returning to attack Medina.

srd-057.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Ḥashr
srd-057.q: The verse shown speaks of people of the Book driven from their homes at the 'first gathering'. Which tribe does it refer to, according to Ibn ʿAbbās?
srd-057.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that Ibn ʿAbbās called Sūrat al-Ḥashr 'the sūra of Banū al-Naḍīr'; they were expelled after plotting against the Prophet, and many settled in Khaybar.

srd-058.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-058.q: Which clause of the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya seemed most unfair to many companions?
o: Meccan converts were returned, but not the reverse
The Muslims had to pay a yearly tribute to Quraysh
The Muslims were barred from ʿumra for ten years
The Muslims had to hand Khuzāʿa over to Quraysh
srd-058.e: The treaty required the Muslims to send back anyone who came to them from Quraysh, while Quraysh did not have to return anyone who went to them; ʿUmar famously questioned this. There was no tribute, and ʿumra was allowed the following year.

srd-059.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-059.q: Who arrived in chains while the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya was being written and was returned to Mecca under its terms?
o: Abū Jandal, son of Suhayl ibn ʿAmr
Abū Baṣīr ʿUtba ibn Asīd al-Thaqafī
srd-059.e: Abū Jandal, a Muslim imprisoned by his father Suhayl, escaped to the Muslim camp; Suhayl insisted on the new clause and he was sent back. Abū Baṣīr escaped later, after the treaty, to Medina.

srd-060.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Muzāraʿa, bāb al-muzāraʿa bi-l-shaṭr
srd-060.q: After the conquest of Khaybar, on what terms were its Jewish inhabitants allowed to stay on the land?
o: They worked it in return for half of the produce
They bought it back for a fixed sum of money
They paid a fixed jizya for every adult man
They kept it without any obligation at all
srd-060.e: Ibn ʿUmar reports in al-Bukhārī that the Prophet left Khaybar to its people to work, for half of what it produced; jurists cite this as the basis for musāqāh and muzāraʿa contracts.

srd-061.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Khaybar
srd-061.q: Which Mother of the Believers came from among the captives of Khaybar and was freed by the Prophet, her freedom being her dowry?
srd-061.e: Ṣafiyya, daughter of the Banū al-Naḍīr leader Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, was freed and married, and Anas reports that her emancipation was her mahr. Juwayriya came from the campaign against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq.

srd-062.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Manāqib, manāqib Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib
srd-062.q: Ibn ʿUmar used to greet the son of a martyr of Muʾta as 'son of the one with two wings'. Who was that martyr?
srd-062.e: Jaʿfar lost both arms holding the banner at Muʾta; he is called al-Ṭayyār and Dhū al-Janāḥayn because, as reported, Allah gave him two wings in Paradise. Ibn ʿUmar greeted his son ʿAbd Allāh in this way.

srd-063.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat al-Fatḥ (ḥadīth ʿAlī)
srd-063.q: The verse shown was revealed when a companion secretly wrote to Quraysh about the Prophet's preparations for the march on Mecca. Who was he?
srd-063.e: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet sent him and others to intercept a woman carrying Ḥāṭib's letter; Ḥāṭib explained that he had wanted protection for his family in Mecca, and the Prophet accepted his excuse since he had fought at Badr.

srd-064.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ghazwat Ḥunayn
srd-064.q: Who commanded Hawāzin at Ḥunayn and brought their women, children and herds onto the battlefield?
srd-064.e: Mālik ibn ʿAwf hoped the families behind the lines would keep his men from fleeing; the aged Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma objected to this plan. Mālik later accepted Islam and was returned his family.

srd-065.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat al-Ṭāʾif
srd-065.q: After Ḥunayn some of the Anṣār were hurt that the spoils went mostly to newly reconciled Qurayshīs. What was the core of the Prophet's reply to them?
o: Others take sheep and camels home, they take the Messenger
They would be repaid later from the spoils of Khaybar
The Anṣār had not done the main fighting at Ḥunayn
The newcomers had been promised these spoils at Badr
srd-065.e: Al-Bukhārī reports the Prophet asking whether they were not content that people go home with sheep and camels while they go home with the Messenger of Allah; they wept and said they were content.

srd-066.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ḥadīth Kaʿb ibn Mālik
srd-066.q: The verse shown concerns three believers who stayed behind from Tabūk without excuse and were later forgiven. Which companion narrated the story at length?
srd-066.e: Kaʿb ibn Mālik, one of the three with Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ and Hilāl ibn Umayya, told the story of the boycott and the acceptance of their repentance in a long hadith in al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

srd-067.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat Tabūk
srd-067.q: Whom did the Prophet leave in charge of his family in Medina during Tabūk, telling him his position was like that of Hārūn to Mūsā?
srd-067.e: ʿAlī was unhappy to be left among women and children; the Prophet reassured him with the comparison to Hārūn, adding that there would be no prophet after him, as reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

srd-068.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb kitāb al-Nabī ilā Kisrā wa-Qayṣar
srd-068.q: Which ruler tore up the Prophet's letter, prompting the Prophet to pray that his kingdom be torn apart?
srd-068.e: Ibn ʿAbbās reports in al-Bukhārī that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfa al-Sahmī delivered the letter to Kisrā, who tore it up; Heraclius and al-Muqawqis received their letters with respect.

srd-069.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, qiṣṣat ahl Najrān
srd-069.q: The verse shown invites the other party to a mutual invocation of curse (mubāhala). Which delegation was it addressed to, according to the commentators?
srd-069.e: The delegation of Najrān came to Medina and debated about ʿĪsā; when invited to the mubāhala they declined and agreed to terms, and the Prophet sent Abū ʿUbayda with them as a trustworthy man, as in al-Bukhārī.

srd-070.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥāba, bāb qawl al-Nabī law kuntu muttakhidhan khalīlan
srd-070.q: Who recited the verse shown to the people on the day the Prophet died, calming them after ʿUmar had denied his death?
srd-070.e: Abū Bakr came from al-Sunḥ, saw the Prophet, then addressed the people: whoever worshipped Muḥammad, Muḥammad has died, and whoever worships Allah, Allah is alive; he then recited the verse shown, and people felt as if they had never heard it before.

srd-071.q: The highlighted word is the name of a companion. What distinction does he hold?
o: He is the only companion named in the Quran
He was the first man to accept Islam
He was the first martyr of Badr
He was the scribe of the Ṣaḥīfa of Medina
srd-071.e: Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, the Prophet's freed and formerly adopted son, is the only companion mentioned by name in the Quran; the verse shown ends the practice of treating adopted sons as natural sons in marriage law.

srd-072.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, ʿumrat al-qaḍāʾ; Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, Maymūna
srd-072.q: According to most biographers, which Mother of the Believers was the last woman the Prophet married, at the time of the ʿumra of 7 AH?
srd-072.e: The Prophet married Maymūna during ʿumrat al-qaḍāʾ in 7 AH, and the marriage was consummated at Sarif on the way back; Ṣafiyya and Umm Ḥabība had been married before her.

srd-073.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, jumlat al-ghazawāt; Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar, bāb ʿadad ghazawāt al-Nabī
srd-073.q: How many ghazawāt (expeditions led by the Prophet in person) does Ibn Isḥāq count in Ibn Hishām's recension, and in how many did fighting take place?
o: 27 expeditions, with fighting in all of them
srd-073.e: Ibn Hishām transmits from Ibn Isḥāq 27 ghazawāt, with fighting in nine (Badr, Uḥud, al-Khandaq, Qurayẓa, al-Muṣṭaliq, Khaybar, the Conquest, Ḥunayn, al-Ṭāʾif). Hadith reports give lower totals (e.g. Burayda in Muslim: nineteen, fighting in eight), and 38 is Ibn Hishām's count of sarāyā, the detachments sent under others.

srd-074.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ḥadīth al-ifk
srd-074.q: The verse shown begins the passage on the slander (al-ifk) against ʿĀʾisha. On the return from which expedition did the incident occur?
srd-074.e: ʿĀʾisha was left behind while looking for a lost necklace on the way back from the campaign against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq and was brought on by Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal. Al-Bukhārī notes that the date of that campaign is disputed (Ibn Isḥāq: 6 AH; Mūsā ibn ʿUqba: 4 AH).

srd-075.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb ghazwat al-Khandaq; Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, on that chapter
srd-075.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement over the date of al-Khandaq?
o: Most date it to 5 AH; Mūsā ibn ʿUqba dates it to 4 AH
Most date it to 4 AH; Ibn Isḥāq dates it to 6 AH
All agree on 5 AH; only the month is disputed
Most date it to 3 AH; al-Wāqidī dates it to 5 AH
srd-075.e: Ibn Isḥāq and most biographers place al-Khandaq in Shawwāl 5 AH, while al-Bukhārī cites Mūsā ibn ʿUqba for Shawwāl 4 AH. Ibn Ḥajar discusses ways of reconciling the reports, for example by a different start for counting the years.

srd-076.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, al-shurūṭ fī al-jihād
srd-076.q: How did the clause on returning Meccan converts effectively lapse after al-Ḥudaybiya?
o: Abū Baṣīr's band harried caravans until Quraysh asked to waive it
The Prophet annulled it after the Muslims' ʿumra of 7 AH
Quraysh dropped it in return for a payment from Medina
It was abolished when Khālid ibn al-Walīd accepted Islam
srd-076.e: Abū Baṣīr, returned under the treaty, killed one of his escorts and settled on the coast at Sīf al-Baḥr; Abū Jandal and others joined him and attacked Qurayshī caravans, until Quraysh themselves asked the Prophet to receive anyone who came to him.

srd-077.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Shurūṭ, mā yajūz min al-shurūṭ fī al-islām
srd-077.q: According to the verse shown and the reports in al-Bukhārī, how was the Ḥudaybiya clause on returning emigrants applied to believing women who came from Mecca?
o: They were tested and, if believers, not sent back
They were sent back like the men
They were sent back only if married
They were kept, and their families paid a ransom
srd-077.e: When Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqba and other women emigrated, the verse shown ordered that believing women be examined and not returned to the disbelievers, with their husbands' dowries repaid; the return clause was thus applied to men only.

srd-078.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, sariyyat ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:217
