srd-078.q: The verse shown answers objections over fighting in a sacred month. Which expedition gave rise to these objections, according to the sīra?
o: The detachment of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh at Nakhla
The detachment of Ḥamza to Sīf al-Baḥr
The detachment of al-Mundhir to Bīr Maʿūna
The march of the Muslims to Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad
srd-078.e: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh was sent with sealed orders to Nakhla between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif; his men attacked a Qurayshī caravan on what may have been the last day of Rajab, a sacred month, and Quraysh made propaganda of it until the verse shown was revealed.

srd-079.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ghazwat al-Rajīʿ wa-Riʿl wa-Dhakwān wa-Biʾr Maʿūna
srd-079.q: After the killing of about seventy Qurʾān reciters at Bīr Maʿūna, what did the Prophet do according to al-Bukhārī?
o: He made qunūt for a month against the tribes responsible
He led an immediate campaign against Banū ʿĀmir
He ended all his treaties with the Bedouin tribes
He forbade sending any more teachers to the tribes
srd-079.e: Anas reports that the Prophet supplicated in qunūt for a month against Riʿl, Dhakwān and ʿUṣayya, who had killed the reciters; this hadith is a main evidence in the discussion of qunūt at times of calamity (qunūt al-nawāzil).

srd-080.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Jihād, bāb hal yastaʾsir al-rajul
srd-080.q: Which companion, captured after the betrayal at al-Rajīʿ and executed in Mecca, is described in al-Bukhārī as the first to establish two rakʿas for a Muslim about to be killed in captivity?
srd-080.e: Khubayb asked to pray two rakʿas before his execution and kept them short so that no one would think he feared death; Abū Hurayra's report calls him the first to set this practice. ʿĀṣim was killed at al-Rajīʿ itself, and Ḥarām ibn Milḥān at Bīr Maʿūna.

srd-081.src: Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, the Ṣaḥīfa; Abū ʿUbayd, Kitāb al-Amwāl
srd-081.q: How does the Ṣaḥīfa of Medina describe the Jews of Banū ʿAwf and their religion?
o: An umma alongside the believers, each keeping its own religion
Protected subjects who paid jizya to the believers
Full members obliged to follow Islamic law in all
Allies in war only, with no other shared obligations
srd-081.e: The document states that the Jews of Banū ʿAwf form an umma with the believers, the Jews having their religion and the Muslims theirs, and that each side bears its own expenses while supporting the other against attack; jizya was not yet legislated.

srd-082.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān, bāb ziyādat al-īmān wa-nuqṣānih
srd-082.q: According to ʿUmar's report in al-Bukhārī, when was the part of the verse shown about the perfection of the religion revealed?
o: On the day of ʿArafa, a Friday, in the Farewell Pilgrimage
On the day of the conquest of Mecca, in Ramaḍān
On the Day of Sacrifice at Minā, in the year 9 AH
A few days before the Prophet's death, in Medina
srd-082.e: A Jewish man told ʿUmar that if such a verse had been revealed to them they would have taken its day as a festival; ʿUmar replied that he knew the day and place: ʿArafa, on a Friday, during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

srd-083.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb baʿth al-Nabī Usāma ibn Zayd fī maraḍih
srd-083.q: Which army did the Prophet prepare during his last illness, which Abū Bakr then sent out after his death despite objections?
o: Usāma ibn Zayd's army towards the Syrian frontier
The army of Khālid ibn al-Walīd towards Iraq
The army of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ towards Egypt
The army of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib towards Yemen
srd-083.e: The Prophet appointed the young Usāma, whose father Zayd had fallen at Muʾta, over an army bound for the Byzantine frontier; some objected to his youth, and Abū Bakr insisted on dispatching it after the Prophet's passing.

srd-084.src: Ibn Kathīr, al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya, wafāt Rasūl Allāh; Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, bāb maraḍ al-Nabī
srd-084.q: Which statement correctly describes what the sources say about the date of the Prophet's death?
o: Monday in Rabīʿ al-Awwal 11 AH is agreed; the day of the month is disputed
The 12th of Rabīʿ al-Awwal is agreed; the weekday is disputed among them
A Friday in Ṣafar 11 AH is agreed; only the hour of death is disputed
A Monday is agreed; the year is disputed between 10 and 11 AH
srd-084.e: The reports agree that he died on a Monday in Rabīʿ al-Awwal, 11 AH. The day of the month is disputed: the 12th is the best-known view (from Ibn Isḥāq), while others such as al-Suhaylī and Ibn Ḥajar discussed the 1st or 2nd on calendar grounds.

srd-085.src: Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, Māriya al-Qibṭiyya; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, rusul Rasūl Allāh ilā al-mulūk
srd-085.q: The ruler of Egypt, al-Muqawqis, answered the Prophet's letter courteously and sent gifts. Which person who came with those gifts became the mother of the Prophet's son Ibrāhīm?
srd-085.e: Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa brought back Māriya and her sister Sīrīn among the gifts; Māriya bore Ibrāhīm, who died as an infant, and Sīrīn was given to Ḥassān ibn Thābit. Umm Ayman was the Prophet's nurse from his childhood.

srd-086.src: Abū Dāwūd, Sunan, Kitāb al-Nikāḥ, bāb al-ṣadāq; Ibn Saʿd, al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā, Umm Ḥabība
srd-086.q: Where was Umm Ḥabība bint Abī Sufyān when her marriage to the Prophet was contracted?
o: In Abyssinia, where the Negus arranged it and paid the dowry
In Mecca, while her father still led Quraysh against Islam
In Medina, shortly after the conquest of Khaybar in 7 AH
At al-Ḥudaybiya, during the truce negotiations with Quraysh
srd-086.e: Umm Ḥabība had emigrated to Abyssinia, where her husband ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh died; the marriage was contracted there by proxy, and the reports in Abū Dāwūd mention that the Negus paid her dowry on the Prophet's behalf.

srd-087.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥāba, faḍāʾil Zaynab Umm al-Muʾminīn; Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb al-Zakāt
srd-087.q: The Prophet told his wives that the one with the 'longest hand' would be the first to join him. According to the version in Muslim, who was it, and what did the phrase mean?
o: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh; it meant generosity in charity
Sawda bint Zamʿa; it meant physical arm length
ʿĀʾisha; it meant length of life after him
Ḥafṣa; it meant devotion in night prayer
srd-087.e: In Muslim, ʿĀʾisha explains that they measured their hands, but it was Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, who worked with her hands and gave in charity, who died first. Al-Bukhārī's shorter wording seems to point to Sawda, and Ibn Ḥajar explains that the correct reading is Zaynab.

srd-088.src: al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, biography of Mūsā ibn ʿUqba
srd-088.q: Imām Mālik is reported to have recommended one early book of maghāzī as the most sound. Whose work was it?
srd-088.e: Al-Dhahabī and others report Mālik's praise for the Maghāzī of Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, a student of al-Zuhrī, for its brevity and reliability; Mālik was famously critical of Ibn Isḥāq, and al-Wāqidī and his secretary Ibn Saʿd belong to a later generation.

srd-089.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 9:107; Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, amr masjid al-ḍirār
srd-089.q: The verse shown concerns a mosque built to cause harm and division. What happened to it, according to the sīra?
o: The Prophet had it destroyed on his return from Tabūk
It was converted into a school after the conquest of Mecca
It was left standing but prayer in it was forbidden
Its builders demolished it themselves before Badr
srd-089.e: The hypocrites asked the Prophet to pray in their new mosque before he left for Tabūk; on his return the verses were revealed, and he sent companions to burn and demolish it.

srd-090.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, bāb lā yaṭūf bi-l-bayt ʿuryān
srd-090.q: In the Hajj of 9 AH, led by Abū Bakr, what was announced at Minā on the Prophet's instruction?
o: No polytheist may perform Hajj again and no one may circle the Kaʿba naked
The sanctity of life and property, as in the later Farewell Sermon
The final change of the qibla from Jerusalem towards the Kaʿba
The renewal of the terms of the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya with Quraysh
srd-090.e: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Bakr sent him among the announcers to proclaim that after that year no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would circle the House naked; ʿAlī was also sent to proclaim the opening of Sūrat Barāʾa. The Farewell Sermon came the following year.

tfl-001.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction to Sūrat al-Fātiḥa
tfl-001.q: Which of these is a well-known name of the surah from which the verse shown comes?
o: Sanām al-Qurʾān (the peak of the Quran)
Qalb al-Qurʾān (the heart of the Quran)
tfl-001.e: Al-Fātiḥa is called Umm al-Kitāb and al-Sabʿ al-Mathānī because its seven verses are repeated in every prayer. Al-Zahrāwān refers to al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān together.

tfl-002.q: What is the central meaning of the verse shown?
o: Worship and the seeking of help are directed to Allah alone
Allah is the Lord of all the worlds and their sustainer
Allah alone is the Owner of the Day of Judgement
The believer asks to be guided to the straight path
tfl-002.e: Placing the object first in this verse expresses exclusivity: worship and reliance belong to Allah alone. Ibn Kathīr notes that the first half is freedom from shirk and the second freedom from relying on one's own strength.

tfl-003.q: According to the verse shown, for whom is the Book a guidance?
o: For the scholars of the People of the Book
For the Arabs of Mecca specifically
For those who already memorised it
tfl-003.e: The verse states that the Book, about which there is no doubt, is guidance for the muttaqūn; the following verses describe their qualities.

tfl-004.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:255 (hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)
tfl-004.q: What distinction of the verse shown is established in a hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim?
o: It is the greatest verse in the Book of Allah
It is the last verse revealed to the Prophet
It is the longest verse in the Quran
It is the first verse revealed in Medina
tfl-004.e: In the hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim the Prophet asked which verse is the greatest, and Ubayy named Āyat al-Kursī. The longest verse is 2:282.

tfl-005.q: Which principle opens the verse shown?
o: There is no compulsion in religion
Fighting is prescribed for the believers
tfl-005.e: The verse begins by stating that there is no compulsion in religion, because right guidance has become clearly distinct from error.

tfl-006.q: The verse shown is the longest verse of the Quran. What is its main subject?
o: Recording debts in writing with witnesses
The rules of divorce and the waiting period
tfl-006.e: Known as āyat al-dayn, the verse instructs believers to write down deferred debts, appoint a just scribe and call witnesses.

tfl-007.q: According to the verse shown, what is the purpose of fasting?
o: That you may become physically healthy
That you may feel the hunger of the poor only
That you may complete the recitation of the Quran
tfl-007.e: The verse ends by naming the goal of fasting: attaining taqwā. It also states that fasting was prescribed for those before you.

tfl-008.q: What does the verse shown say about the month of Ramaḍān?
o: It is the month in which the Quran was sent down
It is the month in which the qibla was changed
It is the month of the Battle of Uḥud
It is one of the four sacred months
tfl-008.e: The verse praises Ramaḍān as the month in which the Quran was sent down as guidance for mankind. Ramaḍān is not one of the four sacred months.

tfl-009.q: In the verse shown, who refused to prostrate to Ādam?
tfl-009.e: All the angels prostrated except Iblīs, who refused and was arrogant, and so became one of the disbelievers.

tfl-010.q: Towards which direction does the verse shown command the believers to turn their faces in prayer?
o: Towards the Prophet's Mosque in Medina
Towards the east where the sun rises
tfl-010.e: The verse records the change of the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, which the Prophet had longed for, looking up towards the sky.

tfl-011.q: Between which two places did the night journey mentioned in the verse shown take place?
o: From al-Masjid al-Ḥarām to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā
From al-Masjid al-Aqṣā to Mount Sinai
From the cave of Ḥirāʾ to the cave of Thawr
tfl-011.e: The verse opens Sūrat al-Isrāʾ by glorifying Allah who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā, whose surroundings He blessed.

tfl-012.q: What does the verse shown teach about parents who reach old age?
o: Not even a word of annoyance may be said to them
They should be placed under the care of relatives
Obedience to them ends when they grow old
Kindness to them is recommended but not required
tfl-012.e: Right after the command to worship Allah alone comes excellence towards parents: in their old age one may not show even the slightest sign of irritation, nor rebuke them, but speak to them with noble words.

tfl-013.q: What did Yūsuf see in the dream described in the verse shown?
o: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him
Seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones
Himself carrying bread on his head
tfl-013.e: Yūsuf saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him; the commentators explain them as his eleven brothers and his parents. The other dreams belong to the king and the two prisoners.

tfl-014.src: al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, introduction to Sūrat al-Tawba
tfl-014.q: What is unique about the surah from which the verse shown comes?
o: It is the only surah not preceded by the basmala
It is the only surah named after a woman
It is the only surah revealed entirely at night
It is the only surah without any Medinan verse
tfl-014.e: Sūrat al-Tawba, also called Barāʾa, is the only surah in the muṣḥaf that does not begin with the basmala. The surah named after a woman is Maryam.

tfl-015.q: Who is the 'second of two' with the Prophet in the cave mentioned in the verse shown?
tfl-015.e: The verse refers to the hijra, when the Prophet and Abū Bakr hid in the cave of Thawr; the Prophet reassured his companion that Allah was with them.

tfl-016.q: Which three things does the verse shown command?
o: Justice, excellence (iḥsān) and giving to relatives
tfl-016.e: Allah commands ʿadl, iḥsān and giving to kin, and forbids indecency (faḥshāʾ), wrongdoing (munkar) and transgression (baghy).

tfl-017.q: Which divine law (sunna) is stated in the verse shown?
o: Allah does not change a people's condition until they change what is in themselves
Allah sends a messenger to every nation in its own language
Every community has an appointed term it cannot delay
Allah tests people with fear, hunger and loss of wealth
tfl-017.e: The verse states that Allah does not alter what a people are in until they alter what is within themselves; Ibn Kathīr links it to blessings removed through disobedience.

tfl-018.q: What does the verse shown promise to those who are grateful?
o: Allah will increase them in His favour
Allah will forgive all their past sins
Allah will grant them a long life
Allah will protect them from every trial
tfl-018.e: The verse promises increase for gratitude and warns that ingratitude brings severe punishment.

tfl-019.q: What does Allah guarantee in the verse shown?
o: That He Himself preserves the revealed Reminder
That every prophet will be protected from harm
That the Kaʿba will never be destroyed
That the believers will always be the majority
tfl-019.e: Allah states that He sent down the Reminder (the Quran) and that He is its guardian, protecting it from alteration.

tfl-020.q: Which principle of Allah's law does the verse shown begin with?
o: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity
Every soul will be paid in full for its deeds
No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another
Allah loves those who repent often
tfl-020.e: The verse begins with the principle that Allah charges no soul with more than it can bear; it then teaches the believers a comprehensive supplication.

tfl-021.q: In the passage of the verse shown, what did Nūḥ's son do when his father called him to board the ark?
o: He refused and said he would take refuge on a mountain
He boarded the ark with his wife
He asked for time to call his brothers
He went to warn the people of the city
tfl-021.e: Nūḥ called his son to embark, but the son said he would seek refuge on a mountain to protect him from the water; the waves came between them and he was among the drowned.

tfl-022.q: What is the 'anfāl' about which the Companions asked in the verse shown?
o: The spoils of war, after the Battle of Badr
The gifts sent by foreign kings
tfl-022.e: Anfāl here means spoils of war; the Companions differed about the spoils of Badr, and the verse assigned their disposal to Allah and His Messenger and called for setting relations right.

tfl-023.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 1:7 (hadith of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim in Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī)
tfl-023.q: In the hadith of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim that Ibn Kathīr cites on the verse shown, who are meant by 'those who earned anger' and 'those astray'?
o: The Jews and the Christians respectively
The hypocrites and the polytheists respectively
The people of ʿĀd and Thamūd respectively
tfl-023.e: Ibn Kathīr cites the hadith in al-Tirmidhī identifying the first group with the Jews and the second with the Christians, adding that the first knew the truth and abandoned it while the second lacked knowledge. The meaning extends to all who share these traits.

tfl-024.q: Which qualities of the God-conscious are listed in the verse shown?
o: Belief in the unseen, establishing prayer and spending from provision
Fasting, pilgrimage and fighting in Allah's way
Night prayer, seclusion and frequent fasting
tfl-024.e: The verse describes the muttaqūn as those who believe in the unseen (al-ghayb), establish the prayer and spend from what Allah has provided them.

tfl-025.q: Whom does the parable of the man who kindled a fire, in the verse shown, describe?
o: The jinn who listened to the Quran
tfl-025.e: The verse is the first of two parables for the hypocrites: they gained some light by outwardly accepting faith, then Allah took away their light and left them in darkness. The second parable, of the rainstorm, follows in 2:19.

tfl-026.q: What did Allah teach Ādam according to the verse shown, and what did it demonstrate?
o: The names of all things, showing his merit through knowledge
The art of building, showing his power over the earth
The language of the angels, showing his equality with them
The secrets of the unseen, showing his prophethood
tfl-026.e: Allah taught Ādam the names of all things and then presented them to the angels, who could not name them; this showed Ādam's superiority through knowledge.

tfl-027.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:143 (hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-027.q: How is the highlighted word explained in a hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī?
o: As 'located in the middle of the earth'
tfl-027.e: In the hadith of Abū Saʿīd on Nūḥ's people being asked whether he conveyed the message, the Prophet explained wasaṭ as ʿadl. Ibn Kathīr adds that it also means the best and most excellent.

tfl-028.q: What image does the verse shown use for the relation between spouses?
o: Each is a garment for the other
Each is a field for the other
Each is a shade for the other
Each is a pillar for the other
tfl-028.e: The verse permits intimacy on the nights of fasting and describes spouses as garments for one another, conveying closeness, covering and tranquillity.

tfl-029.q: Which restriction for those in iʿtikāf is mentioned at the end of the verse shown?
o: No marital relations while in iʿtikāf in the mosques
No eating between ʿaṣr and maghrib
No leaving the mosque even for necessities
tfl-029.e: The verse forbids relations with one's spouse while in iʿtikāf in the mosques; the scholars derive from the wording that iʿtikāf takes place in a mosque. Leaving for genuine needs is allowed by consensus.

tfl-030.q: What lesson do commentators draw from the placement of the verse shown among the fasting verses?
o: It encourages supplication during the fast and at its completion
It shows that supplication replaces a missed fast
It limits the answering of prayers to Ramaḍān
It commands a specific prayer before breaking the fast
tfl-030.e: Ibn Kathīr notes that inserting this verse on Allah's nearness and answering the caller between the rulings of fasting is a guidance to strive in supplication during the fast and when completing it.

tfl-031.q: The verse shown negates of Allah the highlighted word and sleep. What does the highlighted word mean?
tfl-031.e: Sina is the slumber that precedes sleep; negating both drowsiness and sleep expresses the perfection of Allah's attribute al-Qayyūm, who sustains everything without lapse.

tfl-032.q: How do the early commentators explain 'the firmest handhold' that contains the highlighted word?
o: As faith, Islam or the testimony of tawḥīd
As the Kaʿba and its sanctity
As the covenant with the People of the Book
tfl-032.e: Ibn Kathīr reports that the salaf explained it as īmān, Islam, or lā ilāha illā Allāh; he notes that these explanations agree in meaning.

tfl-033.q: What reason does the verse shown give for two women witnesses taking the place of one man?
o: So that if one of them errs, the other can remind her
So that the transaction is announced more widely
So that one can write while the other dictates
So that the debtor may choose between them
tfl-033.e: The verse states the wisdom explicitly: if one of the two forgets or errs, the other reminds her. The context is testimony on financial transactions.

tfl-034.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:285 (hadith of Abū Masʿūd in al-Bukhārī and Muslim)
tfl-034.q: What virtue of the last two verses of al-Baqara, beginning with the verse shown, is reported in al-Bukhārī and Muslim?
o: Whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him
Whoever recites them is forgiven the sins of a year
They were revealed together with Āyat al-Kursī
They are read in every rakʿa of the witr
tfl-034.e: In the hadith of Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, the Prophet said that whoever recites the last two verses of al-Baqara at night, they suffice him.

tfl-035.q: How are 'those of understanding' described in the verse shown?
o: They remember Allah standing, sitting and lying on their sides, and reflect on creation
They pray all night and fast all day without break
They withdraw from people to live in the wilderness
They debate the People of the Book with proofs
tfl-035.e: The verse describes them as remembering Allah in every posture and reflecting on the creation of the heavens and the earth, concluding that it was not created in vain.

tfl-036.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 3:144 (report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-036.q: On which later occasion did Abū Bakr recite the verse shown, as reported in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī?
o: On the day the Prophet died
tfl-036.e: Revealed in the context of Uḥud, when it was rumoured that the Prophet had been killed, the verse was recited by Abū Bakr on the day of the Prophet's death; the people felt as if they had never heard it before.

tfl-037.q: What does the verse shown state about those killed in the way of Allah?
o: They are alive with their Lord, receiving provision
They sleep until the Day of Resurrection
Their reward depends on the outcome of the battle
They will be returned to the world once more
tfl-037.e: The verse forbids thinking of the martyrs as dead: they are alive with their Lord and provided for. The commentators cite it in connection with the martyrs of Uḥud.

tfl-038.q: With what reminder does the verse shown open Sūrat al-Nisāʾ?
o: All people were created from a single soul, so fear Allah and honour the ties of kinship
Women are to be given their dowries willingly
The property of orphans must not be consumed
Inheritance is divided according to fixed shares
tfl-038.e: The surah opens by reminding mankind of their common origin from one soul, from which its mate was created, and commands taqwā and respect for the ties of the womb (al-arḥām).

tfl-039.q: What argument for the divine origin of the Quran does the verse shown present?
o: Had it come from other than Allah, much contradiction would be found in it
No human could produce even one surah like it
It foretold the victory of the Romans
It was revealed to an unlettered prophet
tfl-039.e: The verse calls for reflection (tadabbur) and argues that a text from anyone other than Allah would contain much inconsistency; the Quran's coherence points to its source. The challenge to produce a surah is made in other verses.

tfl-040.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 5:3 (report of ʿUmar in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-040.q: According to ʿUmar's report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, when was the passage about the perfection of the religion in the verse shown revealed?
o: On the day of ʿArafa, which was a Friday, during the Farewell Pilgrimage
On the night of the conquest of Mecca
On the day of al-Ghadīr after the pilgrimage
In the last week of the Prophet's illness
tfl-040.e: When a Jewish man told ʿUmar that such a verse would have been taken as a festival, ʿUmar replied that he knew the day and place: it was revealed at ʿArafa on a Friday.

tfl-041.q: In the passage beginning with the verse shown, what did Ibrāhīm point out about the star, the moon and the sun?
o: That they set, so none of them is worthy of worship
That they are angels who intercede with Allah
That they were created before the earth
tfl-041.e: Ibrāhīm argued with his people that a thing which sets and disappears cannot be a lord; he then turned his face to the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Ibn Kathīr understands it as a debate with his people, not personal doubt.

tfl-042.q: What happened when Mūsā asked to see his Lord, according to the verse shown?
o: Allah manifested Himself to the mountain, it crumbled and Mūsā fell unconscious
Mūsā was shown the Garden and the Fire
The sea split and Mūsā crossed it
Mūsā received the staff and the shining hand
tfl-042.e: Allah told Mūsā to look at the mountain; when his Lord manifested Himself to it, it was levelled and Mūsā fell down unconscious, then repented on waking.

tfl-043.q: What portion of the spoils does the verse shown assign to Allah, the Messenger, relatives, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer?
tfl-043.e: The verse sets aside one fifth (al-khums) of war spoils for the listed recipients; the remaining four fifths go to the fighters.

tfl-044.q: How many categories of recipients of ṣadaqāt (zakāt) does the verse shown list?
tfl-044.e: The verse lists eight: the poor, the needy, those employed to collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing slaves, debtors, in the way of Allah, and the wayfarer.

tfl-045.q: What does the verse shown say would happen to Pharaoh after his late declaration of faith at drowning?
o: His body would be preserved as a sign for those after him
He would be forgiven because he believed before death
He would be raised again to rule Egypt
His people would follow his last words
tfl-045.e: Pharaoh's faith at the moment of drowning was not accepted; the verse states that his body would be cast out and preserved so that those after him would take a lesson.

tfl-046.q: Where did Nūḥ's ark come to rest, according to the verse shown?
tfl-046.e: When the earth swallowed its water and the sky ceased, the matter was concluded and the ark settled on al-Jūdī; Ibn Kathīr describes it as a mountain in the Jazīra region.

tfl-047.q: What happened to the women of the city when Yūsuf came out before them, according to the verse shown?
o: They cut their hands, amazed, and said he was a noble angel, not a human
They mocked the governor's wife and left the banquet
They testified that Yūsuf was innocent
They asked the king to release him
tfl-047.e: The governor's wife gave each woman a knife; on seeing Yūsuf they were so struck that they cut their hands and declared he could not be a mere human.

tfl-048.q: Which means of calling to the way of Allah are named in the verse shown?
o: Wisdom, good admonition and arguing in the best manner
Signs, miracles and warnings of punishment
Poetry, sermons and public debates only
tfl-048.e: The verse lays down the method of daʿwa: ḥikma, al-mawʿiẓa al-ḥasana, and disputing in the way that is best.

tfl-049.q: What attitude to spending does the image of the hand in the verse shown teach?
o: Moderation: neither miserliness nor squandering everything
Giving away all wealth before death
Keeping wealth until one's children are grown
tfl-049.e: The verse forbids both tying one's hand to one's neck (stinginess) and stretching it out completely (extravagance), warning of blame and destitution; Ibn Kathīr explains it as a command to moderation.

tfl-050.q: What does the verse shown forbid, and why?
o: Following what one has no knowledge of, since hearing, sight and heart will be questioned
Walking proudly on the earth, since one cannot split it
Approaching the property of the orphan, since it is a trust
Killing children for fear of poverty, since Allah provides
tfl-050.e: The verse forbids pursuing or speaking about what one does not know, for the hearing, the sight and the heart will each be asked about. The other options belong to neighbouring verses.

tfl-051.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 2:8; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:8
tfl-051.q: The verse shown begins the description of the hypocrites. How does Mujāhid divide the opening verses of al-Baqara among the three types of people?
o: Four verses for the believers, two for the disbelievers, thirteen for the hypocrites
Five verses for the believers, two for the disbelievers, twelve for the hypocrites
Four verses for the believers, three for the disbelievers, twelve for the hypocrites
Three verses for the believers, two for the disbelievers, fourteen for the hypocrites
tfl-051.e: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Mujāhid that 2:2–5 describe the believers, 2:6–7 the open disbelievers and 2:8–20 the hypocrites. The long treatment of the hypocrites reflects how dangerous and hidden their state is.

tfl-052.q: According to the view reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and others, what were the 'words' Ādam received from his Lord in the verse shown?
o: The supplication of repentance mentioned in 7:23
The names he had been taught in 2:31
The testimony of faith he would teach his children
A promise that he would return to the Garden
tfl-052.e: Many of the salaf explained the words as the prayer of Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ in 7:23, admitting that they had wronged themselves and asking for forgiveness and mercy; with these words Allah accepted his repentance.

tfl-053.q: How does Ibn Kathīr characterise the angels' question about placing on earth one who would cause corruption, in the verse shown?
o: As an inquiry about the wisdom, not an objection or envy
As a protest that Allah rebuked as disobedience
As an expression of envy towards Ādam
As a claim that they knew the unseen
tfl-053.e: Ibn Kathīr states that the angels' words were not an objection to Allah nor envy of the children of Ādam, but a request to understand the wisdom; Allah answered that He knows what they do not.

tfl-054.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:143 (hadith of al-Barāʾ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-054.q: What is meant by the highlighted word, according to the occasion reported in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī?
o: The prayers offered towards Bayt al-Maqdis before the change of qibla
The faith of the People of the Book before Islam
The belief of those who emigrated to Abyssinia
The faith of the Companions killed at Badr
tfl-054.e: Al-Barāʾ reports that some Muslims had died before the qibla was changed and people wondered about them; the verse assured that Allah would not let their 'faith', meaning their prayer towards Jerusalem, go to waste. Prayer is called īmān because it expresses faith.

tfl-055.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:144 (hadith of al-Barāʾ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-055.q: According to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, for how long did the Prophet pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis in Medina before the command in the verse shown?
tfl-055.e: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months after the hijra while wishing to face the Kaʿba, and then the change was revealed.

tfl-056.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:187 (hadith of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-056.q: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim at first understood the 'white thread and black thread' in the verse shown literally. How did the Prophet explain them?
o: As the whiteness of the day and the darkness of the night
As the first and second calls to prayer
As two threads that become distinguishable at sunrise
As the light of the moon and the darkness before it
tfl-056.e: ʿAdī put a white and a black cord under his pillow and kept looking at them; the Prophet explained that the meaning is the whiteness of day emerging from the darkness of night, i.e. true dawn.

tfl-057.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:256 (report of Ibn ʿAbbās in Sunan Abī Dāwūd)
tfl-057.q: Which occasion of revelation for the verse shown does Ibn Kathīr report from Ibn ʿAbbās?
o: Children of the Anṣār raised among the Jews, whom their parents wanted to compel when Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled
A Companion who wished to force his Christian servant to pray
The captives of Badr who were offered Islam in exchange for freedom
A delegation from Najrān that asked for protection of its churches
tfl-057.e: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that some Anṣārī women whose children did not survive vowed to raise a child as a Jew; when Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled, such children were among them and the Anṣār said they would not leave their sons, and the verse was revealed.

tfl-058.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 3:7 (hadith of ʿĀʾisha in al-Bukhārī and Muslim)
tfl-058.q: In the hadith of ʿĀʾisha on the verse shown, what did the Prophet say about those who follow the mutashābih verses?
o: They are the ones Allah has named, so beware of them
They should be answered with the muḥkam verses only in private
They are excused if they intend to learn
They are the well-grounded in knowledge
tfl-058.e: After reciting the verse, the Prophet said that when you see those who pursue what is ambiguous in it, they are the ones Allah named, so be wary of them. The verse describes them as seeking discord and their own interpretation.

tfl-059.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 3:122 (report of Jābir in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-059.q: According to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, which two groups 'almost lost heart' at Uḥud, as the verse shown mentions?
o: Aws and Khazraj as a whole
tfl-059.e: Jābir said the verse was revealed about his own people, Banū Salima, and Banū Ḥāritha, and that they were glad of it because the verse also says Allah was their protector. Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr were Jewish tribes.

tfl-060.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 6:82 (hadith of Ibn Masʿūd in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-060.q: When the Companions were troubled by the word 'ẓulm' in the verse shown, how did the Prophet explain it?
o: As shirk, citing Luqmān's words in 31:13
As any minor sin committed knowingly
As injustice towards other people only
As neglect of the obligatory prayers
tfl-060.e: The Companions asked who among them had not wronged himself; the Prophet said it is not what they thought but shirk, referring to Luqmān's statement that shirk is a tremendous wrong.

tfl-061.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 6:151 (statement of Ibn Masʿūd in Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī)
tfl-061.q: What did Ibn Masʿūd say about the verse shown and the two verses after it?
o: Whoever wishes to see the Prophet's testament bearing his seal should read them
They were the last verses revealed before the Prophet's death
They abrogate the commandments given to Banū Isrāʾīl
They were recited by the Prophet at every Friday sermon
tfl-061.e: Ibn Kathīr cites Ibn Masʿūd's statement, reported by al-Tirmidhī, that 6:151–153 are like the sealed testament of the Prophet; they gather prohibitions such as shirk, disobeying parents, killing children and approaching indecency.

tfl-062.q: Who are the 'people of al-Aʿrāf' in the verse shown, according to the view Ibn Kathīr reports from Ḥudhayfa, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd?
o: People whose good and bad deeds are equal
The prophets who will intercede for their nations
Angels who guard the gates of the Garden
tfl-062.e: Several views exist, but the best known, reported from these Companions, is that they are people whose good and bad deeds balance; they wait on the heights between the Garden and the Fire before finally entering the Garden.

tfl-063.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 9:118 (hadith of Kaʿb ibn Mālik in al-Bukhārī and Muslim)
tfl-063.q: Who are 'the three who were left behind' whose repentance is accepted in the verse shown?
o: Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ and Hilāl ibn Umayya
Abū Lubāba, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa
Three hypocrites who built the mosque of ḍirār
Three Bedouins who refused to pay zakāt
tfl-063.e: They stayed behind from Tabūk without excuse, were boycotted for fifty nights until the earth felt narrow for them, and were then forgiven, as Kaʿb narrates in his long hadith.

tfl-064.q: What exception does the verse shown highlight about the people of Yūnus?
o: Their faith benefited them when they believed as punishment approached
They were the only people saved by a flood
They were the only nation never sent a warner
Their city was raised to the sky and overturned
tfl-064.e: No town that believed upon seeing the punishment was benefited by it except the people of Yūnus: when they believed, Allah removed the humiliating punishment and let them enjoy life for a time.

tfl-065.q: What is Ibn ʿAbbās reported to have said about the verse shown, which commands steadfastness as one was commanded?
o: No verse was revealed to the Prophet that was harder on him than this one
It was the first verse revealed in Medina
It abrogated the command of patience in Mecca
It was revealed in reply to a question of the Jews
tfl-065.e: Al-Qurṭubī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that no verse was harder on the Prophet than this command to istiqāma, and connects it with the report that Sūrat Hūd and its sisters turned his hair grey.

tfl-066.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 11:114 (hadith of Ibn Masʿūd in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-066.q: What occasion is reported in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī for the verse shown, which states that good deeds remove bad deeds?
o: A man who had kissed a woman came to the Prophet regretting it
A Companion who missed the ʿaṣr prayer at the trench
A Bedouin who urinated in the mosque
A man who broke his fast by intercourse in Ramaḍān
tfl-066.e: Ibn Masʿūd reports that a man kissed a woman and came to the Prophet; the verse on establishing prayer at both ends of the day was revealed, and when he asked if it was for him alone, the Prophet said it was for all of his community.

tfl-067.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 14:27 (hadith of al-Barāʾ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-067.q: According to the hadith of al-Barāʾ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, to what does the 'firm word' in the hereafter in the verse shown refer?
o: The believer's answer when questioned in the grave
The testimony of the limbs on the Day of Judgement
The weighing of deeds on the Scale
tfl-067.e: The Prophet explained that when the Muslim is questioned in the grave he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is His Messenger; this is the firmness Allah grants.

tfl-068.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 15:87 (hadith of Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-068.q: In the hadith of Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, what are the 'seven oft-repeated' mentioned in the verse shown?
o: The seven long surahs from al-Baqara onwards
The seven verses of Āyat al-Kursī and its neighbours
The seven surahs beginning with ḥā-mīm
tfl-068.e: The Prophet told Abū Saʿīd that al-Fātiḥa is the seven oft-repeated and the great Quran he was given. Some salaf named the seven long surahs, but the hadith settles the matter for most commentators.

tfl-069.q: Which description of the verse shown is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd?
o: It is the most comprehensive verse in the Quran for good and evil
It is the verse that most frightened the Companions
It is the last verse revealed about family law
It is the verse that abrogated the law of retaliation
tfl-069.e: Ibn Kathīr cites Ibn Masʿūd's statement that this verse gathers all good to be done and all evil to be avoided. Its use at the end of the Friday sermon is a later practice, not part of the verse's explanation.

tfl-070.q: About which Companion do most commentators say the exception for one compelled while his heart is at peace with faith, in the verse shown, was revealed?
tfl-070.e: Ibn Kathīr notes that most commentators link the verse to ʿAmmār, who was tortured by the polytheists until he said what they demanded; the Prophet told him that if they returned, he might return to it. All four Companions were persecuted, but the verse is tied to ʿAmmār.

tfl-071.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction to Sūrat al-Isrāʾ
tfl-071.q: By which other name does Ibn Masʿūd refer to Sūrat al-Isrāʾ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, listing it among the earliest surahs he learned?
tfl-071.e: Ibn Masʿūd said that Banī Isrāʾīl, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭāhā and al-Anbiyāʾ are among the earliest and most cherished surahs he acquired. Al-Bukhārī titles the chapter of tafsīr with the same name.

tfl-072.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 3:190 (hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī)
tfl-072.q: According to Ibn ʿAbbās in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, when did the Prophet recite the passage beginning with the verse shown?
o: When he woke at night, before praying the night prayer
On the night of the Isrāʾ
tfl-072.e: Ibn ʿAbbās, who spent a night in the house of his aunt Maymūna, saw the Prophet wake, look at the sky and recite the last ten verses of Āl ʿImrān, then perform wuḍūʾ and pray.

tfl-073.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:30; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 2:30
tfl-073.q: Which interpretation of the highlighted word does Ibn Kathīr favour?
o: A people who succeed one another, generation after generation
Ādam alone, as Allah's deputy exercising His authority
Only the prophets and the just rulers among Ādam's offspring
The angels sent down to replace the jinn on earth
tfl-073.e: Ibn Kathīr explains khalīfa as people who succeed each other age after age and says it does not refer to Ādam alone, as some commentators held. Al-Qurṭubī, by contrast, used the verse as a basis for the obligation of appointing an imām.

tfl-074.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:34; al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 2:34
tfl-074.q: Which statement correctly describes the views on whether Iblīs, mentioned in the verse shown, was one of the angels?
o: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī held he was never an angel; reports from Ibn ʿAbbās place him in a group of angels called al-jinn
All the salaf agreed he was the chief of the angels until his refusal
All the salaf agreed he was a jinn raised by the angels from childhood
The dispute concerns only whether he later prostrated in secret
tfl-074.e: The exception in the verse led some to count him among the angels, and reports from Ibn ʿAbbās speak of a tribe of angels called al-jinn. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī insisted he was never an angel even for a moment, relying on 18:50, which states he was of the jinn.

tfl-075.q: After listing the reports identifying the forbidden tree in the verse shown, what conclusion does al-Ṭabarī reach?
o: It was a specific tree whose identity we cannot know, and knowing it brings no benefit
It was wheat, as the strongest report from Ibn ʿAbbās states
It was the grapevine, which is why wine was later forbidden
It was the fig tree, whose leaves they then used to cover themselves
tfl-075.e: Al-Ṭabarī reports views naming wheat, the vine and the fig, then concludes that Allah forbade one particular tree without revealing which; knowing it would not benefit and not knowing it does no harm. This reflects his method of not specifying what revelation leaves unspecified.

tfl-076.q: Who are meant by the highlighted word, according to Ibn Kathīr's summary of the views?
o: Views name the Arab polytheists, the Jewish scholars or the hypocrites, and the verse covers all of them
Only the Christians of Najrān, as all reports agree
Only the hypocrites, by consensus of the Companions
Only the leaders of Quraysh, the other views being rejected
tfl-076.e: Ibn Kathīr reports that some said the polytheists (al-Zajjāj), others the Jewish rabbis (Mujāhid), others the hypocrites, and concludes that the verse is general to all of them, since each group objected to the change of qibla.

tfl-077.src: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, on 2:184; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:184
tfl-077.q: Which statement correctly describes the reports on the fidya clause for 'those who can fast only with hardship' in the verse shown?
o: Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ reported an early choice between fasting and fidya that 2:185 abrogated, while Ibn ʿAbbās held the clause remains for the very old who cannot fast
All Companions agreed the clause was never abrogated and lets anyone who wishes pay fidya
All Companions agreed it was abrogated entirely, leaving no concession for the elderly
The dispute concerns only whether the fidya is one meal or two
tfl-077.e: Both reports are in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: Salama says those who wished could break the fast and pay fidya until the next verse abrogated this, while Ibn ʿAbbās says the clause is not abrogated but applies to the elderly man and woman unable to fast. Ibn Kathīr reconciles them: the general option was abrogated, the concession for the incapable remains.

tfl-078.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 2:255; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:255
tfl-078.q: Which interpretation of the highlighted word did al-Ṭabarī prefer?
o: Allah's knowledge, following a report from Ibn ʿAbbās
The ʿArsh itself, as reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī
Allah's dominion and sovereignty over creation
The footstool, the place of the two feet
tfl-078.e: Al-Ṭabarī listed the views and preferred the report from Ibn ʿAbbās that the kursī is Allah's knowledge. Ibn Kathīr held that the sound report from Ibn ʿAbbās is that it is the place of the two feet, and al-Ḥasan said it is the ʿArsh; the question asks only for al-Ṭabarī's preference.

tfl-079.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 2:256; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:256
tfl-079.q: Which position on the scope of the verse shown did al-Ṭabarī prefer?
o: It is specific to those from whom jizya is accepted, such as the People of the Book, and is not abrogated
It was abrogated by the later command to fight
It applies only to the Anṣār children of its occasion
It applies only to the Arab polytheists of Mecca
tfl-079.e: Al-Ṭabarī reports that some held the verse abrogated and others that it concerns those whose religion may be left to them in return for jizya; he preferred the second. Ibn Kathīr reads it as a general statement: no one should be compelled into Islam, since its truth is evident.

tfl-080.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement on the command to write down debts in the verse shown?
o: The majority hold it is a recommendation, while al-Ṭabarī is reported to have held it obligatory
The majority hold it obligatory, while al-Ṭabarī alone held it a recommendation
All agree it is obligatory and an unwritten loan is void
All agree it was abrogated by the following verse on trust
tfl-080.e: Al-Qurṭubī reports that some held writing debts to be an obligation, naming al-Ṭabarī among them, while the majority (jumhūr) see it as a recommendation for securing rights. Others, such as al-Shaʿbī, said it was abrogated by the mention of mutual trust in 2:283, so there is no consensus on abrogation either.

tfl-081.src: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Kitāb al-Īmān (hadith of Abū Hurayra on 2:284–286); Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:284
tfl-081.q: According to the hadith of Abū Hurayra in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, what did the revelation of the verse shown relieve?
o: The Companions' distress at being held accountable for what is in their souls, as stated in 2:284
The burden of the night prayer imposed at the start of Sūrat al-Muzzammil
The strictness of the early fasting rules mentioned in 2:187
The fear caused by the Jews' objections to the change of qibla
tfl-081.e: When 2:284 was revealed the Companions found it very hard; the Prophet told them to say 'we hear and obey', after which 2:285 was revealed and Allah lifted the burden with 2:286. Many call this naskh, others takhṣīṣ or clarification.

tfl-082.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 3:7; al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 3:7
tfl-082.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about pausing after the name of Allah in the verse shown?
o: Many salaf pause there, so the ultimate reality is known only to Allah; others such as Mujāhid join 'the well-grounded', taking taʾwīl as explanation
All the salaf continue reading, so the well-grounded know every meaning
The pause is a matter of melody only and does not affect meaning
The disagreement is only about whether the verse is Meccan or Medinan
tfl-082.e: Those who pause after the divine name take taʾwīl as the true reality or outcome of things, known only to Allah; those who connect, like Mujāhid and a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, take taʾwīl as tafsīr, which the well-grounded can know. Ibn Kathīr explains that the two readings reflect two meanings of taʾwīl.

tfl-083.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 4:59; al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 4:59
tfl-083.q: After reporting that 'those in authority' in the verse shown were explained as rulers by some and as scholars by others, what does Ibn Kathīr conclude?
o: It apparently includes all those in authority, both rulers and scholars
It refers only to the scholars, and rulers are excluded
It refers only to the four Rightly Guided Caliphs
It refers only to commanders of military expeditions
tfl-083.e: Ibn Kathīr notes the occasion reported in al-Bukhārī about a commander of an expedition, and the views of rulers and of scholars, then says the apparent meaning is general to both. Al-Ṭabarī preferred the view that rulers are meant.

tfl-084.q: Which statement correctly describes the two main explanations of the covenant taken from the offspring of Ādam in the verse shown?
o: Many hold the offspring were actually brought forth and made to testify, citing reports; others among the salaf and later scholars explain it as the innate disposition (fiṭra) to tawḥīd
All agree it is a parable only, with no actual event behind it
All agree it concerns only the sons of Ādam born before his death
All agree it is the covenant taken from the prophets alone
tfl-084.e: Ibn Kathīr cites reports that Allah brought the offspring from the loins of Ādam and made them testify, and also mentions those among the salaf and khalaf who said the testimony means that they were created upon the fiṭra of tawḥīd. The question asks for the shape of this difference, not a single verdict.

tfl-085.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 9:108 (hadith of Abū Saʿīd in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)
tfl-085.q: Which statement correctly describes the views on 'the mosque founded on taqwā from the first day' in the verse shown?
o: Many link the context to Qubāʾ, while a hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim names the Prophet's Mosque; Ibn Kathīr sees no contradiction, both being founded on taqwā
All agree it is al-Masjid al-Ḥarām in Mecca
All agree it is the mosque of Banū Salima, known as al-Qiblatayn
All agree it is the mosque built at Tabūk during the expedition
tfl-085.e: Qubāʾ fits the context of the masjid al-ḍirār, built nearby, and of people who love to purify themselves; but in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim the Prophet, when asked, said it was his own mosque in Medina. Ibn Kathīr says that if Qubāʾ is founded on taqwā, the Prophet's Mosque is even more so.

tfl-086.src: Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī, Abwāb Tafsīr al-Qurʾān, Sūrat al-Tawba; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, introduction to Sūrat al-Tawba
tfl-086.q: In the report in which Ibn ʿAbbās asks ʿUthmān why no basmala separates al-Anfāl from the surah of the verse shown, what reason does ʿUthmān give?
o: Their content was similar and the Prophet died without making clear whether it belonged to al-Anfāl
The basmala was lost when the leaves of the copy were damaged
The Prophet ordered it removed after the expedition of Tabūk
Zayd ibn Thābit forgot to write it and it was never restored
tfl-086.e: ʿUthmān explained that al-Anfāl was among the early Medinan revelations and Barāʾa among the last, their stories resembled each other, and the Prophet did not clarify the matter, so he placed them together without a basmala. Al-Qurṭubī also reports ʿAlī's explanation that the basmala signals security, while Barāʾa came with its withdrawal.

tfl-087.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 17:1; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 17:1
tfl-087.q: What is the majority view on the nature of the journey in the verse shown, and which word of the verse do they cite?
o: It was with body and soul while awake, and they cite the word 'His servant'
It was a vision of the soul in sleep, and they cite the word 'by night'
It was with the soul only while awake, and they cite the word 'blessed'
It happened twice in Medina, and they cite the word 'the farthest'
tfl-087.e: The majority hold the Isrāʾ was in body and soul while awake, arguing that ʿabd denotes the whole person and that a mere dream would not have caused Quraysh to deny it. A minority view, based on reports attributed to some early figures, held it was a spiritual vision.

tfl-088.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 17:23; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 17:23
tfl-088.q: What does the highlighted word mean in this verse, according to the commentators?
o: He commanded and enjoined, not a cosmic decree; Ibn Masʿūd's non-canonical reading has 'enjoined'
He decreed cosmically, so that none could ever worship other than Him
He completed and finished the creation of the heavens
He judged between the disputing parties on the Day of Judgement
tfl-088.e: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and others explained qaḍā here as amara or waṣṣā, a legislative command; it cannot be a cosmic decree, since many people do worship others. Al-Qurṭubī notes that the muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd reads 'waṣṣā', which supports this meaning as tafsīr.

tfl-089.q: How do commentators explain the difference between the verse shown and 6:151, both forbidding the killing of children because of poverty?
o: 6:151 addresses those already poor and mentions the parents' provision first; the verse shown addresses fear of future poverty and mentions the children's provision first
6:151 addresses fear of future poverty and mentions the children first; the verse shown addresses present poverty and mentions the parents first
Both address present poverty; the order differs only for the rhyme
6:151 concerns daughters only, while the verse shown concerns sons only
tfl-089.e: In 6:151 the poverty is already present, so Allah first assures the parents of their own provision; in 17:31 the fear is of poverty to come because of the children, so He first assures the children's provision. This is a classic example of mutashābih al-lafẓ explained by context.

tfs-001.q: Who are the people described in the verse shown?
o: Young believers who took refuge in a cave
Disciples of ʿĪsā hiding in a ship
Soldiers of Firʿawn fleeing the sea
Merchants of Quraysh lost in the desert
tfs-001.e: The verse shows the youths of the cave (aṣḥāb al-kahf), who fled with their faith from a disbelieving people and asked their Lord for mercy and right guidance.

tfs-002.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction to Sūrat al-Kahf
tfs-002.q: The verse shown opens one of the four great stories of Sūrat al-Kahf. Which story belongs to this surah?
tfs-002.e: The four stories of al-Kahf are the youths of the cave, the owner of the two gardens, Mūsā and al-Khiḍr, and Dhū al-Qarnayn. Yūsuf's story is in Sūrat Yūsuf, Ṣāliḥ's she-camel in several Meccan surahs, and the Elephant in Sūrat al-Fīl.

tfs-003.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on the names of the surahs
tfs-003.q: Sūra 19, whose verse is shown, is named after whom?
tfs-003.e: Sūra 19 is named Maryam; the verse shown begins her story, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east. She is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran.

tfs-004.q: When Mūsā came to the fire, what was he commanded in the verse shown?
o: To take off his sandals in the sacred valley
To throw his staff into the river
To return at once to Firʿawn's palace
To fast for forty days on the mountain
tfs-004.e: In the valley of Ṭuwā Mūsā was called and told to remove his sandals, for he was in the sacred valley; the commission to go to Firʿawn comes later in the passage.

tfs-005.q: What is the first piece of advice Luqmān gives his son in the verse shown?
o: Not to associate partners with Allah
To speak little and listen much
To seek knowledge in distant lands
tfs-005.e: Luqmān begins with tawḥīd: he forbids his son shirk and calls it a tremendous wrong (ẓulm ʿaẓīm), since it gives worship to one who has no right to it.

tfs-006.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on the names of the surahs
tfs-006.q: Where does the name of Sūrat Yā Sīn come from?
o: From the two separate letters that open it
From a prophet named Yāsīn in the surah
From the town mentioned in its middle
tfs-006.e: The surah is named after the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) Yā and Sīn in its first verse, like Ṭā Hā, Ṣād and Qāf.

tfs-007.q: The refrain in the verse shown is addressed in the dual. To whom?
o: To the two angels at the grave
tfs-007.e: The refrain of Sūrat al-Raḥmān asks the two 'weighty ones' (al-thaqalān), jinn and humans, which of their Lord's favours they would deny; the surah addresses both groups explicitly (e.g. 55:33).

tfs-008.q: According to the verse shown, why did Allah create death and life?
o: To test who is best in deeds
To show the passing of the seasons
To let the angels record history
To reward every soul in this world
tfs-008.e: Al-Mulk states that death and life were created as a trial, to show which of people is best in deed; the mufassirūn note it says 'best', not 'most', pointing to quality and sincerity.

tfs-009.q: In the passage of the verse shown, the earth is described as a bed. How are the mountains described?
o: As pegs that hold it firm
tfs-009.e: Al-Nabaʾ lists signs of Allah's power to prove the resurrection: the earth spread out like a bed and the mountains as pegs (awtād) that steady it.

tfs-010.q: Who is the blind man referred to at the start of Sūrat ʿAbasa?
tfs-010.e: The mufassirūn report that Ibn Umm Maktūm came seeking instruction while the Prophet was busy inviting leaders of Quraysh; the surah teaches that the sincere seeker deserves attention.

tfs-011.q: What is the main subject of the opening verses of Sūrat al-Takwīr, beginning with the verse shown?
o: The upheaval of the universe at the Last Day
The creation of the heavens in six days
The story of the People of the Cave
The rules of fasting in Ramaḍān
tfs-011.e: Al-Takwīr opens with a series of scenes of the Hour: the sun wrapped up, the stars falling, the mountains moved, ending with every soul knowing what it has brought.

tfs-012.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 93:1–3; al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr
tfs-012.q: The verse shown was revealed after what?
o: A pause in revelation that the Prophet's enemies mocked
The Prophet's victory at the Battle of Badr
The death of the Prophet's son Ibrāhīm
The return of the emigrants from Abyssinia
tfs-012.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that revelation paused for a time and a polytheist mocked the Prophet as abandoned; al-Ḍuḥā was revealed to assure him that his Lord had neither left him nor become displeased.

tfs-013.q: What is the central message of the verse shown and the one before it?
o: Wealth is a sign of Allah's pleasure
Hardship is a punishment for sin
Patience is only needed in war
tfs-013.e: Al-Sharḥ repeats that with hardship comes ease. The mufassirūn observe that 'hardship' is definite and 'ease' indefinite, so one hardship is met by more than one ease.

tfs-014.q: What is special about the verse shown and the four after it?
o: They are the first verses of the Quran revealed
They are the last verses of the Quran revealed
They were revealed in Madīna after the Hijra
They were revealed during the Night Journey
tfs-014.e: According to the hadith of ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, the first revelation in the cave of Ḥirāʾ was the opening five verses of al-ʿAlaq, beginning with the command to read.

tfs-015.q: According to the verse shown, the Night of Decree is better than what?
tfs-015.e: Sūrat al-Qadr states that this night, in which the Quran was sent down, is better than a thousand months; the mufassirūn explain that worship in it surpasses worship in a thousand months without it.

tfs-016.q: What does the verse shown and the one after it teach?
o: Even the smallest good or evil deed will be seen
Good deeds wipe out the need for repentance
Deeds are judged by their size alone
tfs-016.e: The close of al-Zalzala says that whoever does an atom's weight (mithqāl dharra) of good or evil will see it, so no deed is too small to count.

tfs-017.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-ʿAṣr
tfs-017.q: The verse shown names those who are exempt from loss. Which group of qualities does it list?
o: Faith, good deeds, urging truth and urging patience
tfs-017.e: Al-ʿAṣr says all people are in loss except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth and to patience: two qualities perfect oneself and two perfect others.

tfs-018.src: Muslim, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣalāh (hadith of Anas on al-Kawthar)
tfs-018.q: According to the hadith of Anas in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, what is al-Kawthar in the verse shown?
o: A river in Paradise promised to the Prophet
The well of Zamzam in Makka
The night of the Prophet's ascension
tfs-018.e: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim the Prophet, after this surah was revealed, explained that al-Kawthar is a river his Lord promised him in Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbās described it as the abundant good, which includes that river.

tfs-019.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Kāfirūn
tfs-019.q: What is the main theme of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, which closes with the verse shown?
o: Clear disavowal of the polytheists' worship
The story of the Prophet's migration
tfs-019.e: Al-Kāfirūn declares a complete separation in worship: the Prophet does not worship what they worship. Ibn Kathīr calls it the surah of disavowal (barāʾa) from shirk.

tfs-020.q: According to the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, beginning with the verse shown, equals what?
tfs-020.e: The Prophet said that this surah equals a third of the Quran. Scholars explain that the Quran deals with rulings, narratives and tawḥīd, and al-Ikhlāṣ is pure tawḥīd.

tfs-021.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Falaq and al-Nās
tfs-021.q: Sūrat al-Falaq, beginning with the verse shown, and Sūrat al-Nās are together called al-Muʿawwidhatān. What does this name mean?
o: The two surahs of seeking refuge
The two surahs of the night
tfs-021.e: Both surahs begin with the command to seek refuge with Allah, hence 'the two refuge-givers'. The Prophet used to recite them for protection.

tfs-022.q: The verse shown is known as the Light Verse (āyat al-nūr). Which image does its parable use?
o: A lamp in a niche, set inside a glass
A full moon rising over a dark sea
A fire kindled by travellers in the desert
tfs-022.e: The verse likens Allah's light to a niche (mishkāt) holding a lamp inside a glass like a brilliant star, lit from the oil of a blessed olive tree. Fire in the desert and lightning appear in other parables (e.g. 2:17–19).

tfs-023.q: The verse shown mentions different claims about the number of the youths of the cave. What guidance does it give about this?
o: Leave the matter to Allah and do not argue about it at length
Accept the number given by the People of the Book
Count them as three, the first number mentioned
Search for their cave to settle the question
tfs-023.e: The verse reports three guesses, says that their exact number is known to Allah and only a few, and forbids lengthy dispute about it. Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said he was among the few and that they were seven.

tfs-024.q: What etiquette do the verse shown and the one after it teach?
o: To make future plans conditional on Allah's will
To write down every promise one makes
To swear an oath before every journey
To consult a scholar before every decision
tfs-024.e: The believer should not say he will certainly do something tomorrow without adding 'if Allah wills' (in shāʾ Allāh), and if he forgets, he should remember his Lord. Ibn Kathīr links the verses to the delay in revelation after the Prophet promised an answer without saying it.

tfs-025.q: In the parable of the two gardens, what was the wrong of the garden owner shown in the verse?
o: He thought his garden would last forever and doubted the Hour
He withheld his workers' wages and mistreated them
He built his garden on land taken unjustly from orphans
He worshipped idols that he set up among his palms
tfs-025.e: Entering his garden proud and wronging himself, he claimed it would never perish and doubted that the Hour would come; his believing companion warned him, and the garden was destroyed.

tfs-026.q: The verse shown begins the journey of Mūsā with al-Khiḍr. Which event is NOT one of its three incidents?
o: Splitting a rock so that springs gushed out
Making a hole in a boat
Repairing a wall about to collapse
tfs-026.e: The three incidents are the boat, the boy and the wall, each explained at the end by al-Khiḍr. Water gushing from a rock struck by Mūsā's staff belongs to the story of the Children of Israel (2:60).

tfs-027.q: Why did al-Khiḍr damage the boat, according to the verse shown?
o: A king was seizing every sound boat by force
The boat was about to sink in a storm
The owners had refused to carry them
tfs-027.e: The boat belonged to poor people who worked at sea; ahead of them was a king who took every good boat by force, so a defect saved it for its owners.

tfs-028.q: According to the verse shown, why was the wall repaired?
o: It hid a treasure of two orphans whose father was righteous
It protected the town from an approaching army
It was part of a mosque built by a prophet
Its owner had paid al-Khiḍr to repair it
tfs-028.e: The wall belonged to two orphan boys in the town, beneath it was a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous; Allah willed that they reach maturity and take out their treasure. The mufassirūn draw from it that a parent's righteousness benefits the children.

tfs-029.q: What did the people in the verse shown ask Dhū al-Qarnayn to do?
o: To build a barrier between them and Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj
To lead their army on a march to the rising sun
To rule over them as their king for the rest of his life
To teach them the religion of Ibrāhīm and build a temple
tfs-029.e: They complained that Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj were spreading corruption and offered payment for a barrier; he declined the payment, asked for their labour, and built a wall of iron with molten copper.

tfs-030.q: What does the verse shown say about the name of Yaḥyā?
o: No one had been given this name before him
It was chosen by his father Zakariyyā
It was the name of his grandfather
It was given to him by the people of the Temple
tfs-030.e: In answer to Zakariyyā's prayer, Allah gave him the good news of a son named Yaḥyā and stated that no one before had been given this name; some early mufassirūn also read it as 'no one like him'.

tfs-031.q: What characterises Ibrāhīm's speech to his father in the verse shown and those after it?
o: Gentle, respectful address while firmly rejecting idols
Harsh rebuke followed by breaking the idols at home
Agreement to worship the idols on festivals
tfs-031.e: Ibrāhīm repeatedly addresses his father tenderly and asks why he worships what neither hears nor sees; even when threatened, he answers with a greeting of peace and a promise to seek forgiveness for him. The mufassirūn cite it as a model of gentle daʿwa to parents.

tfs-032.q: In his prayer before going to Firʿawn, what does Mūsā ask for in the verse shown?
o: That the knot be loosened from his tongue
That his staff be turned into a serpent
That Firʿawn be destroyed at once
That he be given a large army
tfs-032.e: Mūsā asked for an expanded chest, an eased task and the untying of a knot in his tongue so that his speech would be understood, and asked that Hārūn be made his helper.

tfs-033.q: How were Mūsā and Hārūn told to speak to Firʿawn in the verse shown?
o: With gentle words, that he might reflect or fear
With threats, so that he would submit quickly
In the presence of the whole army
tfs-033.e: Although Firʿawn was a tyrant, they were told to speak to him gently, in the hope that he would take heed or fear. The mufassirūn draw from it that gentleness is the rule in calling even the arrogant.

tfs-034.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 24:11–26; al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr
tfs-034.q: The verse shown begins the passage on the ifk (the slander). Whose innocence does it declare?
o: ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers
tfs-034.e: Verses 24:11 onwards were revealed to clear ʿĀʾisha of the slander spread after the campaign against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, as narrated by her in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. The verse adds that the matter was not evil for the believers but good.

tfs-035.q: How do the servants of the Most Merciful respond when the ignorant address them, according to the verse shown?
o: With words of peace, without answering in kind
By cutting off all contact with them
By calling on Allah to punish them
By debating them until they give in
tfs-035.e: The first quality of ʿibād al-Raḥmān is humble walking; the second is that when the foolish speak to them rudely they reply with peaceable words and do not repay ignorance with ignorance.

tfs-036.q: What does the verse shown teach about how the servants of the Most Merciful spend?
o: Neither wasteful nor stingy, but balanced between the two
Giving away all they own and keeping nothing back
Spending only on their own families and relatives
Saving their wealth so as to leave it to their heirs
tfs-036.e: The verse praises moderation: they neither squander nor hold back, but spend in a just middle way; Ibn Kathīr links it to other verses forbidding both extremes.

tfs-037.q: Within Luqmān's advice, the verse shown speaks of parents. What does it command?
o: Gratitude to Allah and to one's parents
Obedience to parents even in shirk
Leaving one's parents to seek knowledge
Giving parents a fixed share of income
tfs-037.e: The verse mentions the mother's hardship in pregnancy and nursing and commands thanks to Allah and to the parents; the next verse adds that they are not to be obeyed if they call to shirk, though they are still treated kindly.

tfs-038.q: What manners does Luqmān teach in the verse shown?
o: Moderation in walking and lowering the voice
Raising the voice to be clearly heard
tfs-038.e: Luqmān tells his son to be moderate in his pace and to lower his voice, noting that the most unpleasant of sounds is the braying of donkeys; the verse before forbids turning one's cheek away from people in pride.

tfs-039.q: In the parable of the town in Sūrat Yā Sīn, how many messengers were sent, according to the verse shown?
o: Two, then they were reinforced with a third
One, who was later joined by his brother
tfs-039.e: Two messengers were sent and rejected, and Allah strengthened them with a third. Many mufassirūn identified the town as Anṭākiya (Antioch), though Ibn Kathīr raises doubts about this identification.

tfs-040.q: What did the man who came running from the far end of the city urge in the verse shown?
o: That his people follow the messengers
That his people expel the messengers
That the town choose a new king
tfs-040.e: He called his people to follow the messengers, who asked no reward and were rightly guided. He was killed, and the following verses show him wishing that his people knew of the honour he received.

tfs-041.q: What principle does the verse shown establish?
o: Verifying news brought by an untrustworthy person before acting
Rejecting every report that comes from one person
Punishing anyone who brings bad news
tfs-041.e: The verse commands tabayyun: check a report from a fāsiq before acting on it, lest harm be done to people out of ignorance. Many mufassirūn mention as its occasion al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba's report about Banū al-Muṣṭaliq.

tfs-042.q: To what does the verse shown liken backbiting (ghība)?
o: Eating the flesh of one's dead brother
tfs-042.e: Al-Ḥujurāt forbids excessive suspicion, spying and backbiting, and portrays backbiting as eating a dead brother's flesh, something everyone finds repulsive.

tfs-043.q: According to the verse shown, what makes a person most honourable before Allah?
tfs-043.e: The verse states that people were made nations and tribes so that they may know one another, and that the most honoured before Allah is the most God-fearing, not the one of higher descent.

tfs-044.q: Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa divides people into three groups. Which group does the verse shown name?
tfs-044.e: Al-Wāqiʿa names the people of the right, the people of the left and the forerunners; the forerunners, those foremost in good, are the ones brought near (al-muqarrabūn). The people of the heights (al-Aʿrāf) belong to Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.

tfs-045.q: Sūrat al-Ḥadīd takes its name from the verse shown. What does the verse say about iron?
o: It was sent down with great might and benefits for people
It must never be used for weapons of any kind
It was the material from which Nūḥ built the Ark
It was the metal that the Golden Calf was cast from
tfs-045.e: The verse mentions the sending of messengers with the Book and the balance, and of iron with its great might and many benefits. The calf was made of the people's ornaments, not of iron.

tfs-046.q: What characterises the closing verses of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, including the verse shown?
o: A concentrated series of Allah's beautiful names
A list of the prophets sent to Banū Isrāʾīl
The description of the Day of Judgement
tfs-046.e: The last three verses of al-Ḥashr gather many of al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā, such as the King, the Holy, Peace, the Guardian and the Compeller, and end by saying that everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Him.

tfs-047.q: After reminding the Prophet that he was found an orphan and sheltered, what does Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā command in the verse shown?
o: Not to treat the orphan harshly
To adopt every orphan in Makka
To give orphans a share of the spoils
tfs-047.e: Having recalled Allah's favours to him (orphanhood, guidance, sufficiency), the surah commands in return not to oppress the orphan, not to repel the one who asks, and to speak of his Lord's blessing.

tfs-048.q: Among the scenes of the Last Day in Sūrat al-Takwīr, what does the verse shown and the one after it describe?
o: The girl buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed
The scrolls of deeds are spread open before all creation
The angels descend in rows around the gathered people
The scales of deeds are set up for the reckoning
tfs-048.e: The verse refers to the pre-Islamic practice of burying daughters alive (waʾd). Asking the victim rather than the killer is a severe rebuke of those who did it.

tfs-049.src: al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-ʿIlm and Kitāb al-Tafsīr (hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb)
tfs-049.q: According to the hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, why did Mūsā set out for the junction of the two seas mentioned in the verse shown?
o: He had called himself the most learned, and was told of one more learned
He was fleeing from Firʿawn after the killing of the Egyptian man
He was searching for the tablets of the Torah that were lost at sea
He had been sent to call a people living on the shore to tawḥīd
tfs-049.e: In the hadith, Mūsā was asked who was most knowledgeable and answered 'I', without attributing knowledge to Allah; Allah informed him of a servant at the junction of the two seas who knew more, and Mūsā set out to learn from him.

tfs-050.q: What is the Prophet commanded in the verse shown?
o: To stay patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening
To leave Makka and live in seclusion like the people of the cave
To pray through the night until his feet became swollen
To give the leaders of Quraysh precedence over the poor believers
tfs-050.e: The verse commands patience in the company of sincere worshippers, even if poor, and forbids turning one's eyes from them out of desire for worldly adornment. The mufassirūn mention that Quraysh nobles had asked for the poor believers to be sent away.

tfs-051.q: Ibn Kathīr says the end of the verse shown contains the two pillars of an accepted deed. What are they?
o: Sincerity to Allah and following the Sunna
Knowledge before action and patience after it
Intention at the start and supplication at the end
Ritual purity and facing the qibla
tfs-051.e: The verse asks whoever hopes to meet his Lord to do righteous work and associate no one in worship. Ibn Kathīr explains: the deed must be correct according to the Sharīʿa and done sincerely for Allah alone.

tfs-052.q: Besides the prayer for increase in knowledge, what instruction does the verse shown give the Prophet?
o: Not to hasten with the Quran before its revelation is complete
Not to teach the Quran to anyone until Ramaḍān had come
To have each verse written down before memorising it
To recite the Quran aloud only in the prayer at night
tfs-052.e: The Prophet used to hurry to repeat the revelation while it was being delivered; he was told not to hasten and to ask instead for more knowledge. Scholars note this is the only thing he was commanded to ask an increase of.

tfs-053.q: In the version of Ādam's story in Ṭā Hā, how did Shayṭān present the forbidden tree in the verse shown?
o: As the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays
As the tree of knowledge of good and evil
As a tree whose fruit gives the sight of angels
As a tree that would make him a prophet
tfs-053.e: Shayṭān whispered to Ādam, offering to guide him to 'the tree of eternity' and a never-ending dominion. The 'knowledge of good and evil' wording comes from the Biblical account, not the Quran.

tfs-054.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 24:35; al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 24:35
tfs-054.q: How did Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, as reported by al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr, interpret 'the parable of His light' in the verse shown?
o: The light of faith and the Quran in the believer's heart
The light of the sun and the moon in the sky above
The light that will shine for believers on the Ṣirāṭ
The light that shone from the Kaʿba over all of Makka
tfs-054.e: Ubayy explained the parable as the light Allah places in the heart of the believer: the chest is the niche, the heart the glass, faith and the Quran the lamp. Ibn ʿAbbās interpreted the opening of the verse as Allah being the guide of those in the heavens and the earth.

tfs-055.q: The olive tree in the verse shown is described as 'neither of the east nor of the west'. What is the explanation reported from Ibn ʿAbbās?
o: It stands in the open, sunlit all day, so its oil is purest
It grows only in Shām, which lies between east and west
It is a tree of Paradise that is not found on earth
It belongs to no nation, so no one may claim to own it
tfs-055.e: Ibn Kathīr reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and others that the tree is not shaded at sunrise or sunset but exposed to the sun from morning to evening, which makes its oil the clearest and finest.

tfs-056.q: After the grave sins listed before it, what does the verse shown promise those who repent, believe and do good?
o: Allah replaces their evil deeds with good deeds
They are forgiven but lose their rank in Paradise
They must first repay every wrong in this world
