o: Naskh lifts a ruling that applied; takhṣīṣ shows some cases were never meant
Naskh applies only to Meccan verses; takhṣīṣ applies only to Medinan verses
Naskh may rest on a weak report; takhṣīṣ requires a mutawātir report
Naskh affects only the wording; takhṣīṣ affects only the ruling itself
ulc-051.e: In naskh the ruling applied fully and is then lifted from a later time; in takhṣīṣ the general wording is shown never to have been intended for certain individuals. A specifier can also be connected to the text, whereas an abrogating proof must come later.

ulc-052.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 3:7
ulc-052.q: The verse shown divides the verses of the Book into which two kinds?
ulc-052.e: The verse states that some verses are muḥkam, the foundation of the Book, and others mutashābih, and warns against those who follow the mutashābih seeking discord. The other pairs are separate topics of ʿulūm al-Qurʾān.

ulc-053.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on muḥkam and mutashābih; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 39:23
ulc-053.q: In the verse shown, the whole Book is described with the highlighted word (mutashābih). In what sense is the whole Quran mutashābih here?
o: Its parts resemble one another in excellence and truth
Its meanings are unknown to everyone but God
Its rulings have all been abrogated
Its wording resembles that of earlier scriptures
ulc-053.e: Scholars distinguish three usages: the whole Quran is muḥkam in the sense of perfected (11:1), the whole is mutashābih in the sense of its parts resembling each other in beauty and truth (this verse), and some verses are muḥkam and others mutashābih in the specific sense of 3:7.

ulc-054.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 3:7; al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān, ch. on muḥkam and mutashābih; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān
ulc-054.q: Which statement correctly describes the disagreement about the highlighted word ('and those firmly grounded in knowledge') in the verse shown?
o: Many pause before it, so only God knows; others join it, so the learned know too
All scholars agree that one must join it to the name of God without pausing
All scholars agree that the firmly grounded know the reality of every unseen matter
The disagreement concerns only the vowel of its ending, not its meaning at all
ulc-054.e: Many of the Salaf and the majority pause after the name of God, making 'those firmly grounded' the start of a new sentence; others, such as Mujāhid, join them, so they also know the interpretation. Many later scholars reconcile the views: taʾwīl meaning ultimate reality is known to God alone, while taʾwīl meaning explanation is known to the learned.

ulc-055.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on muḥkam and mutashābih; al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān
ulc-055.q: In the specific sense of 3:7, which description best fits a muḥkam verse?
o: Its meaning is clear and needs no other text to explain it
Its ruling has been lifted by a verse revealed later
It was revealed in Mecca before the Hijra took place
Its meaning can be known only by a few of the scholars
ulc-055.e: Among the definitions al-Suyūṭī gives, the most common is that the muḥkam is clear in meaning and stands on its own, while the mutashābih admits several meanings or needs to be referred to the muḥkam for its explanation.

ulc-056.src: al-Kirmānī, al-Burhān fī Mutashābih al-Qurʾān; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān
ulc-056.q: Which scholar wrote al-Burhān fī Mutashābih al-Qurʾān (also known as Asrār al-Takrār), on verses that repeat with slight differences in wording?
ulc-056.e: Al-Kirmānī's work explains why similar verses differ slightly (mutashābih lafẓī). Al-Zarkashī's al-Burhān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān has a similar title but is a general work on the Quranic sciences.

ulc-057.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on general and specific; al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān
ulc-057.q: What is an ʿāmm (general) word in uṣūl and ʿulūm al-Qurʾān?
o: A word covering all individuals it fits, at once and without limit
A word that refers to one unspecified individual of its kind
A word that has two or more unrelated meanings in the language
A word whose meaning is hidden and needs another text to explain it
ulc-057.e: The ʿāmm includes all its individuals together, such as 'the believers'. A word for one unspecified individual is muṭlaq, a word with several meanings is mushtarak, and a word needing explanation is mujmal.

ulc-058.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on general and specific
ulc-058.q: The highlighted word specifies the general term 'mankind' in the verse before it. What kind of specifier is it?
o: A separate specifier from another verse
ulc-058.e: An exception joined to the same speech is a connected specifier (mukhaṣṣiṣ muttaṣil), like condition, description and limit. Separate specifiers (munfaṣil) are independent texts such as another verse, a hadith or consensus.

ulc-059.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on general and specific; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 2:228 and 33:49
ulc-059.q: The verse shown sets three menstrual cycles as the waiting period of divorced women in general. For which group does 33:49 specify it?
o: Women divorced before the marriage was consummated
Women who are pregnant at the time of divorce
Women who no longer menstruate due to age
ulc-059.e: 33:49 states that women divorced before consummation have no waiting period, which specifies the general ruling. Pregnant women and women past menstruation are dealt with in 65:4, and widows in 2:234.

ulc-060.src: al-Sarakhsī, Uṣūl al-Sarakhsī, ch. on the general; al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā, ch. on the general; al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān
ulc-060.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between the Ḥanafīs and the majority on the indication of an unspecified general word?
o: Ḥanafīs: definitive, so no first specification by an āḥād report; majority: probable
Ḥanafīs: probable; majority: definitive, so it can never be specified at all
Both: definitive, so a general Quranic word is never specified by the Sunna
Both: probable, so a general Quranic word may be specified only by analogy
ulc-060.e: The Ḥanafīs held that a general word not yet specified indicates all its individuals definitively, so a solitary hadith cannot be the first to specify a general Quranic text. The majority held its indication to be probable and allowed specification by a sound solitary hadith.

ulc-061.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on general and specific; al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān, on 3:173
ulc-061.q: Al-Suyūṭī cites the highlighted word ('the people') in the verse shown as an example of which category?
o: A general word by which something specific is intended
A general word that remains fully general in meaning
An unrestricted word that was restricted later on
A shared word that has several unrelated meanings
ulc-061.e: Many mufassirūn report that the first 'people' here refers to one man (often named as Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd) or a small group, so the general form intends something specific (ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ). This differs from a general word later specified by another proof.

ulc-062.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on unrestricted and restricted
ulc-062.q: What distinguishes a muṭlaq (unrestricted) word from an ʿāmm (general) word?
o: Muṭlaq means any one of a kind; ʿāmm covers all its individuals at once
Muṭlaq covers all its individuals at once; ʿāmm means any one of a kind
Muṭlaq appears only in Meccan verses, ʿāmm appears only in Medinan ones
Muṭlaq rulings are always abrogated, while ʿāmm rulings never are
ulc-062.e: A muṭlaq word, such as 'a slave' in an expiation, is fulfilled by any one individual of the kind; an ʿāmm word, such as 'the believers', includes every individual. Restricting a muṭlaq is taqyīd, limiting an ʿāmm is takhṣīṣ.

ulc-063.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on unrestricted and restricted; Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī, Kitāb al-Ẓihār; al-Sarakhsī, Uṣūl
ulc-063.q: In the verse shown, the slave freed in expiation for accidental killing is restricted by the highlighted word ('believing'); in the ẓihār expiation (58:3) it is unrestricted. Which describes the positions?
o: Majority (incl. Shāfiʿīs) extend it to ẓihār; Ḥanafīs do not, as causes differ
Ḥanafīs extend it to ẓihār; the majority do not, as the causes differ
All schools agree that 58:3 itself requires a believing slave in ẓihār
All schools agree that 4:92 was abrogated by the unrestricted wording of 58:3
ulc-063.e: Here the ruling (freeing a slave) is the same but the causes (killing, ẓihār) differ. The majority, including the Shāfiʿīs, carry the unrestricted onto the restricted and require a believing slave in ẓihār too; the Ḥanafīs do not, holding that each text keeps its own wording.

ulc-064.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on unrestricted and restricted; al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān, on 6:145
ulc-064.q: Scholars use the highlighted word ('poured forth') in the verse shown to restrict which unrestricted term?
o: The game of the sea mentioned in 5:96
ulc-064.e: Blood is forbidden without qualification in 5:3 and 2:173 but described as 'poured forth' here. Because the ruling and the cause are the same, scholars carry the unrestricted onto the restricted, so blood remaining in the meat and veins after slaughter is not included.

ulc-065.src: al-Bāqillānī, Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the inimitability of the Quran
o: The inability of humans to produce the like of the Quran
The division of the Quran into thirty equal parts
The rules for reciting the Quran beautifully and correctly
The explanation of the Quran by the Sunna of the Prophet
ulc-065.e: Iʿjāz means rendering others incapable: the Quran challenged its audience to produce something like it, and their failure proves that it is from God. The other options describe divisions, tajwīd and tafsīr.

ulc-066.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 17:88
ulc-066.q: What does the verse shown declare about the challenge of the Quran?
o: Humans and jinn together could not produce the like of this Quran
Only the Arabs of Quraysh were challenged to produce ten surahs
Anyone could produce one verse like it but not a surah
The challenge would end with the death of the Prophet
ulc-066.e: The verse states that even if humankind and the jinn gathered and supported one another, they could not bring the like of this Quran. It challenges with the whole Quran and is addressed to all, not only to Quraysh.

ulc-067.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 11:13; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on inimitability
ulc-067.q: The highlighted word belongs to the phrase stating the size of the challenge in the verse shown. How many surahs are the opponents asked to produce?
ulc-067.e: In this verse those who claim the Quran is fabricated are challenged to bring ten fabricated surahs like it. Elsewhere (10:38, 2:23) the challenge is reduced to a single surah.

ulc-068.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 2:23–24; al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān, ch. on inimitability
ulc-068.q: After the challenge in the preceding verse to produce one surah, the highlighted word begins a phrase that adds which element?
o: A firm statement that they will never be able to do it
A permission to seek the help of poets and orators
A time limit of one year for meeting the challenge
A promise of great reward if they should succeed
ulc-068.e: The phrase declares in advance that they will never be able to meet the challenge. Scholars point out that this prediction proved true, which is itself counted among the proofs of the Quran's inimitability.

ulc-069.src: al-Bāqillānī, Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on inimitability; al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān
ulc-069.q: The doctrine of ṣarfa, that God turned the Arabs away from opposing the Quran although they were able to, is associated with whom, and how did the majority respond?
o: al-Naẓẓām; most rejected it, as the miracle would then be the prevention
al-Bāqillānī; most accepted it as the strongest aspect of iʿjāz
ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī; most accepted it with some conditions
al-Zamakhsharī; most considered it the view of the early Salaf
ulc-069.e: Ṣarfa is linked above all to the Muʿtazilī al-Naẓẓām. Al-Bāqillānī, al-Jurjānī and most scholars rejected it, arguing that the Quran itself is inimitable in its composition and that ṣarfa would make the miracle the prevention rather than the text.

ulc-070.q: Which scholar developed the theory of naẓm (the arrangement of meanings through syntax) as the basis of the Quran's inimitability in Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz?
ulc-070.e: Al-Jurjānī argued in Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz that eloquence lies in naẓm, the way words are arranged according to the meanings of grammar. Al-Bāqillānī (Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān), al-Khaṭṭābī (Bayān Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān) and al-Rummānī (al-Nukat fī Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān) wrote other classical treatises on iʿjāz.

ulc-071.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on inimitability; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 30:2–4
ulc-071.q: The verse shown and the two after it, foretelling that the defeated Romans would soon be victorious, are often cited for which aspect of iʿjāz?
o: Informing about the unseen that later came to pass
The legislative perfection of its rulings
The miraculous effect of its sound on listeners
The precise counting of its letters
ulc-071.e: The Romans' defeat and their later victory within a few years, as foretold, is a standard example of the Quran's reports about the unseen. Scholars list this among the aspects of iʿjāz alongside its eloquence and its rulings.

ulc-072.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, introduction
ulc-072.q: Who wrote al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān?
ulc-072.e: Al-Itqān is by Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī and is among the most comprehensive classical works on the Quranic sciences. Al-Zarkashī wrote the earlier al-Burhān, which al-Suyūṭī drew on.

ulc-073.src: al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, introduction
ulc-073.q: Who is the author of al-Burhān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān?
ulc-073.e: Al-Burhān is by the Shāfiʿī scholar Badr al-Dīn al-Zarkashī (8th century AH). Al-Suyūṭī later built on it in al-Itqān.

ulc-074.src: al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān
ulc-074.q: Manāhil al-ʿIrfān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, a widely taught modern work, was written by whom?
ulc-074.e: Al-Zurqānī, a scholar of al-Azhar, wrote Manāhil al-ʿIrfān from his lectures. Mannāʿ al-Qaṭṭān and Ṣubḥī al-Ṣāliḥ each wrote a work called Mabāḥith fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān; Ibn ʿĀshūr wrote the tafsīr al-Taḥrīr wa-l-Tanwīr.

ulc-075.src: al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān, introduction; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, introduction
ulc-075.q: How are al-Burhān of al-Zarkashī and al-Itqān of al-Suyūṭī divided?
o: Both into 114 chapters following the surahs
Both into 30 parts following the ajzāʾ
ulc-075.e: Al-Zarkashī arranged al-Burhān in forty-seven types of knowledge; al-Suyūṭī, building on it and on his own earlier al-Taḥbīr, arranged al-Itqān in eighty types.

ulc-076.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, introduction
ulc-076.q: Al-Suyūṭī wrote al-Itqān as an introduction to a larger tafsīr he planned. What was that tafsīr called?
ulc-076.e: In his introduction al-Suyūṭī says he made al-Itqān a preface to his great tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn wa-Maṭlaʿ al-Badrayn. Al-Durr al-Manthūr is his collection of transmitted reports, al-Jalālayn a concise tafsīr he completed after al-Maḥallī, and Lubāb al-Nuqūl a book on occasions of revelation.

ulc-077.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the classes of mufassirūn; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction
ulc-077.q: Which Companion is known by the title Turjumān al-Qurʾān (interpreter of the Quran)?
ulc-077.e: Ibn ʿAbbās was given this title by Ibn Masʿūd and is known for the Prophet's supplication for him to be given understanding in religion. His students formed the Meccan school of tafsīr.

ulc-078.src: Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr; al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on tafsīr
ulc-078.q: What is meant by al-tafsīr bi-l-maʾthūr?
o: Tafsīr by transmitted reports: Quran, Sunna and the Companions
Tafsīr based mainly on the rules of grammar and rhetoric
Tafsīr based on the personal reasoning of the mufassir alone
Tafsīr based on hidden symbolic meanings of the letters
ulc-078.e: Al-tafsīr bi-l-maʾthūr explains the Quran by the Quran, by the Sunna, and by what is reported from the Companions (and, for many, the Tābiʿūn). Tafsīr bi-l-raʾy relies on reasoned ijtihād, which is praiseworthy only when grounded in knowledge.

ulc-079.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān ʿan Taʾwīl Āy al-Qurʾān, introduction
ulc-079.q: Who wrote Jāmiʿ al-Bayān ʿan Taʾwīl Āy al-Qurʾān, the great early tafsīr built on transmitted reports?
ulc-079.e: Al-Ṭabarī (d. 310 AH) collected the reports of the Companions and Tābiʿūn with their chains and weighed between them, which made his tafsīr a primary reference for later mufassirūn.

ulc-080.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, introduction
ulc-080.q: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, one of the most widely read tafsīrs, was written by whom?
ulc-080.e: Ibn Kathīr, a student of Ibn Taymiyya, explains the Quran by the Quran, the Sunna and the reports of the Salaf, and often comments on the reliability of the reports he cites.

ulc-081.q: Which two scholars wrote Tafsīr al-Jalālayn?
o: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Maḥallī and Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī and Badr al-Dīn al-Zarkashī
Jalāl al-Dīn al-Maḥallī and Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Jalāl al-Dīn al-Rūmī and Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
ulc-081.e: The name means 'the two Jalāls'. Al-Maḥallī explained from al-Kahf to the end and al-Fātiḥa, then died; al-Suyūṭī completed the first half from al-Baqara to al-Isrāʾ in the same concise style.

ulc-082.src: Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction
ulc-082.q: According to Ibn Taymiyya in his Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr, what is the soundest first step in explaining a verse?
o: Explaining the Quran by the Quran
Explaining it by the Arabic poetry of the Jāhiliyya
Explaining it by the reports of the People of the Book
Explaining it by the mufassir's own reasoning
ulc-082.e: Ibn Taymiyya lists the best methods in order: the Quran by the Quran, then by the Sunna, then by the sayings of the Companions, then of the Tābiʿūn. Ibn Kathīr adopts this order in the introduction to his tafsīr.

ulc-083.src: al-Zurqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on tafsīr bi-l-raʾy; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the conditions of the mufassir
ulc-083.q: How do scholars classify tafsīr bi-l-raʾy (tafsīr by reasoning)?
o: Praiseworthy when grounded in the required knowledge, blameworthy when not
Always forbidden, whatever the qualifications of the mufassir may be
Always permitted, since every reader may interpret the text freely
Permitted only for verses about stories, never for verses on rulings
ulc-083.e: Reasoned tafsīr that meets the conditions (knowledge of Arabic, uṣūl, the transmitted tafsīr and the Sunna) and does not contradict them is accepted. Speaking about the Quran without knowledge or to support a preconceived opinion is condemned.

ulc-084.src: Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the classes of mufassirūn
ulc-084.q: Which of these Tābiʿūn belongs to the Meccan school of tafsīr, made up of the students of Ibn ʿAbbās?
ulc-084.e: Ibn Taymiyya names Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ṭāwūs and ʿAṭāʾ among the companions of Ibn ʿAbbās in Mecca. ʿAlqama and Masrūq belong to the Kufan school of Ibn Masʿūd, and Zayd ibn Aslam to the Medinan school.

ulc-085.src: Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, introduction
ulc-085.q: According to Ibn Taymiyya, how should reports from the People of the Book (isrāʾīliyyāt) be treated when nothing in our sources confirms or contradicts them?
o: Neither affirmed nor denied, though they may be narrated
Accepted as true like the reports of the Companions
Accepted only if they concern rulings
ulc-085.e: Ibn Taymiyya, followed by Ibn Kathīr, divides them into three: what our sources confirm is accepted, what they contradict is rejected, and what they neither confirm nor deny is neither believed nor rejected, though it may be narrated; it rarely brings any religious benefit.

ulc-086.src: al-Jaṣṣāṣ, Aḥkām al-Qurʾān; Ibn al-ʿArabī, Aḥkām al-Qurʾān; Kiyā al-Harrāsī, Aḥkām al-Qurʾān
ulc-086.q: Three classical works are each titled Aḥkām al-Qurʾān. Which pairing of author and school is correct?
o: al-Jaṣṣāṣ: Ḥanafī; Ibn al-ʿArabī: Mālikī; Kiyā al-Harrāsī: Shāfiʿī
al-Jaṣṣāṣ: Mālikī; Ibn al-ʿArabī: Shāfiʿī; Kiyā al-Harrāsī: Ḥanafī
al-Jaṣṣāṣ: Shāfiʿī; Ibn al-ʿArabī: Ḥanafī; Kiyā al-Harrāsī: Mālikī
al-Jaṣṣāṣ: Ḥanafī; Ibn al-ʿArabī: Shāfiʿī; Kiyā al-Harrāsī: Mālikī
ulc-086.e: Abū Bakr al-Jaṣṣāṣ wrote from the Ḥanafī perspective, Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī (the Mālikī jurist, not the Sufi Ibn ʿArabī) from the Mālikī, and Kiyā al-Harrāsī, a student of al-Juwaynī, from the Shāfiʿī.

ulc-087.src: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān; Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on tafsīr and taʾwīl
ulc-087.q: When al-Ṭabarī introduces a passage with 'the statement on the taʾwīl of His words', in what sense does he use taʾwīl?
o: Explanation of the verse's meaning, the same as tafsīr
Departing from the apparent meaning because of a proof
The ultimate reality that only God knows
Allegorical meanings known only to mystics
ulc-087.e: In the usage of the early mufassirūn, including al-Ṭabarī, taʾwīl means tafsīr, explaining the meaning. The later technical sense, turning a word from its apparent meaning to a less obvious one because of a proof, belongs mainly to the uṣūlīs and theologians.

ulr-001.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on how the revelation descended
ulr-001.q: Which angel brought the Quran down to the Prophet ﷺ?
ulr-001.e: Jibrīl is the angel of revelation who brought the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ. Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl and Mālik have other tasks.

ulr-002.q: Where was the Prophet ﷺ when the first revelation came to him?
ulr-002.e: According to the hadith of ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, the Prophet ﷺ used to seclude himself in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, and the angel came to him there. The cave of Thawr is linked to the hijra.

ulr-003.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the first revelation
ulr-003.q: According to the soundest view, which passage was revealed first? (Its first verse is shown.)
o: The opening verses of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq
The opening verses of Sūrat al-Muddaththir
The opening verses of Sūrat al-Baqara
ulr-003.e: The soundest view, based on the hadith of ʿĀʾisha in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, is that the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq came first. Al-Muddaththir and al-Fātiḥa are other, weaker views.

ulr-004.src: al-Zarqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on revelation
ulr-004.q: What is the linguistic meaning of waḥy?
ulr-004.e: In the language, waḥy means informing someone in a hidden and swift way (al-iʿlām al-khafī al-sarīʿ). The technical sense is Allah informing a prophet of what He wills.

ulr-005.q: The verse shown names the ways in which Allah speaks to a human being. Which list matches it?
o: Inspiration, from behind a veil, through a sent messenger
Inspiration, true dreams, through a sent messenger
Direct speech, true dreams, from behind a veil
True dreams, inspiration, an angel in human form
ulr-005.e: The verse names three ways: waḥy in the sense of inspiration, speech from behind a veil, and sending a messenger (an angel) who conveys by Allah's leave. True dreams fall under the first kind but are not named separately.

ulr-006.q: According to ʿĀʾisha in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, how did revelation first begin for the Prophet ﷺ?
o: With true dreams that came like the break of dawn
With a voice calling him in the marketplace
With a written page that he found in Ḥirāʾ
With visions of the angel in the Masjid al-Ḥarām
ulr-006.e: ʿĀʾisha reported that revelation began with true dreams in sleep; every dream he saw came true like the light of dawn. Then seclusion became dear to him and the angel came in Ḥirāʾ.

ulr-007.q: When al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām asked how the revelation came, which mode did the Prophet ﷺ describe as the hardest on him?
o: When it came like the ringing of a bell
When the angel came in the form of a man
When it came in a dream during sleep
When it was cast into his heart
ulr-007.e: In the hadith of ʿĀʾisha in al-Bukhārī, the Prophet ﷺ said it sometimes came like the ringing of a bell (ṣalṣalat al-jaras), which was the hardest on him; at other times the angel came as a man and spoke to him.

ulr-008.q: What did ʿĀʾisha report seeing when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ on a very cold day?
o: His face turning pale and cold
ulr-008.e: ʿĀʾisha said she saw the revelation come to him on an intensely cold day, and when it left him his forehead was dripping with sweat. This shows the weight of receiving revelation.

ulr-009.q: The verse shown describes Allah speaking to Mūsā. Under which of the modes named in 42:51 does this fall?
ulr-009.e: Allah spoke to Mūsā directly, without an angel in between, yet Mūsā did not see Him. Scholars therefore place it under speech from behind a veil, as in the Prophet's ﷺ experience during the Miʿrāj.

ulr-010.q: In the verse shown, waḥy is used for the bee. What does it mean here?
o: Instinctive guidance placed in a creature
A command conveyed by a prophet
A true dream seen in sleep
ulr-010.e: The verse uses waḥy in its linguistic sense: Allah guided the bee by instinct to build its dwellings and gather food. It is not revelation in the technical sense given to prophets.

ulr-011.q: The highlighted word, together with the word after it, is a title. To whom does it refer?
ulr-011.e: The 'trustworthy spirit' (al-rūḥ al-amīn) who brought the Quran down upon the Prophet's ﷺ heart is Jibrīl, by agreement of the exegetes.

ulr-012.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ṣalāt; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on how the revelation descended
ulr-012.q: Which surah is linked to the report of Anas in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim in which the Prophet ﷺ raised his head smiling after a brief doze (ighfāʾa) and recited a surah just revealed to him?
ulr-012.e: The report concerns al-Kawthar. Some took it as revelation during sleep, while al-Suyūṭī and others explained the 'doze' as the state that came over him when revelation descended, so the principle that the whole Quran came through Jibrīl while awake remains.

ulr-013.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān, chapter on Jibrīl reviewing the Quran
ulr-013.q: Jibrīl used to review the Quran with the Prophet ﷺ each Ramadan. What was different in the year of his death?
o: He reviewed it with him twice
He reviewed it with him three times
There was no review that year
The review took place in Shaʿbān
ulr-013.e: Al-Bukhārī reports that Jibrīl reviewed the Quran with him once every year, and twice in the year he passed away; the Prophet ﷺ understood this as a sign that his death was near.

ulr-014.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb Badʾ al-Waḥy
ulr-014.q: What is meant by fatrat al-waḥy?
o: A temporary pause in revelation after the first revelation
The period between the hijra and the battle of Badr
The night on which the whole Quran descended
The years in which only Medinan verses were revealed
ulr-014.e: Fatrat al-waḥy is the pause after the first verses of al-ʿAlaq during which no revelation came, until the angel appeared again and the opening of al-Muddaththir was revealed.

ulr-015.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the first revelation; al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Muddaththir
ulr-015.q: Jābir's report in al-Bukhārī and Muslim names the surah shown as the first revealed. How do most scholars reconcile this with the report of ʿĀʾisha?
o: Al-Muddaththir was the first revealed after the pause in revelation
Al-ʿAlaq came in a dream, al-Muddaththir while awake
Jābir's report is weak and is set aside
Both surahs were revealed in full on the same day
ulr-015.e: Jābir's own wording mentions the angel 'who had come to me in Ḥirāʾ', so al-Muddaththir came after al-ʿAlaq. Scholars therefore say al-ʿAlaq was absolutely first, and al-Muddaththir first after the fatra, or first in commanding him to warn.

ulr-016.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Īmān, report of ʿUmar on 5:3
ulr-016.q: According to ʿUmar's report in al-Bukhārī, where was the passage on the perfection of the religion in the verse shown revealed?
o: At ʿArafa during the Farewell Pilgrimage
In Mecca on the day of the conquest
In Medina during his final illness
ulr-016.e: ʿUmar said he knew the day and place: it was revealed on the day of ʿArafa, a Friday, while the Prophet ﷺ was standing at ʿArafa in the Farewell Pilgrimage.

ulr-017.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the last revelation (report of al-Nasāʾī)
ulr-017.q: According to a report from Ibn ʿAbbās transmitted by al-Nasāʾī, what distinction does the verse shown have?
o: It was the last verse of the Quran revealed
It was the first verse revealed in Medina
It was revealed at ʿArafa in the Farewell Pilgrimage
It was revealed twice, in Mecca and in Medina
ulr-017.e: Al-Nasāʾī transmits from ʿIkrima that Ibn ʿAbbās said the last thing revealed of the Quran was this verse about the day of return to Allah. Al-Suyūṭī lists it among the main views on the last revelation.

ulr-018.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
ulr-018.q: In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib names the verse shown as the last verse revealed. Which surah does he name as the last surah revealed?
ulr-018.e: Al-Barāʾ said the last surah revealed was Barāʾa and the last verse the kalāla verse at the end of al-Nisāʾ. Other Companions named other passages; scholars hold each reported what he last knew.

ulr-019.q: According to Ibn ʿAbbās in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, which was the last surah revealed complete at one time?
ulr-019.e: Ibn ʿAbbās asked ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh whether he knew the last surah revealed all together, and named al-Naṣr. The qualifier 'complete at one time' distinguishes this from reports about the last verse.

ulr-020.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the last revelation (citing al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī, al-Intiṣār)
ulr-020.q: How does al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī, cited by al-Suyūṭī, explain the differing reports on the last revelation?
o: None is attributed to the Prophet ﷺ; each Companion spoke from his own judgment or what he last heard
One report is authentic and the others are fabricated
The Prophet ﷺ himself named several verses as the last
The reports refer to different modes of recitation
ulr-020.e: Al-Bāqillānī noted that none of these statements is raised to the Prophet ﷺ; each Companion said it by ijtihād and strong likelihood, possibly reporting the last thing he heard from him. This removes the apparent contradiction.

ulr-021.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on how the revelation descended
ulr-021.q: Over roughly how many years was the Quran revealed, as commonly stated?
ulr-021.e: The Quran came down in portions from the start of the mission until shortly before the Prophet's ﷺ death, commonly stated as about 23 years: about 13 in Mecca and 10 in Medina.

ulr-022.src: al-Zarqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on the descent of the Quran
o: Revealing the Quran in portions over time
Counting the verses of each surah
Writing the Quran with vowel marks
ulr-022.e: Tanjīm means that the Quran was sent down in separate portions according to events and needs, not all at once. The word comes from najm, an instalment.

ulr-023.q: The disbelievers asked why the Quran was not sent down all at once. Which wisdom does the verse shown give in reply?
o: To make firm the Prophet's ﷺ heart
To allow the scribes time to buy materials
To match the length of earlier scriptures
ulr-023.e: The verse answers that it was revealed in parts to strengthen the Prophet's ﷺ heart and was recited in measured order. Repeated revelation renewed his support at every stage of the call.

ulr-024.q: What does the highlighted word, together with the word before it, express about the revelation?
o: That it was recited to people at a measured pace
That it was hidden from people for a time
That it was revealed only at night
That it was written before it was recited
ulr-024.e: The phrase means 'with deliberation': the Quran was divided into parts so that the Prophet ﷺ would recite it to people slowly and at intervals, making it easier to understand and memorise.

ulr-025.q: In the well-known stages by which wine was forbidden, what role does the verse shown play?
o: It is the final, decisive prohibition
It first mentions both harm and benefit
It forbids approaching prayer while intoxicated
It mentions intoxicants among Allah's provisions
ulr-025.e: Scholars cite wine as the classic example of gradual legislation: 2:219 mentions harm outweighing benefit, 4:43 forbids prayer while intoxicated, and 5:90–91 make the prohibition final.

ulr-026.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān, chapter on the arrangement of the Quran (taʾlīf al-Qurʾān)
ulr-026.q: ʿĀʾisha said, in al-Bukhārī, that the first revealed were surahs of the mufaṣṣal mentioning Paradise and the Fire, and only later rulings on lawful and unlawful. Which wisdom of tanjīm does this show?
o: Faith was established in hearts before laws were imposed
Short surahs were easier for the scribes to write
Rulings were kept secret until Medina
The Quran followed the order of the earlier scriptures
ulr-026.e: She added that had the prohibition of wine come first, people would have refused to give it up. Gradual revelation first built belief in Allah and the Hereafter, so that later commands were accepted.

ulr-027.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ (report of Zayd ibn Thābit)
ulr-027.q: The highlighted word begins a phrase that, per Zayd ibn Thābit in al-Bukhārī, was revealed separately after the rest of the passage. What occasioned it?
o: The complaint of Ibn Umm Maktūm about his blindness
Kaʿb ibn Mālik staying behind from Tabūk
The excuses of the hypocrites before Uḥud
The lameness of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ
ulr-027.e: When the verse on the inequality of those who stay behind was dictated, Ibn Umm Maktūm, who was blind, raised his excuse, and the exemption for those with disability came down. It shows that a revelation could be as short as part of a verse.

ulr-028.src: al-Zarqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on the wisdom of gradual revelation
ulr-028.q: Passages in which the Quran answers questions people put to the Prophet ﷺ (the yasʾalūnaka passages) illustrate which wisdom of gradual revelation?
o: Answering questions and events as they arose
Hiding rulings until the community was larger
Matching the order of revelation to the order of the muṣḥaf
Testing the scribes' speed in writing
ulr-028.e: Many verses came in response to a question or an event at the time it happened. Revealing the Quran in parts allowed guidance to meet real situations directly, which made it clearer and more memorable.

ulr-029.q: According to the verse shown, in which month was the Quran sent down?
ulr-029.e: The verse states that Ramaḍān is the month in which the Quran was sent down as guidance for people. The night of its descent is Laylat al-Qadr, which falls in Ramaḍān.

ulr-030.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Qadr
ulr-030.q: According to the verse shown, Laylat al-Qadr is better than what?
ulr-030.e: The verse states that the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months: worship on it is better than worship in a thousand months that do not contain it.

ulr-031.q: Which night do the majority of exegetes take the 'blessed night' in the verse shown to be?
ulr-031.e: The majority identify it with Laylat al-Qadr, since 97:1 and 2:185 place the descent in Ramaḍān. A view attributed to ʿIkrima linked it to the night of mid-Shaʿbān; Ibn Kathīr calls that view far-fetched.

ulr-032.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on how the revelation descended (reports of Ibn ʿAbbās)
ulr-032.q: The Quran was revealed on Laylat al-Qadr, yet also over about 23 years. How does the report of Ibn ʿAbbās reconcile these?
o: It descended all at once to the lowest heaven, then gradually to the Prophet ﷺ
Only al-Fātiḥa descended on Laylat al-Qadr
It descended on a different Laylat al-Qadr each year
The Meccan part came at once and the Medinan part gradually
ulr-032.e: Ibn ʿAbbās said the Quran was sent down in one piece on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven, and from there it came down in portions over the years of the mission. Al-Suyūṭī calls this the soundest and best-known view.

ulr-033.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on how the revelation descended (reports of al-Ḥākim and al-Nasāʾī)
ulr-033.q: In the reports of Ibn ʿAbbās, what is the name of the place in the lowest heaven to which the Quran first descended as a whole?
ulr-033.e: Ibn ʿAbbās named Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven. Al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr is the house visited by angels, Sidrat al-Muntahā is in the highest heavens, and the Preserved Tablet is where the Quran is recorded before any descent.

ulr-034.src: al-Zarqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on the descents of the Quran
ulr-034.q: Some scholars describe the Quran's descent in stages. For which stage is the verse shown usually cited?
o: Its being recorded in the Preserved Tablet
Its descent onto the Prophet's ﷺ heart
Its being written by the scribes
ulr-034.e: Al-Zarqānī and others speak of the Quran's existence in the Preserved Tablet (citing 85:21–22), its descent to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, and then its gradual descent upon the Prophet ﷺ through Jibrīl.

ulr-035.src: al-Wāḥidī, Asbāb al-Nuzūl, on Sūrat ʿAbasa; al-Tirmidhī, al-Jāmiʿ, Abwāb Tafsīr al-Qurʾān
ulr-035.q: The surah that begins with the verse shown was revealed about a blind man who came to the Prophet ﷺ asking to be taught. Who was he?
ulr-035.e: Ibn Umm Maktūm, who was blind, came while the Prophet ﷺ was speaking with leaders of Quraysh, hoping they would accept Islam. The surah taught that the sincere seeker deserves attention first.

ulr-036.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Masad
ulr-036.q: The surah of the verse shown was revealed after the Prophet ﷺ called Quraysh together from al-Ṣafā. Who had answered him with a curse?
ulr-036.e: Ibn ʿAbbās reports in al-Bukhārī that when the Prophet ﷺ warned Quraysh from al-Ṣafā, his uncle Abū Lahab cursed him, and this surah was revealed about him.

ulr-037.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Maghāzī, ḥadīth al-ifk
ulr-037.q: The verse shown begins the passage revealed about the slander (al-ifk). Whose innocence did it declare?
ulr-037.e: The verses of al-Nūr from this verse onward were revealed to clear ʿĀʾisha of the false accusation spread by the hypocrites after the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq.

ulr-038.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on asbāb al-nuzūl
ulr-038.q: What is sabab al-nuzūl (occasion of revelation)?
o: An event or question about which revelation came at the time it occurred
The reason a surah is placed where it is in the muṣḥaf
The place in which a verse was revealed
The reason one reading differs from another
ulr-038.e: An occasion of revelation is an incident or a question in the Prophet's ﷺ time in response to which a verse or passage came down, close to when it occurred.

ulr-039.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on asbāb al-nuzūl; al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān, first category
ulr-039.q: What does the principle 'al-ʿibra bi-ʿumūm al-lafẓ lā bi-khuṣūṣ al-sabab' mean?
o: The ruling follows the general wording of the verse, not only the specific person or event
A verse applies only to the person it was revealed about
The occasion of revelation overrides the wording of the verse
General verses are always restricted by their occasion
ulr-039.e: The majority hold that when a verse is general in wording, its ruling covers everyone it includes, even though it was revealed on a particular occasion. The occasion is the clearest case of the verse, not its limit.

ulr-040.q: The verse shown was revealed about a woman who pleaded with the Prophet ﷺ about her husband's ẓihār. Who was she, as she is commonly named?
ulr-040.e: She is commonly named Khawla bint Thaʿlaba, wife of Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, who had declared ẓihār against her. ʿĀʾisha said she was in the room and did not hear all that was said, yet Allah heard it.

ulr-041.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā
ulr-041.q: What occasioned the surah of the verse shown, according to the report of Jundub in al-Bukhārī?
o: A pause in revelation and a taunt that his Lord had left him
The death of his son Ibrāhīm
The boycott of Banū Hāshim in the valley
The rejection he met in al-Ṭāʾif
ulr-041.e: Jundub reports that the Prophet ﷺ was unwell and did not rise for a night or two, revelation paused, and a woman taunted him that he had been abandoned. Al-Ḍuḥā was revealed to deny this.

ulr-042.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-042.q: Which of these surahs is Meccan?
ulr-042.e: Al-Muddaththir is among the earliest Meccan revelations. Al-Baqara, al-Nisāʾ and al-Anfāl are Medinan, dealing with laws, family and the battle of Badr.

ulr-043.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-043.q: Which of these surahs is Medinan?
ulr-043.e: Al-Nūr is Medinan: it contains the slander passage, the punishment for zinā and rules of modesty. Yā-Sīn, al-Mulk and Maryam are Meccan.

ulr-044.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-044.q: By the best-known definition, what makes a verse Medinan?
o: It was revealed after the hijra, wherever it came down
It was revealed inside the city of Medina
ulr-044.e: Al-Suyūṭī calls the time-based definition the best known: Meccan is what came before the hijra and Medinan what came after it, even if revealed in Mecca or on a journey.

ulr-045.src: Mannāʿ al-Qaṭṭān, Mabāḥith fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-045.q: Which set of features is typical of Meccan revelation?
o: Tawḥīd, resurrection and stories of earlier prophets, often in short verses
Detailed laws of inheritance, divorce and trade
Rulings on fighting, treaties and spoils of war
Exposure of the hypocrites and their schemes
ulr-045.e: Meccan revelation focuses on belief: the oneness of Allah, the resurrection and the stories of earlier nations, usually in short, forceful verses. Laws, treaties and the hypocrites are Medinan themes.

ulr-046.q: The highlighted word is one of the names of the Quran. What does it mean?
o: The criterion between truth and falsehood
ulr-046.e: Al-Furqān means that which distinguishes (faraqa) between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance; the surah carrying this name opens with it.

ulr-047.q: In the verse shown, the Quran is described by the highlighted word. Which description is it?
ulr-047.e: The verse describes the Quran as a clear light sent down to people, because it illuminates the way of guidance. Cure, spirit and criterion are other descriptions found elsewhere.

ulr-048.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the number of surahs and verses
ulr-048.q: How many surahs does the Quran contain?
ulr-048.e: The muṣḥaf contains 114 surahs, from al-Fātiḥa to al-Nās, by the agreement of the Muslims on the ʿUthmānic muṣḥaf.

ulr-049.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the number of surahs and verses
ulr-049.q: Which is the longest surah of the Quran?
ulr-049.e: Al-Baqara is the longest surah, with 286 verses in the Kufan count. Āl ʿImrān has 200 and al-Aʿrāf 206.

ulr-050.src: al-Dānī, al-Bayān fī ʿAdd Āy al-Qurʾān
ulr-050.q: Which of these surahs has only three verses?
ulr-050.e: Al-Kawthar has three verses, as do al-ʿAṣr and al-Naṣr. Al-Ikhlāṣ has four, al-Falaq five and al-Nās six.

ulr-051.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the order of surahs
ulr-051.q: Which surah does not begin with the basmala?
ulr-051.e: Al-Tawba (Barāʾa) is the only surah without the basmala at its start. Al-Naml is special in the opposite way: it has the basmala at its start and again within the surah.

ulr-052.q: Why is the highlighted word in the verse shown notable for counts of the Quran?
o: It begins a basmala inside a surah, so al-Naml contains it twice
It is the middle word of the whole Quran
It begins the longest verse of the Quran
It is the only word written without an alif
ulr-052.e: In the letter of Sulaymān to the Queen of Sabaʾ, the basmala occurs within the text. So al-Naml has the basmala twice, balancing al-Tawba, which has none, and the basmala occurs 114 times in the muṣḥaf.

ulr-053.src: al-Dānī, al-Bayān fī ʿAdd Āy al-Qurʾān, on the Kufan count
ulr-053.q: How many verses does the Quran have in the Kufan count, which is used in muṣḥafs printed in the riwāya of Ḥafṣ?
ulr-053.e: The Kufan count, transmitted from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī from ʿAlī, gives 6236 verses. The popular figure 6666 has no basis in the counting schools.

ulr-054.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān, chapter on the scribe of the Prophet ﷺ
ulr-054.q: Which Companion is best known as the scribe of the revelation in Medina?
ulr-054.e: Zayd ibn Thābit wrote down the revelation for the Prophet ﷺ in Medina; al-Bukhārī reports the Prophet ﷺ calling for him when a verse came down. Anas served the Prophet ﷺ but was not his scribe.

ulr-055.q: According to al-Wāḥidī, how alone may the occasion of a verse's revelation be known?
o: By transmission from those who witnessed the revelation
By reasoning from the meaning of the verse
By the position of the verse in the muṣḥaf
By comparing the verse with similar verses
ulr-055.e: Al-Wāḥidī states in the introduction of his Asbāb al-Nuzūl that speaking about occasions of revelation is only permissible through narration and hearing from those who witnessed it. Personal reasoning cannot establish a historical event.

ulr-056.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on asbāb al-nuzūl; Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on 58:1–4
ulr-056.q: The ẓihār verses came down about Khawla bint Thaʿlaba and her husband. On what basis do jurists apply their ruling to every man who pronounces ẓihār?
o: The general wording of the verses, which is not restricted to the occasion
Analogy with the case of Khawla, since the verses concern her alone
A later verse that extended the ruling to all
The consensus that every occasion is a mere example
ulr-056.e: The following verses speak generally of 'those who pronounce ẓihār', so the ruling covers all by its wording; this is the standard illustration of the principle that the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, not the specific cause.

ulr-057.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Ḥajj, chapter on the obligation of saʿy
ulr-057.q: ʿUrwa understood the phrase 'there is no blame' in the verse shown to mean that saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa is optional. How did ʿĀʾisha correct him?
o: By explaining the occasion: some Anṣār had felt it sinful to go between them
By citing a later verse that made saʿy obligatory
By noting that the phrase is a later addition to the verse
By pointing to a different reading of the verse
ulr-057.e: ʿĀʾisha explained that some of the Anṣār had felt uneasy about going between the two hills because of pre-Islamic practice, so the verse removed that sense of sin. This is a classic example of how knowing the occasion prevents misunderstanding.

ulr-058.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Tawba
ulr-058.q: The verse shown, forbidding the funeral prayer over hypocrites, was revealed after the Prophet ﷺ prayed over whom?
ulr-058.e: Ibn ʿUmar reports in al-Bukhārī that when ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy died, the Prophet ﷺ prayed over him despite ʿUmar's objection, and then this verse was revealed.

ulr-059.src: al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt
ulr-059.q: According to Ibn al-Zubayr in al-Bukhārī, the verse shown on lowering voices before the Prophet ﷺ followed a dispute between whom?
o: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, over whom to appoint over the Banū Tamīm delegation
Two men of the Anṣār, over the spoils of Ḥunayn
The Aws and the Khazraj, over the hypocrites
ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās, over the keys of the Kaʿba
ulr-059.e: When a delegation of Banū Tamīm came, Abū Bakr proposed one man as their leader and ʿUmar another, and their voices rose in the Prophet's ﷺ presence. Ibn al-Zubayr said ʿUmar afterwards spoke so softly the Prophet ﷺ had to ask him to repeat.

ulr-060.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-060.q: The verse shown was revealed at ʿArafa in the Farewell Pilgrimage. How is it classified under the best-known (time-based) definition?
o: Medinan, because it came after the hijra
Meccan, because it came down in the Meccan area
Neither, since it was revealed on a journey
Meccan, because it addresses the pilgrims
ulr-060.e: Under the time-based definition, everything revealed after the hijra is Medinan, even if it came down in Mecca, at ʿArafa or on a journey. A place-based definition would need a third category for such verses.

ulr-061.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan
ulr-061.q: Some defined Meccan as what addresses 'O mankind' and Medinan as what addresses 'O you who believe'. Why does the verse shown weaken this definition?
o: It addresses mankind yet lies in a Medinan surah
It addresses the believers yet lies in a Meccan surah
It was revealed in Mecca after the hijra
It contains no form of address at all
ulr-061.e: Al-Baqara is Medinan by agreement, yet the verse shown opens with an address to mankind; the same is true of al-Nisāʾ. So the addressee criterion is neither comprehensive nor exclusive, though it describes a general tendency.

ulr-062.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan (signs of the Meccan)
ulr-062.q: Al-Suyūṭī cites a rule of thumb about the word kallā. What is it?
o: Every surah in which kallā occurs is Meccan
Every surah in which kallā occurs is Medinan
Kallā occurs only in surahs with a prostration
Kallā occurs only in the first half of the Quran
ulr-062.e: Kallā (a word of rebuke and denial) occurs only in Meccan surahs, all in the second half of the muṣḥaf. Its sternness suits the address to the obstinate Meccan opponents.

ulr-063.q: The highlighted word describes the revelation given to the Prophet ﷺ. Why is the Quran called by this word?
o: Because it gives life to hearts as the soul gives life to bodies
Because it was brought by the angel called the Spirit
Because it was revealed at night
Because it cannot be seen, only heard
ulr-063.e: The Quran is called rūḥ because hearts live by it just as bodies live by the soul; without guidance the heart is as if dead. Jibrīl is called al-rūḥ al-amīn elsewhere, but here the word describes the revelation itself.

ulr-064.src: al-Zarqānī, Manāhil al-ʿIrfān, ch. on the definition of the Quran
ulr-064.q: In the technical definition of the Quran, which element excludes the ḥadīth qudsī?
o: That its recitation is an act of worship (al-mutaʿabbad bi-tilāwatih)
That it is the speech of Allah
That it was revealed to Muḥammad ﷺ
That it is written in the muṣḥafs
ulr-064.e: The ḥadīth qudsī is also attributed to Allah and came to the Prophet ﷺ, so those elements do not exclude it. What sets the Quran apart is that reciting it is itself worship, valid in the prayer, and that it was revealed with its wording as a challenge.

ulr-065.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the openings of the surahs
ulr-065.q: How many surahs open with the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa)?
ulr-065.e: Twenty-nine surahs open with disconnected letters. The number 14 refers to the distinct letters used in these openings, which is a common source of confusion.

ulr-066.src: Muslim, al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥāba; Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān
ulr-066.q: Which of these Companions is counted among the scribes of the Prophet ﷺ?
ulr-066.e: Muslim reports that Abū Sufyān asked the Prophet ﷺ to make Muʿāwiya his scribe and he agreed; Muʿāwiya is listed among the scribes by Ibn Ḥajar and others. The other three are great narrators but were not his scribes.

ulr-067.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on asbāb al-nuzūl (multiple occasions for one verse)
ulr-067.q: Two authentic, explicit reports name different occasions for one passage, and the events were close in time. How does al-Suyūṭī resolve this?
o: The passage was revealed after both events, so both are its occasion
The later report is preferred and the earlier dropped
Both reports are suspended for contradicting each other
The report of the older Companion is preferred
ulr-067.e: Al-Suyūṭī ranks the cases: a sound report beats a weak one, and a stronger or eye-witness report is preferred. If both are equal and the events close in time, the passage came after both, as with the liʿān verses and the cases of Hilāl ibn Umayya and ʿUwaymir. If far apart, the passage may have been revealed more than once.

ulr-068.src: al-Zarkashī, al-Burhān, first category (knowing the occasions of revelation); Ibn Taymiyya, Muqaddima fī Uṣūl al-Tafsīr
ulr-068.q: Why do al-Zarkashī and Ibn Taymiyya warn against treating every statement 'this verse was revealed concerning X' as an explicit occasion?
o: Such wording was often used to state what the verse covers, not what caused it
Such wording only ever appears in weak chains
Such wording refers to the place of revelation
Such wording is used only for abrogated verses
ulr-068.e: Al-Zarkashī notes it was the habit of Companions and Successors to say 'it was revealed concerning this' meaning that the verse includes this ruling. Explicit causal wording, such as naming an event followed by 'so Allah revealed', is what establishes an occasion.

ulr-069.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on asbāb al-nuzūl (general wording and specific cause)
ulr-069.q: A minority held that the lesson lies in the specific cause, not the general wording. How did they still extend such rulings to others?
o: Through analogy (qiyās) or another proof showing the ruling is not restricted
They did not; the ruling remained limited to the occasion forever
Through the consensus that all occasions are examples
Through the general wording, which they also accepted
ulr-069.e: Al-Suyūṭī notes that those who held the specificity view still applied the rulings to similar cases, but by qiyās or separate evidence rather than by the wording itself. So the practical difference between the two views is smaller than it appears.

ulr-070.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan (signs of the Medinan)
ulr-070.q: Al-Suyūṭī cites the rule that every surah mentioning the hypocrites is Medinan, with one exception. Which surah is it?
ulr-070.e: Hypocrisy appeared in Medina, so surahs mentioning the hypocrites are Medinan, except al-ʿAnkabūt, which is Meccan and yet speaks of them (in 29:11). Al-Aḥzāb mentions them too but is Medinan, so it is no exception.

ulr-071.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan (signs of the Meccan)
ulr-071.q: Every surah opening with disconnected letters is Meccan, with two agreed exceptions. Which are they?
ulr-071.e: Al-Suyūṭī gives the rule with the exception of al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, which are Medinan; he adds that there is disagreement about al-Raʿd. Yūnus, Hūd, Maryam, Ṭā-Hā, Luqmān and al-Sajda are Meccan.

ulr-072.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan; al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tafsīr, Sūrat al-Fātiḥa
ulr-072.q: The majority hold al-Fātiḥa to be Meccan, against a view attributed to Mujāhid. Which argument draws on the verse shown?
o: It is in a Meccan surah and mentions the 'seven oft-repeated', which the Prophet ﷺ identified as al-Fātiḥa
It mentions prayer, which was only prescribed in Mecca
It addresses the people of Mecca by name
It states that al-Fātiḥa was revealed in Ḥirāʾ
ulr-072.e: Al-Ḥijr is Meccan, and in it Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that He has already given him the seven oft-repeated; the hadith of Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā in al-Bukhārī identifies them with al-Fātiḥa. So al-Fātiḥa existed before the hijra. Some also said it was revealed twice.

ulr-073.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on Meccan and Medinan (Medinan verses in Meccan surahs)
ulr-073.q: Some scholars consider the verse shown Medinan although al-Muzzammil is Meccan. Which feature of the verse do they point to?
o: It mentions people fighting in the path of Allah
It addresses the People of the Book
It names the hypocrites of Medina
It refers to the change of qibla
ulr-073.e: The verse speaks of some who travel seeking Allah's bounty and others who fight in His path, and commands giving zakāt; fighting was prescribed after the hijra. Others keep it Meccan, reading the mention of fighting as a foretelling.

ulr-074.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, ch. on the names of the Quran
ulr-074.q: Which scholar held that 'al-Qurān' (read without hamza) is a proper name of Allah's Book, not derived from qaraʾa, like al-Tawrāh and al-Injīl?
ulr-074.e: Al-Suyūṭī reports that al-Shāfiʿī, who read with the Meccan reading of Ibn Kathīr, held it to be a non-derived name. Al-Liḥyānī and others made it a verbal noun of qaraʾa (to recite), while al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿUbayda linked it to qarʾ in the sense of gathering.

ulr-075.src: al-Dānī, al-Bayān fī ʿAdd Āy al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Fātiḥa
ulr-075.q: All counting schools give al-Fātiḥa seven verses. How do the schools that do not count the basmala as a verse (e.g. the Madinan and Basran) reach seven?
o: They place a verse-end within the verse shown, after the mention of those Allah has favoured
They count the āmīn after al-Fātiḥa as a verse
They divide the first verse of praise into two
They count the basmala of the next surah
ulr-075.e: The Kufan and Meccan counts make the basmala verse one and the verse shown a single verse. The Madinan, Basran and Shāmī counts drop the basmala and instead end a verse after the mention of those whom Allah has favoured, splitting the verse shown into two.

ulr-076.src: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, Kitāb Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān, chapter on the scribe of the Prophet ﷺ; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, al-Istīʿāb, entry Ubayy ibn Kaʿb
ulr-076.q: Which Companion is reported to have been the first to write for the Prophet ﷺ after his arrival in Medina?
ulr-076.e: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and Ibn Ḥajar report that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb was the first to write for him in Medina; when Ubayy was absent Zayd ibn Thābit wrote, and Zayd later became the most constant scribe. Muʿāwiya wrote only after the conquest of Mecca.

vc-001.src: al-Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī, al-Mufradāt fī Gharīb al-Qurʾān, entry rabb
vc-001.q: What is the basic meaning of the highlighted word, used for God?
o: Lord and Sustainer: the one who owns, cares for and nurtures
Judge who decides on the Day of Reckoning
Creator who brings things out of nothing only
King who rules over a single land
vc-001.e: Rabb means the one who owns and brings a thing gradually to its completion by caring for it, hence ‘Lord and Sustainer’. Judge, Creator and King translate other names: dayyān, khāliq, malik.

vc-002.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
o: A clear, wide path or road
vc-002.e: Ṣirāṭ means a clear, broad road, which suits the idea of the straight path to God. It does not refer to a pass, a well or a landmark.

vc-003.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Baqara
vc-003.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the verse shown?
vc-003.e: Rayb is doubt that carries suspicion or a sense of unease. The verse says there is no such thing about the Book.

vc-004.q: What does the highlighted word literally mean, and what is it used to express between spouses?
o: A garment: closeness, covering and protection
A rope: a bond that cannot be cut
vc-004.e: Libās is clothing. The verse uses the image to describe how spouses cover, shelter and are close to each other.

vc-005.q: What does the highlighted word literally mean?
vc-005.e: Ḥabl is a rope. The verse uses it as an image of the bond with God (His covenant or His Book) which believers should hold on to together.

vc-006.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Yūsuf
vc-006.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-006.e: Sayyāra is derived from sayr (travelling) and means a company of travellers, here the caravan that came to the well.

vc-007.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Yūsuf
vc-007.q: What object did the water-drawer let down into the well, according to the highlighted word?
vc-007.e: Dalw is the bucket used to draw water; the verb before it means he let it down into the well.

vc-008.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Naḥl
vc-008.q: Which creature is named by the highlighted word, to which God gave inspiration (waḥy in the sense of instinct)?
vc-008.e: The word is the name of the bee, which also gives its name to the chapter. God directed it to make its homes in mountains and trees.

vc-009.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
vc-009.q: Which creature does the highlighted word name?
vc-009.e: The word is the spider, whose house is used in the verse as the weakest of homes; the chapter takes its name from it.

vc-010.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Yā Sīn
vc-010.q: What does the highlighted word describe about the earth?
vc-010.e: Maytatu means dead: land without plants. God brings it to life with water, which is offered as a sign.

vc-011.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the verse shown?
vc-011.e: Khuluq (with ḍamma on the lām) is the inner disposition and character, as distinct from khalq (with fatḥa), the outward form. The verse praises the Prophet's character.

vc-012.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Muzzammil
vc-012.q: What does the highlighted title mean?
o: The one wrapped in his garment
vc-012.e: Al-Muzzammil is the one who has wrapped himself in a cloth, an address to the Prophet. It is often paired with al-Muddaththir, the one covered with a cloak.

vc-013.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Muddaththir
vc-013.q: What does the highlighted title mean?
o: The one covered with a cloak
The one who is shivering with fear only
The one who is praying at night
vc-013.e: Al-Muddaththir is the one who covers himself with a dithār (outer cloak). Commentators relate it to the Prophet after the first revelation.

vc-014.q: What does the highlighted verb mean?
vc-014.e: Uqsimu is from qasam, an oath. The Quran often swears by created things or by days to emphasise what follows.

vc-015.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Fajr
vc-015.q: What does the highlighted word describe about the soul?
vc-015.e: Al-muṭmaʾinna is the soul that has settled in its trust in God and is at rest. It is addressed at the end of the chapter.

vc-016.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā
vc-016.q: What time of day does the highlighted word refer to?
vc-016.e: Al-ḍuḥā is the time when the sun has risen and is bright, the forenoon. The chapter swears by it and by the night.

vc-017.q: What does the highlighted verb mean here?
vc-017.e: Sharḥ means to open up, expand. The verse speaks of God widening the Prophet's chest for guidance and patience.

vc-018.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Tīn
vc-018.q: What does the highlighted word name?
vc-018.e: Al-tīn is the fig. The chapter takes its name from this fruit, which God swears by together with the olive.

vc-019.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-ʿAlaq
vc-019.q: What does the highlighted word refer to in the creation of the human being?
vc-019.e: ʿAlaq is something that clings or hangs on, the clot-like stage after the drop of fluid. Dry clay and water belong to other descriptions.

vc-020.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Qāriʿa
vc-020.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-020.e: Al-qāriʿa comes from qarʿ, to strike or knock hard. It is a name of the Last Hour because its terror strikes hearts.

vc-021.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Falaq
vc-021.q: What does the highlighted word most commonly mean?
vc-021.e: Al-falaq is the splitting of darkness at dawn. It is the most commonly given meaning, from the verb falaqa, to split.

vc-022.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-022.e: Ḥāsid is the envier: the person who wishes that another loses a blessing. The verb is in the same verse.

vc-023.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Baqara
vc-023.q: What does the highlighted word name?
vc-023.e: Al-ghamām means clouds. In the verse God shades the Israelites with them in the wilderness.

vc-024.q: What does the highlighted word refer to?
vc-024.e: Al-maysir is gambling or games of chance, mentioned in the verse alongside wine.

vc-025.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa
vc-025.q: What is the highlighted word, a name of the Last Hour?
vc-025.e: Al-wāqiʿa means the occurrence that is sure to happen, a name of the Day of Judgment. The chapter is named after it.

vc-026.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry ʿadā
vc-026.q: The highlighted word is a plural. What is its singular?
vc-026.e: Aʿdāʾ is the plural of ʿaduww, enemy. The verse reminds the believers that they were enemies before God joined their hearts.

vc-027.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry akhā
vc-027.q: The highlighted word is a plural. What is its singular?
vc-027.e: Ikhwān is a plural of akh, brother; the other plural, ikhwa, is used mostly for blood brothers. Ikhwān commonly describes brotherhood of friendship or faith.

vc-028.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry shahida
vc-028.q: The highlighted word is a plural. What is its singular?
vc-028.e: Shuhadāʾ is the plural of shahīd, one who bears witness. In the verse the believers are told to be witnesses for God in justice.

vc-029.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry zawj
vc-029.q: The highlighted word is a plural. What is its singular?
vc-029.e: Azwāj is the plural of zawj, a spouse or one of a pair. In the verse it covers the pairs among humans and among cattle.

vc-030.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry walī
vc-030.q: The highlighted word is a plural. What is its singular?
vc-030.e: Awliyāʾ is the plural of walī, one who is close, an ally or protector. The verse likens those who take protectors besides God to the spider.

vc-031.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the broadest sense?
vc-031.e: Al-kawthar is an intensive form from kathra, abundance: great and plentiful good. Commentators mention a river in Paradise as one instance of it.

vc-032.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Baqara
vc-032.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-032.e: Ṣawāʿiq (singular ṣāʿiqa) are thunderbolts: lightning strikes that kill. In the verse the hypocrites put their fingers in their ears to avoid them.

vc-033.q: The highlighted word is used here for the hearts of the hypocrites. What does it mean?
o: Sickness of the heart (doubt and hypocrisy)
vc-033.e: Maraḍ literally means sickness, and here the commentators explain it as the spiritual sickness of doubt and hypocrisy. God increases it as a result of their denial.

vc-034.src: al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān, ch. on the names of the Quran
vc-034.q: What does the highlighted word refer to?
vc-034.e: Al-dhikr, the Reminder, is one of the names of the Quran. God promises in the verse that He Himself will preserve it.

vc-035.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Kahf
vc-035.q: What does the highlighted word mean, said of the Book?
vc-035.e: ʿIwaj is bending or deviation. The verse says God has put none of it in the Book, so it is straight.

vc-036.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the parable of light?
o: A niche in a wall that holds a lamp
vc-036.e: Mishkāt is a recess in a wall in which a lamp is placed, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and others. The parable then describes the lamp inside glass.

vc-037.q: What does the highlighted word name in the parable of light?
vc-037.e: Zujāja is glass, here the glass casing in which the lamp burns. It is likened to a shining star.

vc-038.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Qāf
vc-038.q: What does the highlighted word, in ‘the rope of the …’, refer to?
o: The jugular vein in the neck
vc-038.e: Al-warīd is the large vein of the neck, called the jugular. God says He is nearer to a human being than that; the phrase is an image of extreme closeness.

vc-039.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Najm
vc-039.q: What does the highlighted verb mean here?
vc-039.e: Hawā means to fall or descend, so ‘when it fell/set’. The verb is said of the star that the chapter swears by.

vc-040.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Insān
vc-040.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-040.e: Al-dahr is time or a long period. The verse asks whether a span of it passed over the human being when he was not even something mentioned.

vc-041.q: The highlighted word is a contraction. Of what?
vc-041.e: The preposition ʿan merges with the question word mā (its alif dropped after the preposition), giving ‘about what?’. The question is rhetorical, setting up a great announcement.

vc-042.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Infiṭār
vc-042.q: What does the highlighted verb mean?
vc-042.e: Infaṭara is to split or burst open. The chapter is named after this sign of the end of the world.

vc-043.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Infiṭār
vc-043.q: What does the highlighted verb mean, said of the seas?
o: They were burst open and let flow into each other
vc-043.e: Fujjirat means were burst forth: the barriers between the seas are broken and they overflow and mix. It is another sign of the end.

vc-044.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn
vc-044.q: Who are the people named by the highlighted word?
o: Those who give short measure and weight
Those who refuse to pay zakāt
vc-044.e: Taṭfīf means giving less than is due, being stingy in measure. The chapter opens with a threat against those who do it.

vc-045.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Ṭāriq
vc-045.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
o: The one that comes at night (the piercing star)
The one that guides on a road
The one that shakes the earth
The one that sweeps the dust
vc-045.e: Al-ṭāriq is what comes at night, from ṭarq (knocking). The following verses explain it as the piercing star.

vc-046.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Balad
vc-046.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-046.e: Kabad means hardship, toil and struggle. The verse says God created the human being in it, as Ibn ʿAbbās and others explained.

vc-047.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā
vc-047.q: What does the highlighted verb mean, said of the night?
o: It became still and covered everything in darkness
vc-047.e: Sajā describes the night when it becomes calm and its darkness settles over everything. The chapter swears by it.

vc-048.q: What does the highlighted verb mean?
vc-048.e: Qalā means to hate and to leave out of dislike. The verse reassures the Prophet that his Lord has neither left nor disliked him.

vc-049.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt
vc-049.q: What does the highlighted word describe?
o: The panting sound of galloping horses
vc-049.e: Ḍabḥ is the loud breathing of galloping horses. Later verses mention sparks and dust, which are different things.

vc-050.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Fīl
vc-050.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-050.e: Abābīl means flocks or groups following one another, said of the birds. Its singular is unused in the language according to the commonly stated view.

vc-051.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Fīl
vc-051.q: What does the highlighted word name?
o: Crop leaves or husks left after the grain
vc-051.e: ʿAṣf are the dried leaves or husks of crops, and the verse says the army became like those eaten or trampled.

vc-052.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Kawthar
vc-052.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-052.e: Al-abtar is the cut-off one whose line or memory is severed. The verse turns the insult back on the Prophet's enemy.

vc-053.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Masad
vc-053.q: What does the highlighted verb mean?
vc-053.e: Tabba means perished or was lost. The chapter begins with the curse on Abū Lahab.

vc-054.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ
vc-054.q: Which explanation of the highlighted word is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās?
o: The master to whom all turn in their needs
The one who was born of nothing
The one with no beginning in time only
vc-054.e: Ibn ʿAbbās explained al-ṣamad as the chief to whom creatures turn in their needs and requests. Other explanations, such as ‘without a hollow interior’, are also reported.

vc-055.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Falaq
vc-055.q: What does the highlighted verb, said of the darkness (ghāsiq), mean?
vc-055.e: Waqaba means to enter or settle in, so the darkness of night when it spreads. The verse seeks refuge from the evil that can come then.

vc-056.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Falaq
vc-056.q: What does the highlighted word describe?
vc-056.e: Al-naffāthāt are those who blow on knots, as practised in sorcery. The verse seeks protection from their evil.

vc-057.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat al-Nās
vc-057.q: What does the highlighted word describe about the whisperer?
o: One who slinks back when God is mentioned
vc-057.e: Al-khannās is the one who withdraws; the commentators say the whisperer slinks away when God is remembered and returns when the person is heedless.

vc-058.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Baqara
vc-058.q: The highlighted word is the second item sent to the Israelites in the wilderness. What is it?
vc-058.e: Al-salwā is the quail, a bird, sent with al-mann (a sweet substance), according to the commentators from Ibn ʿAbbās onwards.

vc-059.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Baqara
vc-059.q: What does the highlighted verb mean?
o: They were shaken violently (by fear and trials)
vc-059.e: Zulzilū comes from zalzala, to shake hard. The verse says earlier believers were so shaken by hardship that the Messenger himself asked when God's help would come.

vc-060.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Āl ʿImrān
vc-060.q: What does the highlighted word mean in ‘on the … of a pit of fire’?
vc-060.e: Shafā is the edge or brink of something. The believers were once at the very brink of the fire before God saved them.

vc-061.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-061.e: Al-qisṭ is justice, equity in giving each their due. The verse commands standing firmly for it even against oneself.

vc-062.q: What does the highlighted word refer to?
o: Animals brought to the sanctuary as an offering
vc-062.e: Al-hady is the sacrificial animal sent or driven to the sanctuary of Makka. The verse forbids violating it.

vc-063.q: What does the highlighted word mean when said of the Prophet?
o: Unlettered (not trained in reading and writing)
Of the city of Makka only
vc-063.e: Al-ummī is explained by the commentators as the unlettered, like a person as his mother bore him. Another derivation links it to umm al-qurā, the mother of cities, but the first is better known.

vc-064.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Aʿrāf
vc-064.q: What does the highlighted verb describe?
o: It pants with its tongue hanging out
vc-064.e: Yalhath means to pant with the tongue hanging out, as a dog does. The parable says the man is like this whether chased or left alone.

vc-065.q: Who are the people described by the highlighted word, among the recipients of zakāt?
vc-065.e: Al-ghārimūn are those burdened by debt. They are one of the eight categories in the verse; travellers are ‘the son of the road’ and collectors are ‘those working on it’.

vc-066.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat Yūsuf
vc-066.q: What does the highlighted word mean, in the place where they threw Yūsuf?
o: The depths or hidden part of the well
vc-066.e: Ghayāba is whatever hides a thing, here the dark bottom of the pit. The word following it means the well or pit.

vc-067.q: Whom does the highlighted word, with the faithful, designate in this verse?
vc-067.e: Al-rūḥ al-amīn, the Faithful Spirit, is Jibrīl according to the consensus of the commentators in this verse; he brought down the Quran to the Prophet's heart.

vc-068.q: What does the highlighted word mean in Zakariyyā's prayer?
vc-068.e: Al-mawālī are the relatives or heirs from the wider family. Zakariyyā feared what they would do after him since his wife was barren.

vc-069.q: What does the highlighted word mean, which the verse forbids to hold back punishment?
vc-069.e: Raʾfa is a deep tenderness and pity. The verse says it must not prevent the carrying out of God's penalty.

vc-070.src: Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿArab, entry nisāʾ
vc-070.q: The highlighted word means ‘women’. What is peculiar about it?
o: It has no singular from the same word; the singular is imraʾa
It is a plural with a singular nisā
vc-070.e: Nisāʾ is a plural whose singular comes from another word, imraʾa. Arabic has several such irregular pairs.

vc-071.q: What does the highlighted word mean?
vc-071.e: Aʿjamī refers to a non-Arab or to what is not clear Arabic. The verse says if the Quran were in a foreign tongue they would complain, ‘Why were its verses not made clear?’.

vc-072.q: What does the highlighted divine attribute mean?
o: Originator who creates without a model
vc-072.e: Fāṭir comes from faṭara, to split, and is used for the one who brings creation into being, as if splitting nothing open. It is a name of creation, not of forgiveness.

vc-073.q: Who are the people named by the highlighted word, helpers of ʿĪsā?
vc-073.e: Al-ḥawāriyyūn are the close disciples who supported ʿĪsā; the word is linked to ḥawar, whiteness or purity of heart, or to their trade of washing clothes.

vc-074.q: What does the highlighted verb mean, said of the Anṣār?
vc-074.e: Yuʾthirūna means to give preference to others over oneself, even when in need. The verse praises the Anṣār for this generosity.

vc-075.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
vc-075.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the parable of the plants?
vc-075.e: Ḥuṭām is dry, broken-up stubble: the end of the plants in the parable, which stands for the passing of worldly life.

vc-076.q: What does the highlighted word mean in the verse about the heavens and the earth?
vc-076.e: Ratq means joined or closed up as one mass, while fataq (the verb that follows) means to split open. The verse uses the pair to describe the separation of heaven and earth.

vc-077.src: al-Zamakhsharī, al-Kashshāf, on Sūrat ʿAbasa; al-Suyūṭī, al-Itqān, on the gharīb
vc-077.q: What does the highlighted word name?
o: A kind of grain for bread
vc-077.e: Abb is the grass and herbage on which animals graze, as distinct from the fruit eaten by people mentioned just before. A report tells of ʿUmar being unsure of its detail but understanding its sense.

vc-078.src: Ibn Qutayba, Gharīb al-Qurʾān, on Sūrat al-Qāriʿa
vc-078.q: What does the highlighted word name in the description of the mountains on that day?
vc-078.e: ʿIhn is dyed wool; the mountains are described as like carded wool, scattered and fluffy. The word after it describes this carded state.

vc-079.q: What does the highlighted word describe?
o: One who habitually slanders and backbites
One who lies down in the dust
vc-079.e: Humaza is the intensive form of hamz, to pierce or defame. Commentators describe it as one who habitually backbites; it is paired with lumaza, who mocks or taunts.

vc-080.q: What does the highlighted word describe about the stones?
vc-080.e: Sijjīl is explained as hard, baked clay; a view holds the word comes from Persian. The stones were thrown by the birds.

vc-081.src: Ibn Kathīr, Tafsīr, on Sūrat Quraysh
vc-081.q: What is the best meaning of the highlighted word?
o: Their habit and secure arrangement for journeys
vc-081.e: Īlāf means the familiar, protected habit; Quraysh were secure in their summer and winter caravans because of their guardianship of the sanctuary.

vc-082.q: What does the highlighted verb mean, said of the one who treats the orphan badly?
vc-082.e: Yadʿu means to push or drive off roughly. The verse describes the denier of the religion as one who repels the orphan with force and contempt.

vc-083.q: Which statement fits the commonly given distinction between the highlighted word and the one after it?
